title: An accepted scheduled ride whose pickup has passed stays the 'next' ride forever and filters out every trip offer
description: _nextScheduledRide is ScheduledRideStore.upcoming.first, and upcoming sorts accepted rides soonest first without dropping ones whose pickup has passed. When the next ride's pickup has passed and lateSince is null, _planScheduled returns at line 140 (`if (state.lateSince == null && !pickupAt.isAfter(now)) { return; }`), so no Leave-now, late warning or backup is ever planned and the ride never leaves Accepted. _fitsSchedule (305-320) then calls SmartGap.offerFits against that past pickup. offerFits returns `!now.add(needed).isAfter(at)`, which is always false for a past `at`, so every Radar deck trip, Live-list trip (_rideAllowed in home_offer_rules.dart:22) and Exclusive offer (home_offer_radar.dart:241/326) is rejected. _towardPickupTime also keeps saying 'Trips toward your HH:MM pickup'. There are several ways a past ride gets there. (1) Requests are never pruned when their time passes (see the next finding), so the driver can accept one from Scheduled rides. (2) The Home popup can raise a released request whose pickup has passed: _exclusiveStepReached returns false when untilPickup is null, so _waitsForHome is true. (3) An assignment that waited while the driver was offline can be accepted after its time (_maybeShowAssignment never checks the pickup time). (4) A won Exclusive claim whose pickup has just passed is saved 'for later' (home_reservation.dart:494-498).
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test on the fast test day. At 08:10 the 08:05 Lidingö request is still listed (openRequests=2). The driver accepts it, giving upcoming=[Today 08:05, Tomorrow 08:15], then goes online, and dispatch publishes a trip that ends near the driver. Control run without the stale accept: the Radar deck shows ['toward']. With the stale accept: no Radar deck at all (deck found=0). The driver gets no trips for the rest of the session, and the 08:05 ride sits in Accepted indefinitely.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:113-116 `final upcoming = ScheduledRideStore.upcoming; return upcoming.isEmpty ? null : upcoming.first;`
home_scheduled.dart:140 `if (state.lateSince == null && !pickupAt.isAfter(now)) { return; }`
home_scheduled.dart:312-320 `final fits = SmartGap.offerFits(...); if (!fits) { return false; }`
smart_gap.dart:131 `return !now.add(Duration(minutes: needed)).isAfter(at);`
scheduled_rides.dart:626-633 upcoming keeps every ride with `route.pickupAt(now) != null`, past ones included
suggested_fix: Leave rides whose pickup has passed out of `upcoming` and _nextScheduledRide, or move them out of Accepted (missed or backup) when they pass. Refuse to accept a request, popup or assignment whose pickup has passed.

title: Reservation requests whose pickup time has passed stay listed, counted on the Home dot and acceptable
description: _visibleRequests filters only on block, category and clash. It never checks request.route.untilPickup(now). A request that nobody took stays in the Requests tab after its pickup time, for example the id-less Lidingö demo request, which dispatch never expires. It is still counted in openRequests (the Home green dot and the LED badge), still shows its 'Today, 08:05–08:15' card, and can still be accepted locally: _claim returns true for an empty id. Accepting it then triggers the offer blackout described in the previous finding.
failure_scenario: Fast test day at 08:10. ScheduledRideStore.openRequests.value is still 2, including the 08:05 request whose pickup has passed. The driver taps it and Accepts, and 'Accepted · pickup 08:05' is shown for a ride in the past.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:541-547 `_requests.where((ride) => DriverCategoryChoice.takes(ride.category) && _clashWith(ride) == null)`
scheduled_rides.dart:268 `if (dispatch == null || ride.id.isEmpty) return true;`
Repro output: `now=2015-01-01 08:10:00.000 open=2`
suggested_fix: Leave out requests whose pickupAt(now) has passed (or is inside the Radar step) in _visibleRequests and isOpen, and refresh openRequests when that time is reached.

title: Scheduled trip opened by 'Leave now' passes a localized matchedVia, so in sv/fr the scheduled waiting terms are not applied
description: _startScheduledTrip opens the trip with matchedVia = tr.scheduledRide ('Bokad resa' in sv, 'Course planifiée' in fr). AcceptRide picks its waiting terms with WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: ...), which only checks `via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')`. In sv/fr a scheduled ride is therefore typed `normal`. The reservation policy's included waiting (ScheduledRideRules.includedWaitingMinutes) and any admin scheduled-ride waiting rule are dropped, and the 'Scheduled ride' rule label disappears from the terms. The Exclusive reservation path (home_offer_radar.dart:837, tr.exclusiveReservation) has the same root cause.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: typeOf('Scheduled ride') gives scheduled, free=5, noShow=5, rule 'XL · Scheduled ride'. typeOf('Bokad resa') and typeOf('Course planifiée') give normal, free=3, noShow=3, rule 'XL'. A Swedish driver on an XL scheduled ride starts charging waiting and can mark a no-show after 3 minutes instead of the 5 included minutes.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:234-237 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide);`
waiting_rules.dart:248-251 `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled; }`
accept_ride.dart:991 `type: WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)`
app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`
suggested_fix: Pass a language-neutral ride type (or the WaitingRideType itself) to AcceptRide instead of deriving it from the localized display label.

title: Accepted and requested rides store a relative 'Today'/'Tomorrow' that is re-read against the current date, so after midnight a ride moves a day later
description: Reservations carry pickupDay 'Today' or 'Tomorrow', fixed when they are built (DemoReservations books them once from the first clock reading; the seed accepted ride is 'Tomorrow'). Every consumer resolves them again with pickupAt(now) = today or tomorrow of the current `now`. Once the date changes, a 'Tomorrow 00:30' ride booked at 22:30 resolves to the day after. _planScheduled re-runs on every store change and every time Radar goes live (_onRadarLive). After midnight it recomputes pickupAt and cancels the correct Leave-now timer, replacing it with one 24 h later. The same shift reaches the late-cancel rule (isLateCancel calls a 20-minutes-to-pickup cancel free), the smart gap, the clash check and the cards, which still say 'Tomorrow'.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: a ride with pickupDay 'Tomorrow' and pickupTime '00:30' resolves to 2026-10-22 00:30 when seen at 22:30, but to 2026-10-23 00:30 when seen at 00:05 (leaveAt 2026-10-23 00:12). A driver accepts at 22:40 and goes online at 00:05. Leave now never fires for the real 00:30 pickup, no backup is triggered, and cancelling at 00:10 is not counted as late.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:130-137 `final now = _clock.now(); final pickupAt = ride.pickupAt(now); final leave = SmartGap.leaveAt(ride, ..., now: now, ...)`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:239-245 `final offset = day == 'today' ? 0 : day == 'tomorrow' ? 1 : null; ... DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset)`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:494 `return build(clockLabel(at), days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow');`
suggested_fix: Store an absolute pickup DateTime (or a date) on the reservation and derive the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' label from it when displaying.

title: Late-cancel pause ends early: it is lifted as soon as the first counted cancel leaves the 7-day period, not at the announced date
description: pausedUntil recomputes `recent`, the late cancels in the last lateCancelPeriodDays, at every call, and returns null when fewer than lateCancelLimit remain. The pause end is announced as recent.last + pauseDays (Notifications, island and the confirmation sheet). With the defaults (limit 2, period 7 days, pause 7 days), the pause actually ends 7 days after the earlier of the two cancels, which can be minutes after it began.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: late cancels at 20 Oct 09:00 and 27 Oct 08:00. Right after the second cancel, pausedUntil gives 3 Nov 08:00 and the driver is told 'Scheduled rides paused until 3 Nov'. At 27 Oct 09:01, 61 minutes later, pausedUntil returns null and the requests are back.
evidence: scheduled_rides.dart:494-500 `final since = now.subtract(Duration(days: rules.lateCancelPeriodDays)); final recent = _lateCancels.where((at) => at.isAfter(since)).toList(); if (recent.length < rules.lateCancelLimit) { return null; } final until = recent.last.add(Duration(days: rules.pauseDays));`
suggested_fix: Record the pause (its start and end) when the limit is reached and honour that end date, instead of re-deriving it from a sliding window.

title: ScheduledRideStore is never cleared on logout: the next driver inherits the previous driver's accepted reservations, Leave-now trips, late cancels and pause
description: All scheduled-ride state is static (_requests, _accepted, _lateCancels, reminder, backupNote), and reset() is @visibleForTesting with no app caller. Logout (_logout in main.dart:180-195 and the Profile fallback) clears prefs, the waybills, demo dispatch, safety alerts and the session, but not this store. After logout and a new login on the same device, the new DriverHome runs _startScheduled on the old store. It shows the previous driver's accepted rides (rider names, addresses), plans their reminders and Leave-now, and opens them as this driver's trip. It also keeps their late-cancel pause. The demo dispatch reset re-opens the same reservations while the store still marks them accepted.
failure_scenario: Driver A accepts the Karin reservation and late-cancels twice, which pauses Scheduled rides. A logs out and driver B logs in on the same phone. B sees 'Scheduled rides paused until …' and A's accepted ride. At A's Leave-now time, the ride opens as B's active trip.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:706-707 `@visibleForTesting static void reset() {`
main.dart:180-194 `_logout()` resets prefs, MapTrafficSetting, DriverLanguage, _activeRide, _waybills, dispatch, _safetyAlerts and _session, but never ScheduledRideStore
suggested_fix: Expose a non-test clear on ScheduledRideStore (and DemoReservations.reset) and call it from the logout path alongside the other in-memory resets.

title: Leave-now is pushed later than the latest departure whenever the drive is longer than the 'be online' window allows, so the driver is guaranteed to be late, and gets no reminders
description: SmartGap.leaveAt is documented as 'the latest moment to set off'. _planScheduled clamps the trip start to `leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave`, so when leave < onlineBy the ride opens at onlineBy, after the latest moment to leave. The reminders and the online reminder are also only scheduled when they are `isBefore(leave)`, so in this case none fire between leave and the clamped start. For a normal ride (online 30 min before, spare 15 min) this happens whenever the estimated drive exceeds 15 min, roughly 6 km straight-line. A code comment says 'never before the be online window' is intended, but that rule directly contradicts leaveAt's meaning.
failure_scenario: The driver is 12 km from a normal 10:00 pickup. The estimated drive is 31 min, so leave = 09:14 and onlineBy = 09:30. No 60-min reminder fires, because 09:00 is not before 09:14. The trip opens at 09:30, 16 minutes after the latest departure, and the driver arrives about 10:01 plus the spare time they no longer have.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:146 `if (time.isAfter(now) && time.isBefore(leave)) {`
home_scheduled.dart:153 `if (onlineBy.isAfter(now) && onlineBy.isBefore(leave)) {`
home_scheduled.dart:157 `final start = leave.isBefore(onlineBy) ? onlineBy : leave;`
smart_gap.dart:94-95 `/// "Leave now": the latest moment to set off ...`
suggested_fix: Open the trip at `leave` when it is earlier than onlineBy (or at least warn at `leave`), and schedule the reminders relative to the actual start.

title: The Accepted-tab reminder note survives a driver or rider cancel of the ride it was for
description: ScheduledRideStore.reminder is set by Home's reminders ('Pickup at 08:05 in 1 h: …', 'Head to your 07:40 pickup now') and cleared only on Leave-now start, a backup handoff, or reset(). _cancelAccepted (689-704) and riderCancelled (674-684) remove the ride but leave the reminder. The Accepted tab keeps showing the Reminder note (_notes at 108-114) for a ride that no longer exists.
failure_scenario: The 60-min reminder for the 08:05 ride fires, then the driver cancels that ride in Scheduled rides. The Accepted tab still shows 'Reminder · Pickup at 08:05 in 1 h: Högsätravägen, Lidingö.' with no such ride listed.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:689-704 `_cancelAccepted` never touches `reminder`
scheduled_rides.dart:674-684 `riderCancelled` never touches `reminder`
scheduled_rides.dart:108-114 `if (_selectedTab == 1 && reminder != null) _ScheduledNote(... body: reminder)`
suggested_fix: Clear (or tie to a ride id) the reminder when the ride it refers to leaves Accepted.

title: The 'New scheduled ride' notification body uses the raw English pickupDay ('Today'/'Tomorrow') in the sv/fr feed
description: _onReservationRising adds DriverNotices.newScheduledRide(day: request.pickupDay, ...). The day is the stored English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' from _DemoReservationSet._at. It is inserted verbatim into tr.noticeScheduledBody, even though ReservationWhen.dayWord exists for exactly this mapping.
failure_scenario: Swedish UI: the Notifications screen shows 'Today 09:30 · 126.75 kr · Tryck för att visa'.
evidence:
home_reservation.dart:212-217 `DriverNotices.newScheduledRide(at: feed.now, day: request.pickupDay, time: request.pickupTime, fare: request.fare)`
driver_notifications.dart:202 `body: tr.noticeScheduledBody(day, time, fare)`
app_sv.arb:1289 `"noticeScheduledBody": "{day} {time} · {fare} · Tryck för att visa"`
suggested_fix: Pass ReservationWhen.dayWord(request.pickupDay), or better the ReservationWhen label.

title: 'N rides hidden: clashes with your pickup' counts requests the driver would not see anyway because of their categories
description: _clashing iterates all _requests without the DriverCategoryChoice.takes filter that _visibleRequests applies. The note at 100-107 therefore says rides were hidden by a clash when they were actually filtered out by category, and its count can exceed what is really hidden.
failure_scenario: The driver drives only Comfort and accepts the 07:40 Comfort ride. The Premium 08:05 Lidingö request (never shown to them) still produces '1 ride hidden · It clashes with your 07:40 pickup'.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:553-556 `for (final ride in _requests) if (_clashWith(ride) case final taken?) (ride, taken)`
scheduled_rides.dart:544-546 `DriverCategoryChoice.takes(ride.category) && _clashWith(ride) == null`
suggested_fix: Apply the same category filter in _clashing.

title: openRequests (Home dot, Home popup) is never refreshed when a pause or admin 'off until' expires
description: block() depends on the current time (pausedUntil(now), driverAccess.offAt(now)), but openRequests is only recomputed inside _changed(), and no timer calls it when the block expires. Home's green dot and _onScheduledRequestsChanged, which re-sends released requests to the popup, stay at 0 or stale until some unrelated store mutation happens. Meanwhile the Scheduled rides screen, which recomputes on build, already lists the requests again.
failure_scenario: Admin sets Scheduled rides off until 14:00 (or a late-cancel pause ends). After 14:00, Home still shows no scheduled-rides dot and no popup, while opening Scheduled rides shows open requests.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:559-561 `static final ValueNotifier<int> openRequests = ValueNotifier<int>(_visibleRequests.length);`
scheduled_rides.dart:568-571 `_changed()` is the only writer; nothing is scheduled at `block().until`
suggested_fix: Schedule a _changed() at the block's `until` (and at request pickup expiry).

title: Requests tab header always says 'Available today' even when the listed requests are tomorrow
description: The Requests tab header is the fixed string tr.schedAvailableToday, whatever pickupDay the requests have. The app's demo books them 2 h, 2 h 25 and 5 h ahead, so from early evening they are 'Tomorrow' while the header still says today.
failure_scenario: At 20:00 the Requests tab reads 'Available today' above cards 'Tomorrow, 01:00–01:05'.
evidence: scheduled_rides.dart:159 `_selectedTab == 0 ? tr.schedAvailableToday : tr.schedUpcoming,`
suggested_fix: Use a neutral header ('Available') or derive it from the requests' days.

title: Driver cancel / end-trip-early / no-show never ends the trip in DriverSessionController, so Home is left permanently 'on trip' and the driver cannot go online
description: Every other way a trip ends calls widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip() (endTrip): accept_ride_trip.dart:379, 402, 456 and 469, plus ride_completed.dart:71. _submitTripCancellation (accept_ride_trip.dart:1356-1447) handles the driver's own cancel, end-trip-early and no-show, and it never calls it. It writes the journal, calls _rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow, discards the waybill and then runs navigator.pop() (or pushReplacement to the next trip). DriverSessionController therefore keeps _activeTripId = A and status onTrip. Back on Home: _isOnline is false, because availableForOffers requires status online. setOnline(true) during a trip only records intent (driver_session_controller.dart:108-112). beginGoingOnline returns early because _activeTripId != null (line 129). didPopNext does not re-check recovery because activeTripId != null (home.dart:182). With a secured next trip, the next AcceptRide's beginTrip(B) is also refused (line 58-61) because A still owns the session.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway widget test. I pushed AcceptRide(tripId 'C1') over Home with DriverSessionController(initialOnline: true), tapped Arrived, slid to start, then Trip options > End trip early > 'Rider asked to end the trip' > confirm. Output: 'G: AcceptRide=0 home=1 activeTripId=C1 status=DriverOnlineStatus.onTrip available=false'. The driver is back on Home but stays offline. Tapping Go online shows the 'online' island notice (home.dart _goOnline calls IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.online)) but the driver never becomes available, until the app is restarted. The same happens for a pre-pickup cancel (released to dispatch) and for a rider no-show.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:1384 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) {...}`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1444-1446 `if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }` (no stayOnlineAfterTrip anywhere in 1356-1447)
compare accept_ride_trip.dart:456 `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); home.pop();`
driver_session_controller.dart:108 `if (_activeTripId != null) { ... _offlineAfterTrip = !value; ... return; }`
home.dart:182 `if (_recoveryResolved && _driverSession.activeTripId == null) {`
suggested_fix: Call widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip() in _submitTripCancellation once the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeded, before pop or pushReplacement, the same way the rider-cancel and authoritative exits do.

title: System/browser Back on the Ride completed screen skips _finish(): the session stays 'on trip' and a handed-off next trip is never opened
description: _completeCurrentTrip replaces AcceptRide with BottomToTopTransition(DriverRideCompleted(...)) (accept_ride_trip.dart:959). The session's trip only ends in DriverRideCompleted._finish (line 71). The next trip is only opened there too (line 72-75). DriverRideCompleted has no PopScope. BottomToTopTransition is a plain ModalRoute, so Android Back, or browser Back on the web/PWA (handlePopRoute -> maybePop), pops it straight back to Home. The session then keeps _activeTripId = A with status onTrip. Home.didPopNext does not restore because activeTripId != null (home.dart:182). If a next trip B was secured, the journal has already handed B's snapshot to storage but nothing opens it. The driver sees an idle Home that cannot go online, while B's rider waits.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway widget test. session.beginTrip('A'), then I pushed BottomToTopTransition(DriverRideCompleted(sessionController: session)) and called tester.binding.handlePopRoute(). Result: the screen pops to Home and 'C: activeTripId=A status=DriverOnlineStatus.onTrip available=false', even after session.setOnline(true).
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:61-76 `void _finish() { ... widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); if (nextRide != null) { _waybills.promoteNextToCurrent(); navigator.pushReplacement(BottomToTopTransition(nextRide)); return; } ...`
(no PopScope/WillPopScope in ride_completed.dart)
navigation_transition.dart:10 `class BottomToTopTransition extends ModalRoute<void>`
home.dart:182 `if (_recoveryResolved && _driverSession.activeTripId == null) {`
suggested_fix: Wrap the page in PopScope(canPop: false, onPopInvokedWithResult: (_, __) => _finish()) so every exit from the completed screen goes through _finish.

title: An admin reassign/release of the current trip silently drops the secured next trip (no handoff, waybill cleared)
description: For every other end of trip A, a secured next trip B is carried forward. Authoritative terminals and rider cancels pass next to CompletionJournal.finish, which hands B to storage, and then push AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next) (lines 314-322, 371-386, 422-475). Driver completion and driver cancel do the same. The released-to-dispatch branch (lines 324-338) only calls _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status). That runs _finish: markTerminal(A) plus clearForTrip(A), with no journal and no next. _leaveAfterRelease then calls _waybills.clearNext() and pops. Dispatch still has B assigned to this driver, but B's snapshot, waybill and screen are gone, and nothing tells dispatch or the rider.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway widget test with PrefsActiveRideRepository. AcceptRide.fromPersisted(A, onTrip, next 'A-next') is mounted and storage holds A with next. Emitting a trip_projection with status searching for A leaves storage with no active snapshot ('A: snapshot after release = null') and no history. The accepted next trip 'A-next' never opens and is not recoverable after a restart.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:324-336 `} else if (status.isReleasedToDispatch) { ... if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) {...} ... await _leaveAfterRelease(status);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:400-401 `_waybills.discardCurrent(); _waybills.clearNext();`
active_ride_controller.dart:125-133 released -> `_write(() => _finish(status), ...)` (markTerminal + clearForTrip only)
suggested_fix: When a next trip is secured, route the release through CompletionJournal-style handoff (or an explicit RideHandoffRepository.handoff(A, next)) and open AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next), as the other terminal exits do. Otherwise explicitly release B to dispatch and record it.

title: Next-trip ids are '<tripId>-next' for every offer during a trip, so a re-offered next trip collides in history and its completion is never archived
description: _uniqueDemoNext (and _onTripRadarOfferForDestination at accept_ride_trip.dart:1038) gives every next-trip offer during trip A the same id: '${widget.tripId}-next' or '-next-destination'. trip_occurrence.dart says every accept path must use a per-occurrence id 'so a repeated demo ride is never hidden as an already-finished trip'; this path does not. Cancelling a secured next trip archives it in history with that id (accept_ride_sheet.dart:270-286). Radar then returns to scanning and the next offer reuses the same id. If the driver secures it, finishes A and completes B, the journal's non-authoritative archive finds an existing row with that tripId and returns without writing (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202).
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway test. Archiving 'A-next' as a driver cancel (searching) and then running CompletionJournal.finish(record 'A-next') leaves history as 'rows=[A-next:TripStatus.searching]'. The completed trip and its earnings never appear, and History shows it as cancelled by the driver.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:963-964 `_NextTripRadarOffer get _uniqueDemoNext => _NextTripRadarOffer(
 id:'${widget.tripId}-next', ...`
accept_ride_sheet.dart:271-283 archive(record, status: TripTransitions.apply(TripStatus.accepted, TripCommand.cancel, TripActor.driver), ...)
prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-202 `if (rows.whereType<Map>().any((row) => row['tripId'] == record.tripId)) { if (!authoritative) return;`
suggested_fix: Give each next-trip offer occurrence its own id (tripOccurrenceId('${widget.tripId}-next')) so a cancelled and a later secured next trip never share an archive or terminal identity.

title: Resuming a stale (>6 h) waiting snapshot adds the whole gap to the pickup wait, putting thousands of kronor of waiting fee on the trip
description: Home offers 'Resume trip' for a snapshot that fails isFresh (home.dart:530-535, the button is enabled whenever endpoints are verified). AcceptRide.initState then adds now - savedAt to _waitSeconds whenever the restored stage is waitingForRider or a stop wait. The free 6-hour window, which exists so 'an abandoned trip cannot revive days later' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:16-17), is not respected for the wait clock, and WaitingTerms.waitingFee has no cap. When the driver slides to start, _paidWaitSeconds += paidWait, and the fee goes into the archived fare and the cash to collect.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway widget test. AcceptRide.fromPersisted(stage waitingForRider, waitSeconds 0, savedAt now-7h) renders AdaptiveTripIsland with 'waitingSeconds=25200 paid=24900'. At 12,26 kr/min that is about 5 088 kr of waiting fee, added to the fare and the cash to collect, for a trip the driver resumed after the app sat dead overnight.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:613-617 `if (restored?.savedAt != null && (widget.initialStage == ActiveRideStage.waitingForRider || _paidStopWait)) { final elapsed = DateTime.now().difference(restored!.savedAt!).inSeconds; _waitSeconds += math.max(0, elapsed); }`
home.dart:535 `FilledButton(onPressed: snapshot.hasVerifiedEndpoints ? () => popOwned(context, true) : null, child: Text(tr.resumeTrip))`
waiting_rules.dart:53-58 waitingFee is uncapped
suggested_fix: Do not credit elapsed wall-clock time beyond the freshness window, or cap it at the no-show point, when resuming a snapshot the driver confirmed as stale.

title: persistNow() silently drops a state change when another background save is in flight (stop advance, secured next trip, next-trip cancel)
description: persistNow calls _write, which returns false without saving or setting persistenceError when _writing is already true (line 276). The trip screen relies on persistNow to make non-stage progress durable. Examples: the stop wait starting (accept_ride_trip.dart:529), the stop wait ending with _stopCursor += 1 and _paidWaitSeconds (862), securing a next trip (1206), and cancelling the secured next trip (accept_ride_sheet.dart:269). A GPS snapshot (every 2 min, line 676) or a lifecycle save can be in flight at that moment. The newer state is then not written until the next 2-minute GPS save, no error SnackBar appears, and no retry runs. This is unlike driver commands, which wait for the background save (D-09).
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway test. With a slow repository, a background persistNow() is in flight; stopIndex changes to 1 and a second persistNow() returns false. After the first save completes, the stored snapshot still has stopIndex 0 ('F: second=false saved=[0] error=null'). If the tab or app dies within the next 2 minutes, the restore puts the driver back at the already-finished stop, or brings back a next trip the driver cancelled (already archived as cancelled), or loses a just-secured next trip.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:276-278 `if (_disposed || _writing) { return false; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:317-320 `return _write(() => _repository.save(_snapshot(_stage)), background: true);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:858-862 `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; ... _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1206 `_rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
suggested_fix: When a background save is in flight, mark the snapshot dirty and re-run the save when it completes (coalesce), instead of returning false.

title: AcceptRide treats AppLifecycleState.inactive as a pause and stops the trip GPS while the trip is still on screen
description: didChangeAppLifecycleState sends inactive into the same branch as paused/hidden/detached, which runs _pauseLiveUpdates. That cancels the position subscription, sets _hasLiveLocation = false, suspends the camera, stops the wait timer and cancels next-trip offer timers. Inactive is reported while the app stays visible: Android multi-window when another app has focus, system dialogs, iOS Control/Notification Center or a call banner, and window blur on the web PWA. DECISIONS.md describes only 'Lifecycle pause persists the snapshot and stops GPS'. While inactive, _nearArrivalTarget is false (location unusable), so Arrived is blocked with 'Location unavailable', and the car and route freeze. The known finding home.dart:189 covers Home's rendering, not the trip screen.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this in a throwaway widget test. With AcceptRide mounted, the GPS stream has a listener. After handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(AppLifecycleState.inactive) alone: 'D: GPS listener after inactive = false'. A driver running Movera side by side with another app (Android split screen), or a web driver whose browser window lost focus, gets no position updates and cannot confirm arrival until the app is focused again.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:716-726 `switch (state) { case AppLifecycleState.resumed: ... case AppLifecycleState.inactive: case AppLifecycleState.hidden: case AppLifecycleState.paused: case AppLifecycleState.detached: _rideLifecycle.persistNow(); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._pauseLiveUpdates(); }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:126-129 `_locationEpoch++; _hasLiveLocation = false; _positionSubscription?.cancel(); _positionSubscription = null;`
suggested_fix: Persist on inactive, but only stop GPS and live updates on hidden/paused/detached.

title: Journal replay re-stamps the queued trip's savedAt to 'now', so a queued trip left in a days-old journal is restored as fresh with no stale-trip prompt
description: An interrupted CompletionJournal (app killed between writing the journal and finishing the handoff, or a storage failure) is replayed by Home on the next cold start (home.dart:508). handoff() writes next.stamped().toJson(), and stamped() sets savedAt = DateTime.now(). Neither handoff nor _replay compares the journal's completedAt with PersistedActiveRide.freshnessWindow. Home then reads a snapshot that is always isFresh and pushes AcceptRide.fromPersisted(B) directly, skipping the 'older than 6 hours' dialog that a normal snapshot of the same age would get.
failure_scenario: The driver finishes A with next trip B secured. The app dies right after the journal write (afterWrite 'journal'). Two days later the driver opens the app: reconcile hands off B with savedAt = now, and Home immediately restores B as a live trip heading to a pickup from two days ago, with no 'Unresolved trip' prompt.
evidence:
prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:184 `if (!await prefs.setString(key, jsonEncode(next.stamped().toJson()))) {`
active_ride_repository.dart:212 `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now(),`
completion_journal.dart:226-227 `await (repository as RideHandoffRepository).handoff(id, next);` (completedAt never compared to the freshness window)
suggested_fix: Stamp the handed-off trip with the journal's completedAt (or keep its original savedAt) so Home's freshness check still applies to an old replay.

title: Snapshot times are stored as local ISO strings with no offset, so on the autumn DST night a restore adds an extra hour of waiting (and the freshness check is off by 1 h)
description: savedAt, arrivedAt, acceptedAt and startedAt are written with toIso8601String() on local DateTime values, which have no 'Z' or offset. They are parsed back with DateTime.tryParse as local time. During the repeated 02:00-03:00 hour in Europe/Stockholm, Dart resolves the ambiguous wall time to the first (CEST) instant. A snapshot saved in the second (CET) 02:xx therefore reads back one hour earlier than it was written. AcceptRide adds now - savedAt to the wait (accept_ride.dart:615), and isFreshAt uses the same difference.
failure_scenario: Tested with the SDK's dart under TZ=Europe/Stockholm: a time saved at 2026-10-25 02:20 CET parses as 00:20Z instead of 01:20Z, and 10 real minutes later the computed age is 1:10:00. A driver waiting at a pickup whose app reloads in that hour gets 3 600 s of extra paid waiting, about 735 kr at 12,26 kr/min.
evidence:
active_ride_repository.dart:251 `if (savedAt != null) 'savedAt': savedAt!.toIso8601String(),`
active_ride_repository.dart:387 `savedAt: DateTime.tryParse(json['savedAt'] as String? ?? ''),`
accept_ride.dart:615 `final elapsed = DateTime.now().difference(restored!.savedAt!).inSeconds;`
suggested_fix: Store snapshot instants as UTC (toUtc().toIso8601String()), as the terminal markers already do.

title: Scheduled-ride waiting terms are chosen by searching the localized matchedVia label for 'scheduled', so they never apply in French or Swedish (and a restored trip keeps whatever language it was accepted in)
description: Home starts a reservation with _openOfferTrip(..., tr.scheduledRide) (home_scheduled.dart:234-237). matchedVia is therefore 'Scheduled ride', 'Course planifiée' or 'Bokad resa'. AcceptRide._waitTerms calls WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia), which only matches 'scheduled' or 'reservation' in the text. In fr/sv the ride type is normal, so the 'Scheduled ride' rule (free wait = ScheduledRideRules.includedWaitingMinutes) and its label are skipped. matchedVia is persisted in the snapshot, so a restored trip keeps whichever type the accept-time language produced.
failure_scenario: Admin sets the reservation policy's included waiting to 10 minutes. A Swedish-speaking driver starts a reserved ride with 'Leave now': the trip shows the zone's 5 free minutes and charges paid waiting and offers no-show after 5 minutes, whereas the same ride in English gets 10.
evidence:
waiting_rules.dart:250-253 `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled; }`
home_scheduled.dart:234-237 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide,);`
lib/l10n/app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`
suggested_fix: Pass the ride type explicitly (or a non-localized source id) into AcceptRide and persist it in the snapshot, instead of deriving it from a display string.

title: Crash/reload restore also drops the rider's bag count, so the trip island stops mentioning the bags after a reload
description: Home passes offer.bags into AcceptRide (home_offer_radar.dart:973) and the island shows it (accept_ride.dart:1314 `bags: widget.bags`). PersistedActiveRide has no bags field and _buildSnapshot does not save it, so AcceptRide.fromPersisted always builds the widget with the default bags = 0. This is separate from the known pickupKm drop.
failure_scenario: A rider booked with 2 bags. The PWA reloads on the way to pickup, the trip is restored from movera_driver_active_ride, and the island no longer tells the driver about the bags.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:143 `this.bags = 0,`
accept_ride.dart:253-291 fromPersisted builds AcceptRide(...) without bags
accept_ride_trip.dart:13-61 _buildSnapshot has no bags
suggested_fix: Add bags to PersistedActiveRide (toJson/fromJson/stamped) and pass it through _buildSnapshot and fromPersisted.

title: A restored trip's waybill shows the time of the last background save as its issue time, not when the trip was accepted
description: _waybillFromSnapshot sets issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt. savedAt is re-stamped on every save (GPS every 2 minutes, lifecycle, stage changes), while the snapshot also carries acceptedAt. After any crash or reload the current waybill's Time row (waybill_sheet.dart:74 formatWaybillTime(record.issuedAt)) shows the last-save time instead of when the trip was accepted. AcceptRide's own path uses DateTime.now() at accept time.
failure_scenario: A trip accepted at 14:02 is restored after a reload at 14:40 whose last GPS snapshot was at 14:38. The waybill shown to the driver (and to an inspector) says the trip was issued at 14:38.
evidence:
home.dart:627 `issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt ?? DateTime.now(),`
active_ride_repository.dart:212 `savedAt: at ?? DateTime.now(),` (stamped on every save)
suggested_fix: Use snapshot.acceptedAt (falling back to savedAt) for the restored waybill's issuedAt.

title: Waybill earnings take Movera's 25% fee out of the waiting fee, which the rules say is all the driver's
description: At completion, _paidWaybill (accept_ride_trip.dart:75-80) folds the driver's waiting fee into the waybill fare (`fare: _fareWithWaiting`) and also stores it in `waitingFee`. The waybill sheet (waybill_sheet.dart:70) then calls `WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)`. The waiting fee is never passed in, so it is treated as part of the rider's base fare and charged the service fee: `_feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round()` and `earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre)`. Q43 / driverShareWaitPercent=100 say the waiting money goes 100% to the driver: ride_completed.dart:174 says 'Q43: the waiting fee is all the driver's' and the wait sheet says 'You get 100% of the wait time'. The bonus is excluded from the fee here, but the waiting fee is not.
evidence:
waybill.dart:319 `int get _feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round();`
waybill.dart:326 `String get earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:76-79 `final fee = _waitTerms.driverWaitingFee(_paidWaitTotal); ... fare: _fareWithWaiting, waitingFee: fee.isZero ? null : fee.formatted`
waybill_sheet.dart:70 `WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: fee=12,26 kr fare=112,26 kr earnings=84,19 kr serviceFee=28,07 kr (expected earnings 75,00 + 12,26 = 87,26 kr)
failure_scenario: A 100,00 kr trip where the driver waits one paid minute (12,26 kr). Ride completed shows 'Includes 12,26 kr waiting fee'. Opening the waybill shows 'Movera fee −28,07 kr' and 'Your earnings 84,19 kr' instead of 87,26 kr. The driver is told Movera keeps 3,07 kr of a waiting fee the app promises is 100% theirs. The error grows with every paid minute.
suggested_fix: Give WaybillPayment the waiting fee (from record.waitingFee) and exclude it from the fee base the same way the bonus is excluded, i.e. fee = round((fare − bonus − waitingFee) × rate). Then show it as its own line.

title: WaybillPayment hard-codes 'kr' and öre, so EUR/TND fares get wrong waybill amounts and wrong currency
description: Money, the contract and DriverAppConfig (currency + rebased waiting rules) support EUR and TND zones. WaybillPayment.fromFare only matches up to 2 decimals (`\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?`), multiplies by 100 and always formats with a ' kr' suffix. So a '24,50 €' fare comes out as '24,50 kr', and a TND fare '125,000 DT' (exponent 3) is read as 125,00 and shown in kr. The same code path drives the offer card's net fare (offer_rules.dart:157 `OfferCardDetails.fare`) and the waybill sheet's 'Paid by the passenger', 'Movera fee' and 'Your earnings' rows.
evidence:
waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);`
waybill.dart:301 `final fareOre = (value * 100).round();`
waybill.dart:333 `return '${_comma ? text.replaceAll('.', ',') : text} kr';`
Throwaway test: EUR 24,50 € → fare=24,50 kr earn=18,37 kr; TND 12,500 DT → fare=12,50 kr earn=9,37 kr
failure_scenario: In a zone whose DriverAppConfig currency is EUR, the waybill of a 24,50 € trip lists 'Paid by the passenger 24,50 kr' and 'Your earnings 18,37 kr'. With net-fare offer cards enabled, the card shows '18,37 kr'. In a TND zone the amounts are also off by the exponent (12,500 DT is read as 12,50).
suggested_fix: Parse with Money.parseLabel (currency-aware, thousands-aware), compute in minor units of that currency, and format with Money.formatted.

title: Waybill always says payment 'In the app', even for a cash trip
description: The payment section of every waybill hard-codes `_Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp)`. WaybillRecord carries no payment method, and the sheet is opened from the Ride-completed page and the trip options for cash trips too. A cash trip's waybill therefore states the passenger paid in the app, although the driver just took the cash in the car (Collect cash sheet), and the Ride-completed page right behind it says 'Cash'.
evidence:
waybill_sheet.dart:89-90 `_Row(tr.paidByPassenger, payment.fare),
      _Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp),`
ride_completed.dart:225 `onTap: () => showMoveraWaybillSheet(context, record, title: tr.lastWaybill)`
accept_ride_trip.dart:966 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'`
failure_scenario: The driver finishes a cash trip, taps Waybill › Open on Ride completed, and the receipt reads 'Payment: In the app' for a trip that was paid in cash. A driver showing it to an inspector or the rider shows a false payment record.
suggested_fix: Store the payment method on WaybillRecord (it is known when the waybill is built) and show the localized method, cash included.

title: Ride-completed chip shows the stored English source ('Exclusive offer', 'Local demo', 'Demo Radar') instead of sourceText
description: WaybillRecord.source holds English storage values (`exclusiveOfferSource = 'Exclusive offer'`, `localDemoSource`, `demoRadarSource`). Its doc says screens must show `sourceText` in the driver's language, and the waybill sheet does (`_Row(tr.via, record.sourceText)`). The Ride-completed chip joins the raw `record.source` instead. A secured next trip is always started with `matchedVia: WaybillRecord.exclusiveOfferSource` (accept_ride_trip.dart:942/1401), and that value becomes the waybill's source (accept_ride_trip.dart:186).
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:340-343 `final label = [ record?.service ?? 'Movera', if (record != null && record.source.trim().isNotEmpty) record.source, ].join(' · ');`
waybill.dart:45-46 `They stay in English in storage; the screens show them in the driver's language.`
failure_scenario: A Swedish or French driver completes a trip that came from an Exclusive offer (or a demo trip). The completion chip reads 'Movera · Exclusive offer' or 'Comfort · Local demo' in English, while the waybill opened from the same page shows the translated source.
suggested_fix: Use `record.sourceText` in the chip.

title: Ride-completed payment row shows hard-coded English 'Card'/'Cash', and says 'Card' for Apple Pay / Google Pay / Swish trips
description: accept_ride_trip.dart:966 passes `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'`, and the page prints it as-is (`Text(widget.paymentMethod ?? '—')`). The value is an English literal, so it is never localized. It is also derived only from the paidByCash bool, while offers carry 'Apple Pay', 'Google Pay' or 'Swish' (api_dispatch_repository.dart:14-19, RideOffer.payment). Every non-cash trip is therefore reported as paid by 'Card'.
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:215 `_row(tr.payment, Text(widget.paymentMethod ?? '—', style: _value)),`
accept_ride_trip.dart:966 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card',`
api_dispatch_repository.dart:17-18 `'apple_pay': 'Apple Pay', 'google_pay': 'Google Pay',`
failure_scenario: A French driver completes an Apple Pay trip. Ride completed shows 'Paiement: Card': the method is wrong and the word is English. A Swedish cash trip shows 'Betalning: Cash'.
suggested_fix: Carry the offer's payment method into AcceptRide and the snapshot, and map it to localized labels (tr.cash, tr.card, …) on display.

title: On a cash trip with a Movera bonus, the driver is told to collect the bonus from the rider
description: RideOffer.driverBonus is 'Movera-paid extra… [fare] already includes it', and WaybillPayment says of the bonus 'the rider never pays it'. On a cash trip whose offer has no explicit cashToCollect (null means 'the fare'), `_cashToCollect` falls back to `widget.fare`, which includes the bonus. That amount (plus the waiting fee) is what the Collect cash sheet shows in the big 'Collect … in cash' tray, and it is journaled as cashCollected. api_dispatch_repository parses driverBonus and paymentMethod independently, so a cash + bonus offer is a valid input.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1007-1009 `String get _cashToCollect => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.cashToCollect ?? widget.fare, _waitTerms.waitingFee(...));`
dispatch_repository.dart: `/// Movera-paid extra for this driver ... [fare] already includes it`
waybill.dart:288-290 `[bonus] ... is Movera's extra already in [fare]: the rider never pays it`
cash_collect_sheet.dart:75 `final amount = _short(cash);`
failure_scenario: An admin radar-group trip with fare 152,40 kr including a 40 kr Movera bonus, paid in cash, with no cashToCollect from the server. At drop-off the sheet says 'Collect 152,40 kr in cash', so the rider is charged Movera's 40 kr bonus. The cash balance then shows 'Settled' instead of Movera owing the driver the bonus.
suggested_fix: When cashToCollect is null, default the cash to fare − driverBonus (plus the rider's waiting fee), so the balance shows the bonus as owed by Movera.

title: 'See all' under Recent payouts opens the bank-account screen, not the payouts list
description: _sectionHeader(title: tr.recentPayouts, action: tr.seeAll) wires its button to push MyBank, the same destination as the payout-account card below. A driver who taps 'See all' expecting the payout history lands on the bank account page.
evidence:
wallet.dart:48 `_sectionHeader(title: tr.recentPayouts, action: tr.seeAll),`
wallet.dart:280-284 `onPressed: () { pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => const MyBank())); },`
failure_scenario: Wallet › Recent payouts › See all opens 'My bank' (payout account) instead of a list of payouts.
suggested_fix: Hide or disable 'See all' until a payout history exists, or point it at a payouts screen.

title: An admin direct-assign claim won after the driver goes offline mid-claim is silently discarded
description: _claimAdminAssign awaits dispatch.claimOffer and then returns early when `_outsideRadarOffer?.id != offer.id`. _goOffline (home.dart:957) sets `_outsideRadarOffer = null`. The Exclusive sheet turns its down arrow and the Back button off while a claim runs, but the top-island long-press does not. home_map_sheet.dart:1110 checks only `reservation != null || exclusive != null`, and `exclusive` is non-null only when no island message is showing (line 969). _claimAdminAssign itself posts the 'Matching…' message (line 847), so while the claim runs the island long-press opens 'Go offline?'. When the driver confirms, the claim then resolves `success`, the early return fires, and no trip opens, no message shows and nothing is declined. Dispatch has already given the trip to this driver. The known finding at home_offer_radar.dart:546 covers the same pattern only for the Radar-card Match path, not for this Exclusive admin-assign path.
failure_scenario: An admin direct assign is up. The driver taps the orb (Accept) and the island shows 'Matching…'. The driver long-presses the island and confirms Go offline. Dispatch answers success. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (completer-controlled claim): island onLongPress enabled during claim: true; AcceptRide after the won claim: 0; island messages: [Radar online, Exclusive ride, Matching…, Radar offline]. The rider's trip is assigned to a driver who never sees it.
suggested_fix: Turn the island (and any other) Go-offline entry off while `_HomeExclusive._exclusiveClaiming` is true, or have _goOffline wait for or decline the claim in flight. Alternatively, on success with the offer no longer on screen, show the trip or send dispatch a decline or release instead of returning silently.

title: Turning Cash rides off (or switching a category off) while a Radar Match claim is in flight drops the won trip and leaves Home stuck in 'Matching'
description: _setAcceptsCash(false) calls _dismissRadarHomeOffer on every cash card, whatever its match state. _onCategoriesChanged (line 33-35) does the same for cards in a category that was switched off. _dismissRadarHomeOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:479-492) removes the card and its match state but never clears `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` or `_claimedHomeOffer`. When the claim then succeeds, _claimHomeRadarOffer still matches the id (line 546) and calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon. _acceptRadarHomeOffer then returns because the card is no longer listed (line 926), so the trip never opens. `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` stays set for good: every other card's Match is disabled (onMatch null at line 1127), the radar orb reads 'Matching / Please wait' with no tap, and _scheduleVisibleOffers returns early on every resume (line 1167-1171). The Home sheet that holds the Cash switch can be dragged open while a Radar card is matching, because only an Exclusive offer locks it. The known finding at home_offer_radar.dart:895 covers only the × path into the same function.
failure_scenario: A cash Radar card is on the deck. The driver taps Match, swipes the Home sheet up and turns 'Cash rides' off before dispatch answers. Dispatch answers success. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: AcceptRide 0; radar orb 'Matching / Please wait', onTap disabled; the other card's Match button disabled; 20 s later still no trip and only the one claim sent. The driver won a trip they never get, and Home cannot match anything else until they go offline and back online.
suggested_fix: Skip resolving or claimed cards in _setAcceptsCash and _onCategoriesChanged. Alternatively, have _dismissRadarHomeOffer clear `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` and `_claimedHomeOffer` when they name the removed offer, and tell dispatch to release a won claim the driver can no longer take.

title: A withdrawn waiting (pending) Radar offer leaves _hasRideOffers true: Home shows 'Trip found / NEW' with no trips and blocks later Exclusive offers
description: _showRadarHomeOffer sets `_hasRideOffers = true` when it parks an offer in _pendingRadarHomeOffers, which happens while an Exclusive offer, a Ride check or a reservation request is up. _onOfferWithdrawn removes that pending offer but never recomputes `_hasRideOffers`. The same happens with _setAcceptsCash(false) (home_offer_rules.dart:53) and _onCategoriesChanged (line 32). When the blocker goes away, _releasePendingRadarOffers returns on an empty pending list (line 459), so nothing resets the flag. Everything that reads the flag is then wrong: the radar button shows the 'Trip found / NEW / Tap for all' face (home.dart:1055-1071), the island gets the green offers ring (home_map_sheet.dart:1061), 'Finding trips' never shows (_waitingForTrips at line 1197), non-reservation Exclusive offers are refused (line 239), and the later Exclusive demo (line 1228) never shows.
failure_scenario: A Ride check is open (or an Exclusive offer is up) when a Radar trip arrives and waits as pending. Dispatch withdraws it (for example, a radar-group trip another driver took). The Ride check is answered. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: with dispatch offers at 0, the radar orb reads title='Trip found' status=NEW subtitle='Tap for all' offer=true, and 'Finding trips' is not shown. The driver is told a trip was found when none exists, and no further Exclusive offer can appear until they tap the radar.
suggested_fix: Wherever pending offers are removed (here, in _setAcceptsCash and in _onCategoriesChanged), recompute `_hasRideOffers = _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty`, as _dismissRadarHomeOffer already does.

title: A pick window that ends during a Match claim is never re-armed: after a network error the card keeps Match enabled indefinitely
description: _startRadarPickWindow stores a Timer in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers and refuses to start another while that key exists (line 425). When the timer fires while the card is `resolving` (a Match claim in flight), the callback returns without adding the id to _radarOfferExpired and leaves the dead timer in the map. If the claim then ends with ClaimOutcome.networkError, _claimHomeRadarOffer only removes the match state (line 560-563), which puts the card back to `available`. It never re-checks the deadline, and no later _startRadarPickWindow call can re-arm, because the stale key is still there. The D-04 rule ('the window has one deadline… Match fades at once when the window ran out') is broken: Match stays live past the deadline until the next pause/resume clears the map. This is a different path from the known :425 finding, which is about expired offers dropped by refresh and listed again.
failure_scenario: A Radar card has about 2 s left in its 15 s pick window. The driver taps Match, the claim takes longer than 2 s and fails with a network error. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: 30 s after the deadline, 'radar-match-audit-card' onPressed is still enabled. The radar sound also keeps treating the card as live.
suggested_fix: On networkError, compare _radarOfferDeadlines[offer.id] with now: mark the card expired if the deadline has passed, otherwise remove the stale timer entry and call _startRadarPickWindow. Alternatively, have the timer callback remove its own map entry.

title: A waiting Radar offer that left dispatch is stuck as a 'Taken' card when Home is paused during its 2.8 s removal
description: The dispatch watcher (line 604-610) also resolves pending offers that left dispatch: they become claimedElsewhere, and the shared _homeRadarLostMatchTimer is meant to remove them 2.8 s later. A pause in that window (another route pushed, a dialog, app inactive) runs _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true), which cancels that timer but keeps the claimedElsewhere state. On resume, _resumeOfferTimers re-schedules removal only for claimedElsewhere offers in _radarHomeOffers, never for those in _pendingRadarHomeOffers. The pending offer stays forever. It counts in the radar button's homeTrips (home.dart:1053), and once the blocker clears, _refreshRadarHomeOffers moves it onto the deck as a 'Taken' card that no timer ever removes. The pick-window timer ignores non-available cards, and the external-claim demo picks only available ones.
failure_scenario: A Ride check is open and a Radar trip waits as pending. Dispatch drops it from the feed. Within 2.8 s the driver opens another screen (any route push) and comes back. The Ride check is then answered. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (with driverRouteObserver installed): after resume the radar still reads '1 trip / NEW'; 25 s later the deck holds ids=[audit-card] taken={audit-card} and the radar reads 'Trip found / Tap for all', though dispatch has had no offers for over 30 s.
suggested_fix: In _resumeOfferTimers, include claimedElsewhere offers from _pendingRadarHomeOffers, or remove pending offers that left dispatch right away instead of giving them a Taken state and a timer.

title: Resuming Home while a Match claim is in flight cancels the reservation's Exclusive-step timer and never re-arms it
description: _scheduleVisibleOffers first calls _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true), which cancels and nulls _reservationOfferTimer (line 789-790). It then returns early when `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != null`, before it re-creates _reservationOfferTimer (line 1238-1245) and before it calls _HomeScheduled._onRadarLive() (line 1248). If the claim then resolves lost (alreadyClaimed/expired/unavailable) or with a network error, nothing calls _scheduleVisibleOffers again until the next pause/resume. The untaken reservation therefore never reaches its 'close to pickup' Exclusive step (job L3, ScheduledRideRules.exclusiveBeforeMinutes), and the smart-gap and assignment start in _onRadarLive is skipped.
failure_scenario: The driver taps Match on a Radar card. During the claim the app goes inactive and comes back (for example, the notification shade is pulled down), or any route is pushed and popped. Dispatch answers 'Taken by another driver'. The open reservation's Exclusive offer, due a few minutes later, never appears on Home while the driver keeps Home open.
suggested_fix: Re-arm the reservation timer and call _onRadarLive before the claim early-returns, or call _scheduleVisibleOffers again when a Home Match claim resolves without opening a trip.

title: The deck's 'All offers' count includes the admin direct assign, which the Radar list and the radar button both exclude
description: _radarTripTotal feeds the LedCountBadge above the Home deck (line 1101). Its count of dispatch trips filters on isNearby, the destination rule and _rideAllowed, but not on isAdminDirectAssign. _radarTripsOpen (line 615-621, used by the radar button) and RideRequests._visibleOffers (ride_requests.dart:134, the list the badge opens) both exclude direct assigns, because 'an admin direct assign is an Exclusive offer, not a Radar trip'. Demo admin offers are on by default outside production (driver_runtime_config.dart:84), and DemoAdminOffers.directAssign has isNearby: true.
failure_scenario: In the default demo build the feed holds admin-group-1, nearby-1..3, admin-group-2 and admin-assign-1. The deck badge reads one more trip than the radar button shows, and one more than the full Radar screen lists when the driver taps it.
evidence:
home_offer_radar.dart:1005-1010:
      final nearby = _latestDispatchOffers
          .where((offer) =>
              offer.isNearby &&
              _followsDestination(offer.dropoffPosition.toLatLng()) &&
              _HomeOfferRules(this)._rideAllowed(offer))
          .length;
vs home_offer_radar.dart:617-618: offer.isNearby && !offer.isAdminDirectAssign &&
suggested_fix: Add `!offer.isAdminDirectAssign` to the filter in _radarTripTotal, or reuse _radarTripsOpen.

title: A Home-accepted trip invents a 4.9 rider rating when the offer's rating does not parse
description: _openOfferTrip passes `double.tryParse(offer.rating) ?? 4.9` to AcceptRide. An offer with no usable rating (empty, '—', 'New') therefore reaches the active ride as a 4.9-star rider. This is the same defect as the known ride_requests.dart:379 entry, but it is a separate call site: every trip accepted from Home (Exclusive offers, the Radar deck, admin assigns, reservations) goes through this line, so fixing only ride_requests leaves it in place.
failure_scenario: Dispatch sends a first-time rider whose rating is '' or '—'. The driver accepts it from the Home deck, and the trip screen shows the rider as 4.9.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:952: riderRating: double.tryParse(offer.rating) ?? 4.9,
suggested_fix: Pass a nullable rating and show 'New' or 'unknown' on the trip screen, as the ride_requests fix should.

title: On DST-change days pickupAt puts every reservation one hour off: it adds the minutes as elapsed time to local midnight
description: pickupAt builds local midnight and then adds the pickup minutes as a Duration. Duration.add counts elapsed time, not wall-clock time. On the day Sweden changes clocks, midnight plus N minutes is a different wall time once you pass 02:00/03:00. Everything scheduled goes through this function: ReservationWhen.pickupOf/ofRequest (reservation_when.dart:104), the Exclusive step and timer (home_scheduled.dart:94, :105), the smart-gap plan (reminders, be-online, 'leave now', backup at home_scheduled.dart:131-161), offerFits/clash (smart_gap.dart:461,496,516) and the late-cancel cut-off (scheduled_rides.dart:518). The next change is Sunday 25 Oct 2026, four days from now. The fallback in ReservationWhen.pickupOf:139 uses DateTime(y,m,d,0,minute), which normalises as wall time, so the two code paths also disagree with each other.
evidence:
driver_home_admin_content.dart:243-244
    return DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset)
        .add(Duration(minutes: minute));
Reproduced with TZ=Europe/Stockholm (throwaway test):
  DST day Today 10:00 -> 2026-10-25 09:00:00.000
  spring day Today 10:00 -> 2026-03-29 11:00:00.000
  Sat eve Tomorrow 10:00 -> 2026-10-25 09:00:00.000
  ReservationWhen.of(at, 08:00) -> 'In 1 h' (pickup shown as 10:00)
failure_scenario: On 25 Oct the driver has accepted a 'Today 10:00' reservation. The app computes the pickup as 09:00. 'Leave now', the reminders, the Exclusive step and the backup hand-off all fire an hour early, and the island says 'In 1 h · 10:00' at 08:00. On 29 March (spring forward) everything fires an hour late, and the ride can be given to a backup driver an hour after the driver should have left. The same happens on the evening before for 'Tomorrow' rides.
suggested_fix: Build the wall time directly: DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset, minute ~/ 60, minute % 60).

title: After midnight, 'Today'/'Tomorrow' reservations are re-read against the new date: a 'Tomorrow 01:00' ride jumps 24 h ahead and never reaches its Exclusive step
description: Reservations keep the relative words 'Today'/'Tomorrow' from when they were booked (DemoReservations._at). pickupAt reinterprets those words against whatever 'now' it is given (driver_home_admin_content.dart:240). The demo books relative to the real clock (main +2 h, clashing +2h25, airport +5 h), so any session opened after 22:00 has 'Tomorrow' rides. At 00:00 each of them silently moves to the day after. Scope code that reads it: _exclusiveStepReached/untilPickup here, _untilExclusiveStep:105, _planScheduled:131 (any re-plan after midnight, e.g. a store change or going online, schedules 'leave now' 24 h late), ReservationWhen.ofRequest (sheet and island labels), ScheduledRideStore.isLateCancel/freeCancelUntil (scheduled_rides.dart:510-519), ScheduledRideStore.upcoming ordering, and the fixed card text built in _ScheduledRide.request (scheduled_rides.dart:1134).
failure_scenario: The driver goes online at 23:00. The main reservation is 'Tomorrow 01:00'. At 00:40 the Exclusive timer fires, _exclusiveStepReached sees 24h20m left and returns false, so the ride never becomes Exclusive on this phone. The Home popup keeps offering it as 'Tomorrow 01:00' when it is 20 minutes away. An accepted 'Tomorrow 01:00' ride cancelled at 00:30 is treated as a free cancel ('Free cancel until tomorrow 00:00') and is not counted as late. A re-plan after midnight moves its 'leave now' to the next night.
suggested_fix: Store an absolute pickup DateTime (or a date plus wall time) when the ride is booked. Derive the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' words only for display.

title: An Exclusive reservation claim won after the offer left the screen (driver went offline mid-claim) is silently discarded
description: _claimExclusiveReservation stops the offer timer and awaits dispatch.claimOffer. If _outsideRadarOffer is cleared meanwhile, the function returns before looking at the result. _goOffline (home.dart:957) and going online (home.dart:918) both set _outsideRadarOffer = null directly; going offline can happen through the Go-offline confirm or _drivingLimitReached (home_account.dart:137). _claimReservation only updates ScheduledRideStore when the claim is lost, so a win is never recorded: no take(upcoming:true), no take(), no trip. The demo dispatch has already removed the reservation from its open set (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:536), so the next claim attempt returns unavailable. This is the same pattern as the known home_offer_radar.dart:856 bug, but on the reservation path.
failure_scenario: The reservation's Exclusive offer is up and the driver taps Accept. While dispatch decides, the driving-time limit is reached (or the driver confirms Go offline). The claim comes back success, but the code returns early. Dispatch has given the reservation to this driver, yet the phone still lists it as Available in Scheduled rides and never starts it. Tapping Accept there later gets 'no longer available', and the rider's booking has a driver who has no record of it.
suggested_fix: On success, always record it: take(id, upcoming: true) when the Exclusive window has not been reached, otherwise keep it as a won trip for when the driver is back online. Only skip the UI work when the offer is gone.

title: Leaving Scheduled rides while an Accept claim is in flight drops a won reservation
description: _openRideDetails pops the details screen with 'accepted' and awaits _claim(ride). The list's back button (_popScheduledRoute) still works while the card shows 'Matching'. If the screen is disposed before dispatch answers, _claim returns false on '!mounted' even when the result was success (line 278), and _openRideDetails also returns on '|| !mounted' (line 222). The ride is never moved from _requests to _accepted, which are static store lists that outlive the widget. Dispatch has already given it to this driver and removed it from its open set.
failure_scenario: The driver taps Accept on a reservation, then taps Back on Scheduled rides before the claim returns. The server awards the reservation to this driver, but locally it stays an open request. Home keeps offering it, and accepting it again gets 'no longer available', which removes it. The driver never gets the ride they won.
suggested_fix: Apply the store change (remove from _requests, insert into _accepted, _changed()) regardless of mounted. Only guard setState, the snackbar and the tab switch with mounted.

title: The late-cancel pause ends early: it is lifted once the oldest triggering cancel leaves the 7-day window, not after pauseDays
description: pausedUntil looks only at cancels inside the last lateCancelPeriodDays and computes the end of the pause from them. As soon as the earlier of the two triggering cancels ages out, recent.length drops below lateCancelLimit and the method returns null, although the pause it announced (recent.last + pauseDays) has not ended. The block notice, the 'Scheduled rides paused until …' notification (scheduled_rides.dart:247-252) and _LateCancelWarning (notes:206) all promise the full period.
failure_scenario: The driver makes late cancels on day 0 and day 6. They are told Scheduled rides are paused until day 13, but on day 7 requests come back. With two cancels an hour apart, the pause ends an hour early.
suggested_fix: Find each moment the limit was reached (the k-th cancel within any period window) and keep the pause until that cancel plus pauseDays, without requiring the older cancels to still be inside the window.

title: The seeded accepted ride stores the translated word as pickupDay, so in Swedish/French it has no pickup time and drops out of the smart gap, clash and late-cancel logic
description: pickupAt only understands the English words 'today'/'tomorrow'. The seed sets pickupDay: tr.tomorrow, which is 'Imorgon' in sv and 'Demain' in fr. Those languages get pickupAt == null for this ride, which removes it from ScheduledRideStore.upcoming (no reminders, no 'leave now'), from SmartGap.clash (requests that clash with it stay visible) and from freeCancelUntil/isLateCancel (the cancel sheet says 'Free cancel up to 1 h before' with no time). In English the same ride takes part in all of those. tr is also read once, at static init, so the language at first access is fixed for the session.
evidence:
scheduled_rides.dart:444-445
        pickupTime: '08:15',
        pickupDay: tr.tomorrow,
Reproduced: language 'sv' -> ScheduledRideStore.upcoming.length == 0; language 'en' -> 1
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver's Accepted tab shows 'Imorgon 08:15'. The app never reminds them or plans 'leave now' for it, and never hides clashing requests. An English driver with the same data gets reminders and a trip at 08:15 tomorrow.
suggested_fix: Keep the stored pickupDay as the canonical 'Tomorrow' (or a date) and translate it only for display (ReservationWhen.dayWord).

title: Reservation cards and the new-reservation notification show the raw English day word ('Today'/'Tomorrow') in Swedish and French
description: _ScheduledRide.request (line 1134) and _ScheduledRide.fromRoute (line 1117) pass route.pickupDay, which is always the English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' from DemoReservations._at, straight into tr.schedSeedTime. _onReservationRising passes request.pickupDay into DriverNotices.newScheduledRide (home_reservation.dart:214), which writes it into tr.noticeScheduledBody. ReservationWhen.dayWord exists for exactly this and is used elsewhere (reservation_route_map.dart:427), but not on these paths.
failure_scenario: With the app in Swedish, every request card in Scheduled rides reads 'Today 07:40–07:45', as do assigned rides in Accepted. The Notifications entry for a new scheduled ride also contains 'Today'.
suggested_fix: Wrap the day with ReservationWhen.dayWord(route.pickupDay), or better, use ReservationWhen.ofRequest, at these three call sites.

title: 'Leave now' is pushed after the latest departure time whenever the drive plus spare exceeds the be-online minutes, so the driver is made late
description: SmartGap.leaveAt is documented as 'the latest moment to set off' (drive + spare before pickup). _planScheduled then takes the later of leave and onlineBy. Whenever driveMinutes + spareMinutes > onlineBeforeMinutes, which only needs a 16-minute drive for a normal ride (30 vs 15 spare), the trip opens at onlineBy, after the latest departure. The arrival is late by the difference, and the planned reminders (filtered to before 'leave') are already gone. The file header calls 'never before its be-online window' intended, so this may be a product choice, but it contradicts leaveAt's contract.
failure_scenario: A normal reservation has a 25-minute estimated drive. leave = pickup-40, onlineBy = pickup-30, so the active trip opens at pickup-30. The driver arrives about 10 minutes after the booked pickup time.
suggested_fix: Open the trip at 'leave' (which is already ≥ the be-online moment when it is later), i.e. start = leave, and use onlineBy only for the be-online reminder.

title: A terminal projection (admin/system cancel, rider cancel, completed) that arrives while an earlier projection is still draining is never applied
description: _onRealtimeEvent stores each status event in _pendingProjection and calls _drainProjection(). If a drain is already running (_drainingProjection true, e.g. it is awaiting applyProjection's save for an earlier stage projection), the new call returns at line 300 without scheduling a retry. When the first drain finishes, the non-terminal branch (lines 340-348) leaves the newer event in _pendingProjection because it is not identical to the one it drained, and the finally block only clears _drainingProjection. Nothing calls _drainProjection again. DriverRealtimeSequenceGate has already recorded the trip as terminal, so every later status event for the trip is dropped as blockedAfterTerminal, and a resync re-delivers the same eventId, which the gate drops as a duplicate. The terminal outcome is only picked up if the driver later tries to finish or cancel (through _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal).
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:300 `if (!mounted || _drainingProjection || _pendingProjection == null) { return; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:340-347 `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } ... if (identical(event, _pendingProjection)) { _pendingProjection = null; }`
driver_realtime.dart:296-298 `if (_terminalTrips.contains(event.tripId) && !event.kind.passesAfterTerminal) { return DriverRealtimeDisposition.blockedAfterTerminal; }`
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. AcceptRide is at headingToPickup and the repository save is held. Emitting the projection `arrived` and then `cancelled_by_admin`, releasing the save and pumping 10 s leaves the active snapshot at waitingForRider and the trip history empty (output: `AUDIT snapshot=ActiveRideStage.waitingForRider history=[]`). The driver keeps navigating to a trip Movera cancelled. After a kill and reopen, Home restores the cancelled trip from the snapshot.
suggested_fix: When _drainProjection returns early because a drain is running, set a 'drain again' flag, or schedule _projectionRetry. At the end of a drain, run again whenever _pendingProjection is not the event just handled.

title: A rider, admin or release cancel pops the topmost route instead of the trip screen: if a sheet or page is open above the trip, the driver is left on a dead trip
description: _handleRiderCancelled uses `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { ... home.pop(); }`. Navigator.pop removes the topmost route. That is AcceptRide only when nothing is open above it. The island and the panel open several routes over the trip: the waiting-time sheet (_openWaitingTime), cancel reasons, trip options, the cash-collect sheet, the rider profile, and pushSingle pages such as Ride history. When the rider cancels while one of these is up, the pop closes that route, and AcceptRide stays mounted with a terminal lifecycle. _advanceRide, _collectCash and the cancel paths all return early on `_rideLifecycle.terminal`, so the trip screen does nothing. The same navigator.pop() exit is used by _leaveAfterRelease (line 403-406) and _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome (line 388-389); the latter pops after its outcome sheet closes, so it again hits the route that was open above the trip.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:452-458 `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { IslandMessages.show(...); widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); home.pop(); return; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:403-406 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.tripRemoved); navigator.pop();`
accept_ride_trip.dart:388-389 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }`
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. Home pushes AcceptRide (waitingForRider), a page is pushed over the trip (as Ride history is from the island), and then riderCancelled is emitted. Result: `AUDIT acceptRide=1 overlay=0 home=1`. The overlay page was closed and the cancelled trip screen is still showing. In real use, a driver who is looking at the Waiting-time sheet when the rider cancels is left on a frozen trip screen and has to leave it by hand.
suggested_fix: Pop to the AcceptRide route itself, for example by capturing ModalRoute.of(context) and calling Navigator.removeRoute, or with popUntil on that route followed by pop. Or close any modal routes above it first.

title: An authoritative projection that moves the trip from waiting to on-trip drops the paid pickup wait (waiting fee lost) and never sets startedAt
description: The driver's own slide (_advanceRide, waitingForRider case, lines 831-843) captures `paidWait = _paidWaitNow`, adds it to _paidWaitSeconds after the transition, cancels the wait timer and sets _onTripStartedAt. ActiveRideController.applyProjection is documented to apply skipped live stages. When a projection rider_onboard, in_trip or approaching_dropoff arrives while the local stage is waitingForRider, _drainProjection calls applyProjection, which changes the stage to onTrip, then only runs _rebuild and _resumeStageSideEffects. The paid seconds already waited are not added to _paidWaitSeconds. Because _paidWaitNow is 0 once the stage is onTrip, _paidWaitTotal, _fareWithWaiting and _cashToCollect drop the waiting fee. _onTripStartedAt stays null, so the short-finish check is also disabled.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:339-341 `} else { if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); _resumeStageSideEffects(); } }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:65-70 `int get _paidWaitNow => !_countingWait ? 0 : ...; int get _paidWaitTotal => _paidWaitSeconds + _paidWaitNow;`
versus accept_ride_trip.dart:832-843 `final paidWait = _paidWaitNow; ... _paidWaitSeconds += paidWait; ... _onTripStartedAt = DateTime.now();`
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. AcceptRide is at waitingForRider with initialWaitSeconds 600 (5 free minutes, so 300 paid seconds), and the projection in_trip is emitted. Saved snapshot before: `wait=600 paid=0`. After: `stage=onTrip wait=600 paid=0 started=null`. The 5 paid minutes (about 61 kr at 12,26 kr/min) disappear from the driver's earnings and from the cash to collect.
suggested_fix: Move the stage-entry bookkeeping into one helper (paid wait carry-over, timer cancel, startedAt, ride-check start) and call it from both _advanceRide and the projection path when the stage changes from waitingForRider.

title: A restored trip loses its pickup distance (and bags), so the waiting terms change after the app is killed and reopened: far-pickup free wait and no-show fee are replaced by the defaults
description: _waitTerms is computed from widget.pickupKm (WaitingRules.termsFor applies the farPickup rule when pickupKm > 5: freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 85 kr). Home, Radar and Ride requests pass offer.pickupKm into AcceptRide. PersistedActiveRide has no pickupKm field, so _buildSnapshot cannot save it, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted does not pass it. After a crash, reload or PWA resume, the same trip gets base terms: 5 free minutes and a 65 kr no-show fee. The waiting clock, the paid seconds, the cash to collect, the driver's earnings and the no-show threshold all change in the middle of the trip. bags is also not saved or restored, so the island's bag notice disappears.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:989-996 `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: widget.category, type: ..., pickupKm: widget.pickupKm);`
accept_ride.dart:253-291 fromPersisted passes no pickupKm and no bags.
waiting_rules.dart `if (pickupKm != null && pickupKm > farPickupKm) { ... terms = terms._with(farPickup, ...); }` with farPickup freeMinutes 1, noShowFee 8500 ore.
failure_scenario: A driver accepts an offer 7 km away and waits at pickup for 4 minutes (3 paid minutes under the far-pickup rule). Safari kills the tab, and Home restores the trip. The island now shows those 4 minutes as included free wait, so the paid wait and the waiting fee drop to 0. The no-show fee the driver is promised falls from 85 kr to 65 kr.
suggested_fix: Save pickupKm (and bags) in PersistedActiveRide.toJson/fromJson/stamped, write them in _buildSnapshot, and pass them through AcceptRide.fromPersisted. Better still, save the resolved WaitingTerms so the trip keeps the terms it was accepted under.

title: An authoritative terminal projection whose local apply fails is archived and marked terminal but never retried: the trip screen stays live on a trip the journal has already closed
