description: For a terminal status other than rider-cancel, _drainProjection first runs CompletionJournal.finish (archive, terminal marker, snapshot cleared) and then calls `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; }`. applyProjection returns false when `saving` is true or when _finish throws (it catches and sets persistenceError). `saving` is true whenever a background persistNow started during the journal's awaits, from a GPS snapshot (every 2 min) or a lifecycle inactive/paused save. Unlike the rider-cancel path (line 343-345) and the release path (line 328-330), this branch schedules no retry and leaves _pendingProjection set. The gate now blocks every later status event, so the controller never becomes terminal. The screen stays on the trip, and every later persistNow against PrefsActiveRideRepository throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip', which shows the 'Trip progress could not be saved' snackbar.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(..., status: status, authoritative:true, next:next); if (!mounted) { return; } if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:115-117 `if (saving || _disposed || ...) { return false; }`
prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:138-139 `throw StateError('Cannot revive a terminal trip');`
failure_scenario: A cancelled_by_admin projection arrives. During the journal write the app goes inactive (notification shade), so persistNow starts a background save. applyProjection then sees saving=true and returns false. The trip is in history as 'Cancelled by Movera', but the driver is still shown navigation to the pickup, and every save attempt shows an error snackbar until they try to finish.
suggested_fix: When applyProjection returns false, call _scheduleProjectionRetry() (as the release branch does), or wait for the background save before applying.

title: Resuming a stale saved trip in the waiting stage adds the whole time the app was closed (6 h or more) to the paid wait
description: Home offers 'Resume trip' for a snapshot older than the 6 h freshness window. In initState, a restored trip at waitingForRider (or at a paid stop wait) adds `DateTime.now() - savedAt` to _waitSeconds without any cap. For a stale snapshot this is at least 6 hours. That time counts as paid waiting and goes into _cashToCollect, _fareWithWaiting and the no-show state.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:613-617 `if (restored?.savedAt != null && (widget.initialStage == ActiveRideStage.waitingForRider || _paidStopWait)) { final elapsed = DateTime.now().difference(restored!.savedAt!).inSeconds; _waitSeconds += math.max(0, elapsed); }`
home.dart:529-535 stale snapshot shows an 'Unresolved trip' dialog with a 'Resume trip' button.
failure_scenario: A driver was waiting at pickup, the phone died, and they reopen the app 7 hours later and tap Resume trip. The island shows about 7 hours of paid waiting. On a cash trip the 'Collect cash' amount includes about 5 000 kr of waiting fee (420 min × 12,26 kr).
suggested_fix: Cap the elapsed time added on restore (for example at the no-show time), or add none when the snapshot is not fresh and the driver chose to resume an unresolved trip.

title: persistNow is silently dropped while another background save is in flight: stop arrival or departure, a secured next trip and a next-trip cancel can be lost on a crash
description: _write returns false at once when `_writing` is true. Several trip changes are persisted only through a single persistNow, and none of the callers check the result or retry: stop arrival (_onArrivedTap sets _paidStopWait, line 529), stop departure (_stopCursor += 1 and paid stop seconds folded in, line 862), a secured next trip (line 1206), and a next-trip cancel (accept_ride_sheet.dart:266). If a GPS snapshot save (every 2 minutes) or a lifecycle save is in flight at that moment, the change is not written until the next save. The documented Safari crash kills the tab with no pause event, so after a reload the trip restores from the older snapshot.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:276-278 `if (_disposed || _writing) { return false; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:856-862 `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; _waitTimer?.cancel(); _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();` (result ignored)
accept_ride_sheet.dart:266 `unawaited(_rideLifecycle.persistNow());`
failure_scenario: A driver leaves stop 1 at the moment a GPS snapshot save is in flight, and the tab crashes a minute later. Restore puts them back in 'waiting at stop 1' and adds the whole drive since the last save to the paid stop wait. A next trip the driver cancelled can likewise come back as secured, while history already records it as cancelled.
suggested_fix: Give persistNow a 'dirty' flag: when a write is in flight, mark the state dirty and save again when that write finishes, instead of returning false.

title: After the trip ends (outcome sheet up), a GPS fix after an app resume can still schedule an on-trip Exclusive offer; when it expires unseen it counts as a missed offer
description: _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome pauses live updates and then awaits showTripOutcomeSheet. If the app is backgrounded and resumed while that sheet is open, _resumeLiveUpdates restarts GPS. _resumeOnTripOffer checks `_rideLifecycle.terminal`, but _applyDriverPosition calls _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer when `_stage == onTrip`, and that function has no terminal check. An offer is then shown under the modal, its expiry timer runs, and _denyNextTripRadar calls ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed(), which can switch the driver offline after the trip.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:684-686 `if (_stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); _rideCheckObserve(); }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1072-1078 the guard checks mounted/paused/stage/scanning only.
accept_ride_trip.dart:1226-1227 `if (ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()) { widget.sessionController?.setOnline(false);`
failure_scenario: Movera cancels a trip while the driver is on board, and the outcome sheet is shown. The driver switches apps and comes back without closing the sheet. 2.2 s later a hidden next-trip offer appears and then expires, and it counts toward the auto-offline missed-offer streak.
suggested_fix: Return early from _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer, _presentOnTripOffer and _resumeLiveUpdates when _rideLifecycle.terminal is true.

title: System back / iOS swipe on any onboarding step closes the whole onboarding flow instead of going to the previous step
description: The onboarding wizard is one route that holds a PageView. Its on-screen back button calls controller.moveToPreviousStep(context), which goes back one page and only pops the route on page 0. The Scaffold has no PopScope or onPopInvoked handler, so the Android system back button, the predictive back gesture and the iOS edge swipe all pop the whole AdditionalInfoNavigation route from every step. The driver then leaves the flow and loses every value typed or picked on earlier steps. The on-screen arrow and the system back behave differently on the same screen.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. I pushed AdditionalInfoNavigation, tapped Continue twice (page == 2) and called tester.binding.handlePopRoute(), which is the Android back button. Output: 'AUDIT onboarding still mounted: false'. The whole wizard was popped, not just step 3 to step 2.
suggested_fix: Wrap the Scaffold in PopScope(canPop: currentPageIndex == 0, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) controller.moveToPreviousStep(context); }), and rebuild it from currentPageIndex.

title: Create account Continue ignores the Terms/Privacy checkbox (and empty name/email)
description: The screen has a Terms of use / Privacy policy consent checkbox (isAccept), but the Continue button reads neither isAccept nor any field. The name and email fields have no controllers, so they cannot be checked. The driver moves on to the phone step without accepting the terms. The checkbox only changes its own look.
evidence:
create_acc.dart:44 `bool isAccept = false;`
create_acc.dart:106-113 CustomCheckBox(value: isAccept, ... onPressed: () { setState(() { isAccept = !isAccept; }); })
create_acc.dart:174-181
  CustomButton(
    centerContent: tr.navContinue,
    onPressed: () {
      Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverCreateAccountPhone()));
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. I opened DriverCreateAccount and tapped Continue without ticking the checkbox or typing anything. Output: 'AUDIT phone step opened without terms: true'.
suggested_fix: Disable Continue (onPressed: null) until isAccept is true and the name and email fields (given controllers) pass validation.

title: Blocked sheet says 'Document approved · You can go online now' while another expired document still blocks going online
description: showDocumentBlockedSheet decides `cleared` from the one document it was opened for. DocumentExpiryStore.blocking, which the going-online gate in home_account.dart uses, returns the first expired document among all of them. When two documents are expired, approving the first one turns the sheet green: 'Document approved', 'You can go online now.', Done. The next go-online attempt is still refused and another blocked sheet opens. The store's documented job is to receive several documents from a backend through load().
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. I used a store with two expired documents A and B, opened the blocked sheet for A, then called uploadNew('A') and approve('A'). Output: 'AUDIT sheet says go online: true; still blocking: B'.
suggested_fix: Compute cleared as documents.blocking == null. When another document is still blocking, show that document's state instead of 'You can go online now'.

title: Camera capture of vehicle registration/insurance is downscaled into an 800x400 box, so portrait document photos come out at about 300x400 px
description: The registration and insurance camera capture passes both maxWidth: 800 and maxHeight: 400 to pickImage. image_picker keeps the aspect ratio and fits the image inside both limits. A normal portrait photo (3024x4032) of an A4 or A5 registration certificate becomes 300x400 px, and a landscape one becomes 533x400. That is too low to read the document's text. The Add vehicle document capture in add_vehicle.dart:850-853 uses only maxWidth: 1024 for the same kind of document.
failure_scenario: The driver holds the phone upright and photographs a registration certificate on the Vehicle registration step. The returned XFile is about 300x400 px and the certificate text cannot be read in the preview or by any later review.
suggested_fix: Drop maxHeight, or use a symmetric bound such as maxWidth: 1600, maxHeight: 1600, with an imageQuality setting so the size stays bounded.

title: Picked document is accepted without checking its type; on web any file passes and is shown as a PDF
description: allowedExtensions is passed to FilePicker.platform.pickFiles, but on web it only sets the input's accept attribute, which is a hint. The user can switch the dialog to 'All files', and a selectFile port can return anything. After the pick the code checks only that the bytes are not empty, then stores the name and bytes and shows 'File selected successfully'. _buildFilePreview shows every non-png/jpg file with the red PDF icon, so a .docx, .heic or .zip looks like an accepted PDF.
failure_scenario: On the web build the driver opens 'Tap to upload', picks 'All files' and chooses notes.docx. The step shows a green 'File selected successfully' snackbar and a PDF icon labelled notes.docx.
suggested_fix: After the pick, check file.extension (lower-cased) against the allowed list, and ideally the magic bytes too, and show couldNotReadSelectedFile for anything else.

title: Phone step Continue opens OTP verification with an empty or invalid phone number
description: The phone number customTextfield has no controller, validator or onChanged. Continue always pushes DriverPhoneVerification, which says a code was sent. The flow moves to OTP entry with no number entered. The phone value is never read, so no later step can use it either.
evidence:
create_acc_phone.dart:82-86 customTextfield(contentHorizPadding: 0, hint: tr.phoneNumber, keyboardType: TextInputType.phone, prefixWidget: ...)  // no controller
create_acc_phone.dart:137-145
  CustomButton(centerContent: tr.navContinue, onPressed: () { Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverPhoneVerification())); })
failure_scenario: In the legacy registration preview the driver taps Continue on the phone step with the field empty and lands on 'Phone verification' with a 4-digit code entry.
suggested_fix: Add a controller, validate the number for the selected country, and enable Continue only when it is valid.

title: Terms/privacy consent text and OTP explanation use RichText, which ignores the system text scale
description: RichText defaults to textScaler: TextScaler.noScaling, unlike Text and Text.rich. The terms and privacy consent sentence next to the checkbox (create_acc.dart:119) and the explanation on the phone verification screen (phone_verify.dart:59) therefore stay at their base size when the user sets large text. All other text on the same screens scales.
evidence:
create_acc.dart:119 `child: RichText(` (no textScaler argument)
phone_verify.dart:59 `RichText(` (no textScaler argument)
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test. At MediaQuery textScaler linear(2) the terms RichText reported 'textScaler: no scaling'.
suggested_fix: Use Text.rich(TextSpan(...)), or pass textScaler: MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context).

title: Phone screens default the country to United States (+1) although the market is Sweden
description: The sign-in phone screen and both create-account screens set the default country to US/+1 in initState, after first declaring '+92' as the field initialiser. DECISIONS.md P2 fixes the market as SEK/Stockholm, and the rest of the app (documents 'Stockholm trips', SEK money) is Swedish. Every Swedish driver has to change the country before typing a number, and a number typed without changing it would be read as a US number.
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver opens 'Sign in with phone' and sees the US flag. They type 0701234567, which would be read as +1 0701234567.
suggested_fix: Default to 'SE' / '+46', or to the market country from DriverAccountRules.current.country.

title: Onboarding vehicle type list is hard-coded English ('Luxury', 'Standard', 'Economy', 'SUV') and the form is pre-filled with sample values as real input
description: The vehicle-type dropdown items are English literals shown as-is in the French and Swedish UI. They also do not match the contract categories (economy, comfort, premium, priority, xl, electric, pet). Separately, make, model, plate and type are initialised as controller text ('Toyota', 'Mark X', 'AQS - 140', 'Luxury'), not as hints. A driver who does not overwrite them keeps sample data as their vehicle. The hint repeats the same value, which makes them look like placeholders.
evidence:
add_vehicle.dart:23-34
  TextEditingController(text: 'Toyota') ... (text: 'Mark X') ... (text: 'AQS - 140') ... TextEditingController(text: 'Luxury');
add_vehicle.dart:38-43 `final List<String> vehicleTypes = const ['Luxury','Standard','Economy','SUV'];`
add_vehicle.dart:171 `hint: 'Luxury',`
failure_scenario: In Swedish, the Add vehicle onboarding step shows 'Luxury/Standard/Economy/SUV' in English. Tapping Continue without editing moves on with Toyota Mark X, plate AQS - 140.
suggested_fix: Start the controllers empty (keep the values as hints only) and build the type list from CategoryCatalog with localized labels.

title: Onboarding Continue/Verify advances through every step with no vehicle data, no document and no ID
description: moveToNextStep advances unconditionally. No step reports whether it is complete: the vehicle fields are not validated and the year is free text, the registration and insurance steps do not require a selected file, and the ID step has nothing to fill. On the last step the button reads 'Verify' and opens document-type selection whatever was entered.
failure_scenario: The driver clears the make field, picks no registration or insurance file and taps Continue four times. They reach 'Verify' and the ID document picker with nothing uploaded.
suggested_fix: Give each step an isComplete signal, for example through a ValueListenable on the controller, and disable Continue/Verify until the current step is valid.

title: DocumentExpiryStore is never reset on logout, so document renewal/approval state and the 'warned' set carry into the next session
description: _logout in main.dart resets the waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and session singletons, but not DocumentExpiryStore.instance, whose reset() is never called from lib. A renewal sent or approved in one session stays: 'in review', or the document now runs a year. The _warned set also survives, so after logout and back in, the 7-day insurance warning is not issued again and Documents shows the previous session's approval.
failure_scenario: The driver taps Upload new and then Approve (demo) on the insurance card, logs out, and taps Return to demo. Documents no longer lists the expiring insurance and Home issues no insurance warning, though a fresh session would show 'expires in 7 days'.
suggested_fix: Call DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset(), and the notification feed equivalent, from _logout next to the other in-memory resets.

title: Legacy auth screens push with raw Navigator.push, so a fast double tap opens the next screen twice
description: Everywhere else the app goes through pushSingle so that a second tap cannot add a duplicate route. The legacy auth and onboarding entry points call Navigator.push directly: create_acc.dart:177, create_acc_phone.dart:140, sign_in.dart:43/81/100/134, select_doc_typ.dart:173 and starter.dart:93. Two taps handled before the next frame push two copies, and the driver then has to press back twice.
evidence:
create_acc.dart:177 `Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverCreateAccountPhone()));`
select_doc_typ.dart:173 `Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(TakeIdPhoto()));`
sign_in.dart:81,100 `Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const AdditionalInfoNavigation()));`
failure_scenario: The driver double-taps 'Continue with Google' and two AdditionalInfoNavigation routes are stacked. Back from step 1 lands on a second copy of the wizard, not on Sign in.
suggested_fix: Replace these calls with pushSingle(context, ...).

title: An OSRM 'continue' or 'new name' step with a turning modifier (uturn, left, right, sharp …) reads "Continue straight 300 m" while the arrow shows the turn
description: In RouteInstructionCopy.cue, the continueStraight/newName branch special-cases only highway 'slight left'/'slight right' and tunnel/toll. Every other modifier falls through to RouteCueKind.continueStraight. OSRM routinely emits type 'continue' with modifier 'left'/'right'/'sharp …', which osrm-text-instructions reads as "Turn left to stay on X", and 'continue' + 'uturn' for turnarounds ("Make a U-turn"). symbolFor() handles the same step correctly: the uturn branch at line 879 and the modifier switch at 909-921 draw a U-turn or left arrow. NavigationController._bannerFor (navigation_controller.dart:575-588) builds banner.primary and banner.instruction from cue(), so the words contradict the arrow. Because continueStraight isOnward, the line is also worded as cruising ('Continue straight 300 m') instead of 'in 300 m'. build() at 573-575 has the same gap ('Continue on X').
failure_scenario: The route reaches a junction where the main road bends left (OSRM: {type:'continue', modifier:'left'}), or OSRM routes a U-turn as {type:'continue', modifier:'uturn'}. The trip banner and island read "Continue straight 300 m" while the icon shows a left or U-turn arrow. A driver who trusts the words drives straight on.
suggested_fix: In the continueStraight/newName branch, return _turn(modifier) for any modifier other than ''/'straight' (and map 'uturn*' to uTurn), the same way the turn branch does. Mirror this in build().

title: A single fix that projects onto a later leg moves the instruction hint forward for good: the banner skips the turns in between and the car snaps to the other street
description: measure() first projects inside [previousAlong-60, previousAlong+400]. The tie rule that prefers forward-consistent progress only applies within 10 m, so any later part of the route that is more than 10 m closer than the current leg wins. This can be a parallel street on an around-the-block route, or the opposite carriageway after a U-turn. The instruction search then starts at instructionHint and only moves forward. NavigationController stores the result unconditionally (_instructionHint = progress.instructionIndex, navigation_controller.dart:480), and DriverCameraPolicy does the same (driver_camera_controller.dart:266). When the next fixes project back onto the real leg (the window misses it, so the global projection is used), along goes back but the hint does not. The maneuvers between the two passes are skipped until a new route object resets the hint: the silent refresh comes after 90 s, or a reroute. The camera policy snaps vehiclePoint to the wrong leg for that fix (driver_camera_controller.dart:269-270), so the car marker jumps to the other street. Fixes with accuracy up to 50 m are accepted, and the jump filter subtracts both accuracies, so a 15-50 m urban-canyon drift is enough.
failure_scenario: The pickup is around the block, or across a divided road that needs a U-turn. One GPS sample drifts toward the return leg. From then on the banner shows the arrival ('Pickup in 500 m') instead of the two turns ahead, for up to 90 s. The camera's turn framing is lost, and the car icon jumps onto the parallel street for that fix.
suggested_fix: Do not let the windowed projection jump forward past a maneuver unless it is clearly better (for example, require the forward candidate to be consistent with the elapsed distance or speed). Also recompute the instruction index from projection.along when along goes backwards (search from 0, or step the hint back while maneuverAlong[hint-1] > along).

title: Any off-route fix resets routeFraction to 0: the trip ETA and remaining distance jump to the full route's values
description: _rebuildBanner sets _progressAlong = progress.offRoute ? null : progress.alongMeters (line 481), so the next projection starts from scratch. routeFraction then reads (_progressAlong ?? 0) / length, so off route the driven share becomes 0 instead of unknown or the last value. AcceptRide uses it directly: _remainingMeters = total * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) and _routeEtaText = seconds * (1 - (routeFraction ?? 0)) (accept_ride.dart:920, 927). The leg progress derived from remaining also drops to 0%. This holds through the 2 s reroute debounce plus the network fetch, and on any single fix more than 50 m off (accuracy up to 50 m is accepted).
failure_scenario: 9 km into a 10 km trip, the driver takes a wrong turn or GPS drifts 60 m. The ETA chip jumps from '2 min' to the full original '18 min', the remaining distance shows the whole route, and route progress falls to 0%. They stay that way until the reroute lands, then jump back.
suggested_fix: Keep the last on-route along value for routeFraction (a separate _lastOnRouteAlong field), or return null while off route and let callers keep their previous ETA, instead of treating null as 0.

title: Web zoom-about-finger compensation uses the requested zoom, not the capped one: on the default raster map, a double tap or pinch at zoom 18 pans the map instead of zooming
description: zoomAt clamps the next zoom to 3..21 and calls map.moveCamera({zoom: next}). Without a configured cloud map ID (the default; the meta tag holds the 'DRIVER_GOOGLE_MAP_ID' placeholder), the map is RASTER with maxZoom capped at 18 (lines 539-541 and zoomCap). Google Maps clamps the applied zoom to maxZoom, but the pan compensation is computed with scale = 2 ** (next - current) using the unclamped next, then applied with pan(). At or near the cap, the map pans by (1 - 2^Δ) × (finger offset from centre) although the zoom did not change, or changed less. The tapped road then moves away from the finger. Pinch does the same on every touchmove frame. The comment at google_driver_camera_port.dart:78 says the bridge caps pinch zoom on raster, but zoomAt uses 21.
failure_scenario: On the web app (raster default), the driver has zoomed in to 18 and double-taps a street 120 px right of centre. The zoom stays 18, but the map scrolls about 120 px sideways. A pinch-out held at the cap makes the map slide away from the fingers on every frame.
suggested_fix: After moveCamera, read the zoom actually applied (Number(map.getZoom())) and compute scale from that, or clamp next to the active maxZoom (zoomCap()) before moving.

title: The 1 s recenter/locate flight clock counts only the 16 ms sleep, not the awaited moveCamera, so the flight runs slower than flightDuration on platforms where moveCamera takes time
description: In the flight branch, flown advances by dt, and dt is measured from a stamp taken after `await _move(...)` returns, around the 16 ms _sleep only. The time spent awaiting controller.moveCamera (a platform-channel round trip on Android/iOS) is never added. The flight therefore lasts flightDuration × (frame time / sleep time) instead of the documented 1 s ('runs on the clock … start to rest'). The #325 measurement was taken on a release web build, where moveCamera resolves almost at once. frame() and tiltTo() in the same class use absolute elapsed time from start, so the inconsistency is only here and in the damped loop (line 333).
failure_scenario: On a phone where each moveCamera await takes about 10-16 ms, a Recenter/Locate tap flies for about 1.6-2 s instead of 1 s, which brings back part of the slow glide #325 removed.
suggested_fix: Measure dt from the previous frame's stamp, taken before _move, or compute the flight progress from a start timestamp like frame() does.

title: The coasted camera chase point is pushed into the car marker via onFrame, so the car icon dead-reckons along the camera's look-ahead bearing (contradicting 'Never the car marker')
description: Each loop frame aims at _at(goal, _coasted(goal)). _coasted extrapolates up to 1.1 s / 22 m along goal.bearing, which is the smoothed camera heading blended up to 21° toward the route ahead, not the car's course. _move calls onFrame(logical) whenever _trackCar is true (target within 25 m of goal.target, which a 22 m coast always is). AcceptRide's onFrame calls _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, …) every frame while following, which overrides the route-snapped _vehicle.moveTo(camera.vehiclePoint). The car marker is therefore drawn at the damped, coasted camera target. DriverCameraPose.speedMetersPerSecond is documented as 'Used only to coast the chase point between GPS fixes. Never the car marker.'
failure_scenario: The driver brakes hard for a light, or makes a turn while the camera bearing lags. Between fixes, the car icon keeps sliding up to 22 m along the old or look-ahead bearing, beyond the stop line or off the road at the corner, then rubber-bands back when the next fix arrives.
suggested_fix: Publish the un-coasted vehicle point (goal.target, or the policy's vehiclePoint) to onFrame, and keep the coasted target only for the camera.

title: formatDistance shows '10.0 km' for 9 950-9 999 m (and '10,0 km' in fr/sv) instead of the '10 km' format used from 10 000 m
description: The decimal count is chosen from km < 10 before rounding. 9.96.toStringAsFixed(1) is '10.0', so distances just under 10 km get a decimal that every distance of 10 km or more drops. This is the same boundary error as the already-reported 999.5 m -> '1000 m' case, at the second boundary, which that finding does not cover.
failure_scenario: The banner counts down a long motorway stretch: '10 km' at 10 020 m, then '10.0 km' at 9 990 m, then '9.9 km'. The label changes format without the value changing.
suggested_fix: Round first (final r = (km * 10).round() / 10;), then choose the decimal count from the rounded value.

title: Answering 'No' to 'Is the car in a safe place?' or 'Is the other person OK?' never reaches the safety alert
description: RideCheckQuestion.updatesAlert only forwards 'Yes' and 'Not sure' (or every answer when alerts:true, which only whoNeedsHelp sets). For carSafe and otherPersonOk the question is phrased the other way round, so 'No' is the dangerous answer: the car is not in a safe place, or the other person is not OK. RideCheckController.answer (ride_check_controller.dart:199) queues services.alerts.update only when updatesAlert is true, so these answers are saved to the trip record but never sent to admin or Dispatch. Meanwhile the harmless 'Yes' (the car is safe, the other person is OK) is sent. The authors saw this polarity problem for whoNeedsHelp ('Any answer updates the alert, not only Yes or Not sure') but not for these two questions. The existing tests check this rule as written (test/core/ride_check_test.dart:422), so they cannot catch it.
evidence:
ride_check.dart:189 `static const carSafe = RideCheckQuestion('Is the car in a safe place?', [yes, no]);`
ride_check.dart:193 `static const otherPersonOk = RideCheckQuestion('Is the other person OK?', [yes, no, notSure]);`
ride_check.dart:213 `bool updatesAlert(String answer) => alerts || answer == yes || answer == notSure;`
ride_check_controller.dart:199 `if (_topic?.red == true && question.updatesAlert(option)) { _queueAlert(...update...) }`
Throwaway test: open, choose(accident), answer anyoneHurt 'No', carSafe 'No', otherPersonOk 'No' -> printed `alert answers: [Ride check=Accident or collision]`
failure_scenario: The driver reports 'Accident or collision', then answers 'Is the car in a safe place?' -> No and 'Is the other person OK?' -> No. The safety team's alert only says 'Accident or collision', with no sign that the car is in an unsafe spot or that the other party is hurt. If the driver had answered that everything was fine ('Yes'), those answers would have been sent.
suggested_fix: Define the alarming answers for each question (for example, carSafe and otherPersonOk alert on No and Not sure), or forward every follow-up answer on red topics.

title: Call 112 from a red follow-up screen is never added to the alert that was already sent
description: On the red follow-up screen, the big 112 button (ride_check_card.dart:738) calls callEmergency. In the followUp case, callEmergency records 'Call 112 = Called 112' locally and then calls _ensureAlert('Called 112'). _ensureAlert returns at once when _alert != null, and no _queueAlert update is made, so the alert sent for the row never learns that the driver went to emergency services. The doc comment on callEmergency says 'Movera is alerted at the same time'.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:157-158 `case RideCheckStep.followUp: _addAnswer('Call 112', 'Called 112');`
ride_check_controller.dart:165 `_ensureAlert('Called 112');`
ride_check_controller.dart:305 `if (_alert != null || _sending) return;`
Throwaway test: choose(unsafe); settle; callEmergency(); settle -> `journal: [sent] alert answers: [I feel unsafe]` while `log answers: [I feel unsafe, Called 112]`
failure_scenario: The driver taps 'I feel unsafe' (an alert is sent), then taps 'Call 112 now'. Dispatch's alert still shows only 'I feel unsafe', with no update that 112 was called. The phone's own trip record does show 'Called 112'.
suggested_fix: In the followUp and called cases, when an alert already exists (or is in flight), queue services.alerts.update(alert.id, answer) with the Called-112 answer.

title: 'Called 112' is recorded and sent as the alert topic before the dialer opens, and is kept when the dialer could not open
description: callEmergency writes the answer 'Called 112' to the record and sends an alert with topic 'Called 112' before handoffEmergencyDial runs. When launch returns false or throws, the card correctly shows 'Could not open the dialer…' (dialFailed), but the trip record (trip details show 'Answer: Called 112') and the alert to Movera still say the driver called 112. Even on success, the app only opens the dialer ('Movera never calls for you'), so 'Called 112' claims a call that may not have happened.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:154 `_addAnswer(RideCheckAnswer.first, 'Called 112');`
ride_check_controller.dart:165-171 `_ensureAlert('Called 112'); final result = await handoffEmergencyDial(...); _dialOpened = result == EmergencyDialResult.opened; _dialFailed = !_dialOpened;` (record and alert never corrected)
failure_scenario: On a device with no dialer (a tablet, or web where tel: is blocked), the driver taps Call 112. The card says the dialer could not open, but the alert sent to admin and Dispatch says the topic is 'Called 112' and the trip history says 'Answer: Called 112'. Responders may assume emergency services are already involved.
suggested_fix: Record the answer as 'Opened dialer for 112' or similar, and append or update with the dial result (opened or failed) after handoffEmergencyDial returns.

title: Ride check (including the instant possible-crash card) opens hidden under Chat or any pushed route or sheet over the trip screen
description: _rideCheckWatching only checks mounted, stage, active, terminal and in-flight flags. It never checks whether the trip route is the current route. The card is drawn inside the trip route's Stack (accept_ride.dart:1357 RideCheckLayer). When the driver has opened Chat (accept_ride_panel.dart:864, pushSingle of a full-screen BottomToTopTransition), or a modal sheet such as the Safety toolkit, a detector event still calls _rideCheck.open and the card opens beneath that route, where the driver cannot see it. RideCheckGate is opened at the same time, so new offers are held back with no visible reason. The 'Is everything OK?' prompt, including a possible-crash card that is meant to open at once with Call 112 on top, stays invisible until the driver happens to go back.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:1451-1453 `bool get _rideCheckWatching => mounted && _stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip && !_rideCheck.active && !_rideLifecycle.terminal && !_completionInFlight && !_cancellationInFlight;`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1471-1473 `_openRideCheck(...) { if (event == null || !mounted) return; unawaited(_rideCheck.open(event, ...)); }`
accept_ride_panel.dart:861-866 `pushSingle(context, BottomToTopTransition(Chat(riderDisplayName: widget.riderName)));`
failure_scenario: Mid-trip, the driver opens 'Message rider' and stays on the Chat screen while stopped for more than 2 minutes. The long-stop check opens on the trip screen under Chat, so the driver sees nothing, and offers silently stop arriving until they leave Chat.
suggested_fix: When the trip route is not current, surface the check above it (for example, pop to the trip route or show it in an overlay or root-level layer), or defer opening and the gate until the trip route is current.

title: tick() trusts a stale stop clock after observation was suspended, so a false 'car has stopped for N min' long-stop check can fire while driving
description: _stillSince is only refreshed by observe(). The trip screen stops calling observe while the app is paused (_pauseLiveUpdates) and while any card is open (_rideCheckWatching is false). After resume, the first fix sets _hasLiveLocation = true (accept_ride_trip.dart:661) but calls _rideCheckObserve only after `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` (up to the 8 s routing timeout, line 683-686). A 20 s ticker tick in that window calls tick(gps: true), which computes `at - _stillSince` from the old timestamp and fires longStop. Nothing resets _stillSince when observation resumes.
evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:81-82 `if (!gps) return _longer(at); return _longStop(at, place) ?? _longer(at);`
ride_check_detector.dart:132-133 `final stopped = at.difference(since); if (stopped <= Duration(minutes: rules.longStopMinutes)) return null;`
accept_ride_trip.dart:661 `_hasLiveLocation = location.isUsableAt(DateTime.now());` ... 683 `await _refreshRoadRoute(force: forceRoute);` ... 686 `_rideCheckObserve();`
failure_scenario: The driver switches to another navigation app for 5 minutes while driving, then returns. On resume, the routing request takes a few seconds. A ride-check tick lands in that window and opens 'Your car has stopped for 5 min', even though the car has been moving the whole time. The longStop trigger is then used up for the rest of the trip.
suggested_fix: Reset the stop clock (_stillAt = null / _stillSince = now) whenever observation resumes after a pause or after a card closes, or call observe before the awaited route refresh.

title: Ride check reason is stored and sent to Movera in the driver's UI language, contrary to the 'record and alert keep English' rule
description: ride_check_l10n.dart states that the topic, trigger and question values 'stay in English: they are what the trip record and the alert to Movera keep'. The reason, however, is built from tr.* (rcStoppedLead, rcMinutes, rcEndedLead, rcOffRouteLead, rcLongerLead, rcCrashLead…) at detection time. Its localized text is then saved in RideCheckRecord.reason (ride_check_controller.dart:124) and sent as SafetyAlert.reason (ride_check_controller.dart:318). As a result, the alert to Dispatch mixes an English topic and answers with a French or Swedish reason, and trip history (ride_check_history_entry.dart:117 `'${check.trigger.text} · ${check.reason}'`) shows the reason in whatever language was active when the check fired, even after the driver switches language.
evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:163 `RideCheckReason(tr.rcLongerLead, tr.rcPercent(percent), tr.rcLongerTrail)`; :176-181 longStopReason uses tr.rcStoppedLead/tr.rcMinutes
ride_check_controller.dart:124 `reason: event.reason.text,`; :318 `reason: event.reason.text,`
ride_check_l10n.dart:4-6 'The values in RideCheckTopic, RideCheckTrigger and RideCheckQuestion stay in English: they are what the trip record and the alert to Movera keep.'
failure_scenario: A Swedish-language driver gets a long-stop check. The alert to the English-speaking safety team reads topic 'Accident or collision' with the reason 'Bilen har stått still i 4 min'. Later, the driver switches the app to English, and the trip details still show 'Long stop · Bilen har stått still…'.
suggested_fix: Keep a language-neutral reason (trigger plus parameters: minutes, meters, place) in the record and alert, and localize it only when displaying it.

title: Ride-check audio files are never deleted: logout keeps them and a second recording orphans the first
description: Recordings go to <documents>/ride_check_audio/<id>.m4a. clearLocalUserData (lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:112-150) only removes SharedPreferences keys, and nothing in lib ever deletes that folder, so cabin audio of riders survives logout and stays on the phone indefinitely, outliving its RideCheckRecord (rows are trimmed to 200 and removed at logout). Within one check, tapping Record again after 'Audio saved' starts a new file (new timestamped id), and _stopRecording overwrites record.audioSeconds. The first file is no longer referenced by anything. LOCAL_DATA.md presents logout as removing the driver's personal ride-check data.
evidence:
ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-38 `Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio') ... path: '${directory.path}/$recordingId.m4a'`
ride_check_controller.dart:251 `await recorder.start('${_record!.id}-${services.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}');`; :287 `_record = _record?.copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds);`
local_data.dart:124-132 only prefs keys removed
Throwaway test (record 30 s, stop, record 5 s, stop) -> `audioSeconds on record: 5` (30 s file unreferenced)
failure_scenario: Driver A records rider audio during Ride checks, then logs out. Driver B logs in on the same phone. Driver A's rider recordings are still in the app's documents folder (and, per the known finding, in iOS backups), with no record pointing to them and no way to remove them except uninstalling.
suggested_fix: Delete the ride_check_audio directory in clearLocalUserData. Delete or keep track of every file produced per check (a list of paths), and remove files whose record was trimmed.

title: Rider-contact unavailable message is hard-coded English in the chat app bar tooltip and snackbar
description: RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage is a const English string. ChatAppBar uses it as the phone button's tooltip and as the snackbar text when tapped (appbar.dart:57-59 and :69), and the trip panel's call button uses it too (accept_ride_panel.dart:851). No localized key exists for it. Its sibling 'pinNotConnected' is localized.
evidence:
rider_contact.dart:9-10 `static const String unavailableMessage = 'Rider phone contact is not connected in this demo.';`
appbar.dart:57-59 `tooltip: RiderContactPolicy.available ? tr.callRider : RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage,`
appbar.dart:68-70 `const SnackBar(content: Text(RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage))`
failure_scenario: In the French or Swedish UI, tapping the phone icon in the rider chat (or on the trip panel) shows the English sentence 'Rider phone contact is not connected in this demo.'
suggested_fix: Add an ARB key (for example riderPhoneNotConnected) and use tr.* at both call sites.

title: Record-audio row shows hard-coded English 'starting…' while the microphone starts
description: Every other state of _RecordAudio uses tr.* strings. The starting state (shown while the permission prompt is up and while the recorder starts) uses a literal English string, which is also read by screen readers through the Semantics label '$title, $detail'.
evidence: ride_check_card.dart:997 `RideCheckAudio.starting => (tr.recordAudio, 'starting…'),`
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver taps 'Spela in ljud' on the Ride check card, and the row reads 'Spela in ljud · starting…' until recording begins.
suggested_fix: Add a localized key (for example recordAudioStarting) and use it here.

title: A malformed Ride-check log is logged with its raw contents and then silently overwritten, losing every saved check
description: _read catches FormatException and logs it with `$error`. FormatException.toString includes a source excerpt, so trip IDs, reasons containing road names and the driver's free-text 'What happened' note reach the log channel (the same class as the known prefs_trip_history/prefs_active_ride findings, at a new site). It then returns an empty list. The next _save writes only the new record over the key, so all earlier checks are destroyed. Individual rows that fail RideCheckRecord.fromJson are also dropped and erased on the next save. Unlike the support repository (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) and the other stores, nothing is preserved.
evidence:
ride_check_log.dart:103-106 `} on FormatException catch (error) { DriverLog.warn('Ride check log malformed: $error'); } return <RideCheckRecord>[];`
ride_check_log.dart:66-76 `final rows = _read(prefs)..removeWhere(...)..add(record); ... prefs.setString(key, jsonEncode({... rows ...}))`
failure_scenario: A truncated localStorage write (for example, the Safari tab killed mid-write, as recorded in DECISIONS.md) leaves movera_driver_ride_checks undecodable. The next Ride check logs the raw blob and replaces the whole history with one row, and the past checks shown in trip details are gone.
suggested_fix: Quarantine the raw value (LocalQuarantine.storeOnce) before overwriting, and log only a generic message without the exception's source excerpt.

title: 'Each trigger opens at most once per trip' is lost on crash-restore: fired triggers are kept only in memory
description: _fired lives in the detector, which AcceptRide recreates in didChangeDependencies (accept_ride.dart:664). AcceptRide.fromPersisted after a reload or PWA resume therefore starts with no fired triggers, and checks the driver already answered on this trip can open again. The restore path also passes the restore time instead of the saved start (accept_ride_trip.dart:108 `startTrip(_rideCheckNow)`), although the detector's doc says 'Restored trips pass their saved start'.
evidence:
ride_check_detector.dart:10 'Each trigger opens at most once per trip.'; :17 `final Set<RideCheckTrigger> _fired = <RideCheckTrigger>{};`; :27-29 '/// Restored trips pass their saved start.'
accept_ride_trip.dart:107-108 `case ActiveRideStage.onTrip: _rideCheckDetector.startTrip(_rideCheckNow);`
failure_scenario: The driver answers a long-stop check ('Traffic'), Safari kills the tab, and the trip is restored while the car is still stuck. A couple of minutes later, the same long-stop check opens again on the same trip.
suggested_fix: Persist the fired triggers (and the trip start) in the active-ride snapshot, or seed them from the trip's saved RideCheckRecords on restore. Pass restored.startedAt to startTrip.

title: Selected support category is discarded when the ticket is saved
description: The draft sheet asks for a category, saves it in the draft, and validates it. The _Ticket built on save has no category field, toJson writes none, and the draft (including the category) is then reset to 'Trip & rider' (line 394-398). The driver's choice is lost as soon as the ticket is created and is never shown again.
evidence:
support_inbox.dart:335-340 `final ticket = _Ticket(subject.text.trim(), message.text.trim(), 'LOCAL DRAFT', false);`
support_inbox.dart:826-834 toJson writes subject, preview, status, unread, messages only
support_inbox.dart:394-398 draft reset to `'category': 'Trip & rider'`
failure_scenario: The driver picks 'Wallet & payments', writes the ticket and saves it. The stored ticket has no category, and the next draft defaults back to 'Trip & rider'.
suggested_fix: Add category to _Ticket (constructor, toJson, fromJson, _valid) and show it on the ticket card or conversation.

title: Driver's own unsent chat messages render as incoming messages (left-aligned with a stock avatar)
description: _sendMessage stores the driver's own text, but every entry is drawn with SenderMessage, which puts a circular profile image (assets/images/chat_prof1.png, a generic memoji) on the left and a grey bubble with an 80 px right margin. That is the usual layout for messages from the other party. The screen title is the rider's name, so the driver's own drafts look like messages from the rider.
evidence: chat.dart:55 `_messages.add(_messageController.text.trim());`; :113-115 `SenderMessage(text: _messages[_messages.length - 1 - index])`; :198-208 avatar `AssetImage(AppAssets.chatProf1)` on the left; :215 `margin: EdgeInsets.only(right: 80)`
failure_scenario: The driver types 'I'm outside' and saves it. The message appears on the left with a face avatar under the rider's name 'Angelica', which reads as the rider's message.
suggested_fix: Right-align the driver's own local messages and drop the rider-style avatar, as the support conversation does.

title: Earnings & history crashes (ArgumentError currency mismatch) as soon as the period holds a non-SEK cash trip
description: `_periodCashBalance` folds every cash trip's balance with `CashBalance.total`, which starts from `Money.ore(0)`, and that is always SEK (cash_balance.dart:54: `balances.fold(Money.ore(0), (sum, item) => sum + item.balance)`). `TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance` builds the balance with `Money.parseLabel`, which keeps the label's own currency ('24,50 €' becomes EUR, '12,500 DT' becomes TND). `Money.operator +` calls `_sameCurrency`, which throws `ArgumentError.value(other.currency, 'currency', 'mismatch')`. `_buildOtherEarningsRow` reads `_periodCashBalance` on every build of the overview, so the throw happens inside build. CashBalanceSheet.build (cash_balance_sheet.dart:49) has the same fold. The contract and ZoneSettings support EUR and TND zones (zone_settings.dart:66-67, 104-105), and RideOffer.fare is a `Money` that keeps its currency, so a cash trip in one of those zones is archived with a non-SEK fare label.
evidence:
ride_history.dart:141-143 `Money get _periodCashBalance => CashBalance.total(_periodCashTrips.map((trip) => trip.cashBalance!));`
cash_balance.dart:53-54 `static Money total(Iterable<CashBalance> balances) => balances.fold(Money.ore(0), (sum, item) => sum + item.balance);`
money.dart:198-201 `if (other.currency != currency) { throw ArgumentError.value(other.currency, 'currency', 'mismatch'); }`
Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: pumping `DriverRideHistory(loadHistory: () async => [TripHistoryRecord(fare: '24,50 €', paymentMethod: 'Cash', completedAt: now-5min, ...)])` gave `tester.takeException()` = `Invalid argument (currency): mismatch: "EUR"`.
failure_scenario: A driver in a EUR or TND zone finishes one cash trip, then opens Earnings & history. The overview build throws and the screen shows the red error widget in debug, or a grey box in release. The cash balance sheet throws the same way.
suggested_fix: Start the fold from the currency of the first balance, or group the totals per currency. Do not add Money values of different currencies.

title: After a network error on Match, the red 'Could not match' banner never clears and covers Radar's Back button and Refresh pill
description: Every other notice is cleared: the lost path arms `_matchNoticeTimer` for 2800 ms and the won path clears the notice after navigation. The `ClaimOutcome.networkError` branch sets `_matchNotice` to an error notice and arms no timer, and nothing clears it until another Match is tapped. The notice is drawn as `Positioned(top: 0)` over the page. `TripStatusBanner` is an opaque Material, which absorbs hits, and it is 10+padTop+44+12 px tall, while the Radar header ends at padTop+64. So the banner fully covers the header: the Back button (`_closeRides`) and the Refresh/new-trips pill cannot be tapped.
evidence:
ride_requests.dart:337-347 `case ClaimOutcome.networkError: setState(() { _matchingOfferId = null; _offerStates.remove(trip.id); _matchNotice = _RadarMatchNotice(type: _RadarMatchNoticeType.error, title: tr.rrCouldNotMatch, message: tr.rrConnectionInterrupted); });` (no timer)
ride_requests.dart:531-537 `if (_matchNotice != null) Positioned(left: 0, right: 0, top: 0, child: _buildMatchNotice(_matchNotice!))`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: a DemoDispatchRepository subclass returns `ClaimResult.networkError()`. After tapping Match on nearby-1 and pumping 60 s, the `radar-match-notice` banner was still present, and tapping the 'Back' tooltip did not call onCloseRides (closeCalls=0).
failure_scenario: The driver taps Match while the connection drops. 'Could not match · Connection interrupted' stays at the top of Radar indefinitely. The driver cannot leave Radar with the Back button or refresh new trips until they tap Match on some other card.
suggested_fix: Arm `_matchNoticeTimer` (for example 2800 ms) in the networkError branch, as the lost branch does. Optionally, also let taps through to the header or offset the banner.

title: Radar's 'N new' refresh pill counts trips that the driver's filter will never show, so Refresh adds nothing
description: `hasNew` lights the refresh pill for any new nearby offer that is not an admin direct assign. It ignores `widget.offerFilter` (Home's `_rideAllowed`: cash rides off, ride categories, the window before an accepted scheduled ride) and ignores destination mode. The pill text `fresh` in `_header` applies the destination filter but not `offerFilter` or admin direct assigns. `_visibleOffers` applies all of them, so after the driver taps Refresh the promised trips do not appear.
evidence:
ride_requests.dart:229-233 `final hasNew = offers.any((offer) => offer.isNearby && !offer.isAdminDirectAssign && !displayedIds.contains(offer.id));`
ride_requests.dart:548-553 `final fresh = _latestDispatchOffers.where((offer) => offer.isNearby && !shown.contains(offer.id) && (!widget.destinationModeActive || _follows(offer))).length;`
ride_requests.dart:135 `if (!(widget.offerFilter?.call(offer.source) ?? true)) { return false; }`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: with `offerFilter` allowing only nearby-1..3, the pill read '9 new' after the demo released its later offers, and tapping it showed none of them (nearby-4 not found).
failure_scenario: A driver with cash rides switched off has Radar open. The demo or the server releases cash trips, the pill says '7 new', and tapping it adds no cards. The same happens in destination mode with off-route trips: the pill says 'New' and nothing is added.
suggested_fix: Compute `hasNew` and `fresh` with the same predicate as `_visibleOffers`: offerFilter, admin direct assign, destination and dismissed.

title: Logout does not reset DrivingTimeClock or DestinationModeSession, so the next driver inherits the previous driver's worked hours, rest block and used destinations
description: `_logout` resets the session, waybills, dispatch, safety alerts, language and traffic setting, but not the two process-wide singletons that enforce admin limits: `DrivingTimeClock.instance` (worked time, `restUntil` after the 12 h limit) and `DestinationModeSession.instance` (`_started` timestamps used by `usedToday()`, `_activeSince`). They are reset only in test/flutter_test_config.dart:64/76. Profile's fallback logout path (profile.dart:397) does not reset them either. Logout then sends the app to DriverStarter in the same process, so the next account that logs in on this phone reads the previous driver's counts.
evidence:
main.dart:179-195 `_logout()` calls clearLocalUserData, MapTrafficSetting.reset, DriverLanguage.reset, _waybills.reset, dispatch.reset, _safetyAlerts.reset, _session.reset, but no DrivingTimeClock or DestinationModeSession reset.
driving_time_clock.dart:15 `static final DrivingTimeClock instance = DrivingTimeClock();`
destination_mode_session.dart:11 `static DestinationModeSession instance = DestinationModeSession();`
destination_mode_session.dart:34 `if (r.dailyLimitOn && usedToday() >= r.destinationsPerDay) { return DestinationRefusal.usedToday; }`
The only resets are in test/flutter_test_config.dart:64 `DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset();` and :76 `DestinationModeSession.instance = DestinationModeSession();`
failure_scenario: Driver A works to the 12 h limit, or uses all of today's destinations, then logs out on a shared phone. Driver B logs in. B is blocked from going online by A's 6 h rest (`restUntil`), or B's first destination is refused with 'destinations used today'.
suggested_fix: Call `DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset()` and replace or reset `DestinationModeSession.instance` in `_logout` and in the profile fallback path.

title: Older history rows without completedAt are never shown in any period, so they cannot be reached in History
description: The repository accepts rows with no `completedAt`: the decoder only validates it when present. The screen even prepares them: `day: at == null ? tr.previous : ...`, and the detail screen's `_when` falls back to `whenLabel` 'for an older record without a time'. But `_periodRidesList` returns false for `at == null` in every period. The overview and the All rides list both read only `_periodRidesList`, so such rides are never listed under Today, Week or Month and their detail screen cannot be opened.
evidence:
ride_history.dart:102-104 `return _rides.where((ride) { final at = ride.completedAt; if (at == null) { return false; } ...`
ride_history.dart:75 `day: at == null ? tr.previous : DriverDates.numericDate(at),`
history_detail.dart:46-52 `/// ... the saved words for an older record without a time.` `return at == null ? _ride.whenLabel : ...`
prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:251-253: completedAt is only validated when non-null.
Reproduced with a throwaway test: a record with no completedAt ('Pick → Drop') was not found under Today, Week or Month.
failure_scenario: A receipt saved before completedAt existed, or a legacy row without a time, stays in storage, but the driver can never see it in Earnings & history.
suggested_fix: Show undated rows in an 'Earlier'/'Previous' group, for example in Month or an All view, or count them under the period that their whenLabel implies.

title: History detail shows the stored English word 'Cash' as the payment method in fr/sv, and card trips show '—' although the completion screen said 'Card'
description: The journal stores the literal 'Cash' for cash trips and null for card trips (accept_ride_trip.dart:916 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null`). The detail row prints `_ride.paymentMethod` raw, so French and Swedish drivers read 'Cash' although `tr.cash` exists. Because card trips are stored as null, their history shows '—', while DriverRideCompleted showed 'Card' for the same trip (accept_ride_trip.dart:966 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'`).
evidence:
history_detail.dart:420 `_detailRow(tr.paymentMethod, _ride.paymentMethod, paymentIcon: true),`
accept_ride_trip.dart:916 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null,`
accept_ride_trip.dart:966 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card',`
app_localizations_en.dart:329 `String get cash => 'Cash';`
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver opens a cash trip in history and reads 'Cash' instead of the Swedish word. For a card trip just completed as 'Card', the history detail shows 'Payment method —'.
suggested_fix: Map the stored code to tr.cash or tr.card when displaying it, and record 'Card' (or a code) for card trips in the journal.

title: Analytics demand labels ('Busy', 'Steady', 'Quiet') and the 'Around Stockholm' title are English in the French/Swedish UI
description: `_areaRow` prints `area.demandLabel` and `_demand` prints `stats.surroundingTitle` straight from the admin seed, which is English only (driver_home_admin_content.dart:716-774 'Busy'/'Steady'/'Quiet', 'Around Stockholm'). Elsewhere the app maps shipped admin defaults to tr (for example WaitingTerms._shown). This screen does not, so localized Analytics mixes English demand chips into fr/sv text. The known finding at analytics.dart:60 covers 'DEMO DATA', the route and the 'Comfort · 21:42' literals, not these.
evidence:
analytics.dart:293 `stats.surroundingTitle,`
analytics.dart:354 `area.demandLabel,`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:716 `demandLabel: 'Busy',` ... :735 `surroundingTitle: 'Around Stockholm',`
failure_scenario: In Swedish, the Analytics area list shows 'Södermalm · Busy 86%' and the heading 'Around Stockholm'.
suggested_fix: Translate the shipped admin default labels through tr, as is done for waiting rules.

title: Destination confirm summary always uses a '.' decimal ('38.1 km') in fr/sv
description: `destinationDistanceTimeLabel` formats with `toStringAsFixed(1)` and a hard-coded 'km · … min'. The confirm sheet shows it unchanged, so French and Swedish drivers see '38.1 km' while the trip island uses the localized ',' mark. This is a separate formatter from the known driver_distance.dart one.
evidence:
destination_confirm.dart:18-19 `String destinationDistanceTimeLabel(double meters, double seconds) => '${(meters / 1000).toStringAsFixed(1)} km · ${_minutes(seconds)} min';`
destination_confirm.dart:331 `destinationDistanceTimeLabel(_meters, _seconds),`
failure_scenario: A French driver confirms a destination and reads '38.1 km · 34 min' instead of '38,1 km'.
suggested_fix: Format the number with the active locale's decimal separator (NumberFormat or the shared distance helper).

title: Trip details keep claiming 'Movera safety team alerted' for Ride checks whose alert only reached the in-memory demo outbox
description: For every record with `alertSent`, the history entry shows `tr.moveraSafetyTeamAlerted` with a red bell. REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md says safety recording and sharing are not connected services and the UI must not claim they succeeded. The known finding covers the live Ride check card (ride_check_card.dart:703). This archived copy in History repeats the claim permanently for each such trip.
evidence:
ride_check_history_entry.dart:148-160 `if (check.alertSent) ... Text(tr.moveraSafetyTeamAlerted, ...)`
docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md: 'safety recording/sharing ... are not connected services. UI must not claim those actions succeeded when only local state changed.'
failure_scenario: After a red Ride check answer, the trip's history detail tells the driver that Movera's safety team was alerted, although nothing left the phone.
suggested_fix: Use wording that says the alert is a demo or was saved locally, consistent with the fix for the live card.

title: Queue position sheet lists English category names, including 'Van', which is not a Movera category
description: The ranks table prints the hard-coded list 'Electric', 'Comfort', 'Electric', 'Electric', 'Van', 'Van' unchanged in every language. 'Van' is not one of the canonical categories in DECISIONS.md P1 (economy, comfort, premium, priority, xl, electric, pet). The airport card opening this sheet says 'Sample: 10 drivers ahead' (tr.queueSample10Ahead), while the sheet shows ranks '2' and '1', so the same sample metric shows two values.
evidence:
my_queue_pos.dart:27-34 `List<String> categories = ["Electric", "Comfort", "Electric", "Electric", "Van", "Van"];`
my_queue_pos.dart:283 `text: categories[index],`
my_queue_pos.dart:195/207 `text: "2"` / `text: "1"`
in_airport_queue.dart:60 `text: tr.queueSample10Ahead,`
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver opens 'My queue position' and sees English category names and a 'Van' category that the app does not offer, next to rank numbers that contradict the '10 drivers ahead' card.
suggested_fix: Use CategoryCatalog display names through tr, use only canonical categories, and keep the sample numbers consistent between the card and the sheet.

title: On web, every live-car marker push leaks a new Blob URL of the arrow PNG and reloads the car image, so memory grows for as long as a trip lasts
description: The active-ride car marker (accept_ride.dart:1484-1498, `icon: widget.vehicleIcon`) uses `MoveraVehicleMarker.createIcon()` -> `arrowAt(1)`, which is `BitmapDescriptor.bytes(png, width, height)`, a BytesMapBitmap (movera_vehicle_marker.dart:128). `_ThrottledVehicleMap` sets `_car.value` every 33 ms whenever the pose changes (accept_ride.dart:1458). While following, `onFrame` snaps the vehicle to the camera target on every 16 ms camera frame (accept_ride.dart:1257-1260), so the pose changes on nearly every tick while driving. Each change goes through `_onLiveMarker` -> `_pushLiveMarker` -> `GoogleMapsFlutterPlatform.instance.updateMarkers(updates)` (custom_google_map.dart:241-242) with the 'driver' marker in markersToChange. In the pinned google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2, `_changeMarker` rebuilds the full options, including the icon (`_markerOptionsFromMarker` -> `_gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor` -> `urlFromMapBitmap`). For a BytesMapBitmap that calls `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(bytes))` through `_bitmapBlobUrlCache`, and `updateMarkers` runs `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches()` after every batch, which clears that cache without `revokeObjectURL`. Every push therefore creates a new, never-revoked Blob URL that holds a copy of the PNG until the page unloads. Because the icon object is new each time, the Maps Marker also fires `icon_changed`. web/driver_map_camera.js:598 handles that by setting `image.src` to the new blob URL, so the browser fetches and decodes the car image on every push. The Home map leaks the same way, once per GPS fix (home_map_sheet.dart:95 rebuilds `_markers`) and once per pin on each RouteFade step. This is the same unbounded growth and per-frame map churn that DECISIONS.md says made Safari kill the tab. Even the documented 5 Hz throttle would not stop it, because the growth comes from the BytesMapBitmap icon being re-sent with each position update. On Android and iOS the same pushes send and decode the PNG bytes on every update, which causes GC and jank but no leak.
failure_scenario: Web or PWA driver on Safari drives a 30-minute trip with the follow camera. About 30 pushes a second for 1800 s is roughly 54,000 Blob URLs (a few KB each, about 100+ MB), plus 30 image decodes a second, and it keeps growing over a shift. Safari's memory pressure reloads the tab ('A problem repeatedly occurred') mid-trip. Worked by hand from the plugin source; not run.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1458 `_ticker = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 33), (_) { ... _car.value = _carMarker; });`
accept_ride.dart:1498 `icon: widget.vehicleIcon,`
movera_vehicle_marker.dart:128 `return cache[key] ??= BitmapDescriptor.bytes(png, width: ..., height: ...);`
custom_google_map.dart:241 `unawaited(GoogleMapsFlutterPlatform.instance.updateMarkers(updates, mapId: controller.mapId));`
google_maps_flutter_web-0.5.14+2 convert.dart:754-760 `_bitmapBlobUrlCache.putIfAbsent(bytesMapBitmap.byteData.hashCode, () { ... return URL.createObjectURL(blob as JSObject); })`
google_maps_controller.dart:577 `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches();` (convert.dart:422-424 `_bitmapBlobUrlCache.clear();`, no revoke)
web/driver_map_camera.js:598 `this.addListener('icon_changed', () => { setIcon(this.getIcon()); car.draw(); });` -> `image.src = icon.url;`
suggested_fix: On web, do not send the car as a bytes-icon marker on every move. Move only the JS car overlay (add a `driverMapCamera.vehiclePosition(id, lat, lng, heading)` call and keep the gmaps Marker static), or use an AssetMapBitmap/stable URL icon on web. At the least, add the 'driver' marker once and update only its position through the JS adapter. Cap the push rate to the documented 5 Hz as well.

title: Home offer-route line animation rebuilds the Home map widget and re-sends up to 7 route polylines at 30 Hz while any offer is shown
description: `_resumeRouteLine` starts `Timer.periodic(_lineTick /*33 ms*/)`. For the first 2.35 s of every 3.6 s cycle each tick computes a new `OfferLinePhase` and assigns `lightLine.value = OfferRouteLine.light(frame.road, phase)`. That builds 6 soft-edge slices plus one 'rest' polyline, each a `routeSlice` walk over the whole road. The Home map is wrapped in `ValueListenableBuilder(valueListenable: _offerRouteFrame.lightLine)` (home_map_sheet.dart:749), so every tick rebuilds `CustomGoogleMap`. The rebuild recomputes `homeMapLayers`, `DriverRouteStyle.sized`, `OfferRouteLine.sized` (a copyWith on every polyline) and the fade wrappers. `GoogleMap.didUpdateWidget` then diffs every polyline (full-route point lists compared element by element) and sends the 7 changed light polylines to the platform, each re-converted to a JS LatLng path on web. CustomGoogleMap.didUpdateWidget also makes the web.configure/vehicle/gestures JS calls on each tick. The Radar deck, Exclusive sheet or reservation sheet can stay up for a long time while online, so this runs continuously. DECISIONS.md records that per-frame rebuilds of the HtmlElementView map made Safari kill the tab, and fixed it by throttling map updates to 5 Hz. RouteFade's own doc says 'The map takes new markers and lines a few times over the fade, not every frame'. This path brings back a 30 Hz map rebuild on Home.
failure_scenario: Driver online on web/Safari with Radar offers on the deck: for every 3.6 s cycle, about 70 Home-map rebuilds and about 490 polyline replacements are sent to Maps JS. That is roughly 8,000 map updates in a 1-minute offer window, which causes jank on low-end phones and the same memory and GC pressure the Safari fix was meant to remove. Worked out from the code; not run.
evidence:
home_offer_route.dart:61 `const Duration _lineTick = Duration(milliseconds: 33);`
home_offer_route.dart:287-296 `frame..linePhase = phase..lightLine.value = OfferRouteLine.light(frame.road, phase, zoom: _routeZoomStep); ... frame.line = Timer.periodic(_lineTick, (_) => tick());`
home_map_sheet.dart:747-756 `ValueListenableBuilder<Set<Polyline>>(valueListenable: _offerRouteFrame.lightLine, builder: (context, light, _) { final layers = layersWith(light); return CustomGoogleMap(...polylines: ...OfferRouteLine.sized(DriverRouteStyle.sized(layers.polylines, ...` 
offer_route_line.dart:125-148 builds up to softSteps(6)+1 polylines per call
suggested_fix: Throttle the light-line updates to the documented 5 Hz (or fewer steps per sweep), keep the outline and core out of the per-tick rebuild by pushing only the light polylines through a platform `updatePolylines` call (as the live marker does), or draw the sweep in the JS adapter on web.

title: Trip camera follow loop (60 Hz moveCamera) and 33 ms car push keep running while the trip screen is covered by another route
description: AcceptRide pauses live updates only on app lifecycle changes (didChangeAppLifecycleState -> `_pauseLiveUpdates` -> `_camera.suspend()`). Unlike Home (didPushNext -> `_pauseHomeUpdates`), it is not RouteAware. When the driver opens a full-screen route from the trip, for example `onHistory: () => pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => const DriverRideHistory()))` (accept_ride.dart:1307), the chat, destination picker or safety screens, GPS keeps arriving and `_camera.update` keeps retargeting. GoogleDriverCameraPort's loop paces itself with `Timer`-based `_sleep(16 ms)`, not vsync, so it keeps calling `controller.moveCamera` about 60 times a second on the hidden map. Each frame's `onFrame` snaps the vehicle pose, so the 33 ms `_ThrottledVehicleMap` timer keeps pushing marker updates. On web each of those pushes also leaks a Blob URL (see the first finding).
failure_scenario: Mid-trip, the driver opens Ride history from the island and reads it for 2 minutes while driving. The invisible trip map gets about 7,200 camera moves and about 3,600 marker pushes, which wastes CPU and battery on native and grows memory on web. Worked out from the code; not run.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:715-724 only lifecycle states call `_rideLifecycle.persistNow(); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._pauseLiveUpdates();`
google_driver_camera_port.dart:328-329 `await _sleep(Duration(milliseconds: settled ? 50 : 16));` (Timer-based, lines 557-563)
accept_ride.dart:1257-1260 `onFrame: (position) { ... _vehicle.snapTo(position.target, _camera.vehicleCourse); }`
home.dart:174 `void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }` (Home has the guard, AcceptRide does not)
suggested_fix: Make AcceptRide RouteAware (or check TickerMode/ModalRoute.isCurrent). On didPushNext suspend the camera and stop the 33 ms ticker, keeping GPS and the trip logic running. On didPopNext resume and recenter.

title: Offer-route pin bitmaps are cached without their localized title, so after a language change Home map pins keep the old language's 'Pickup'/'Drop-off'
description: `OfferRouteMarks.pin` caches the painted bitmap under `'${kind.name}|$value'`. The bitmap's title text is `titleOf(kind)` = `tr.pickup` / `tr.dropOff` (localized). The value is language-neutral for Exclusive and Radar offers ('4 min' comes from `minutes()`, which hardcodes 'min'). DriverLanguage can change at runtime (main.dart:102 listener). After a switch, the next offer with the same minute value reuses the bitmap painted with the old language's title.
failure_scenario: An English-speaking driver sees an Exclusive offer with a '4 min' pickup, then switches to Swedish in Settings. The next offer with a 4-minute pickup shows the pin 'Pickup / 4 min' in English on the Swedish Home map until the app restarts.
evidence:
offer_route_marks.dart:79 `final key = '${kind.name}|$value';`
offer_route_marks.dart:82-83 `return _cache[key] = await RouteMarkPins.labelled(kind, titleOf(kind), value);`
offer_route_marks.dart:21-22 `static String get pickupTitle => tr.pickup; static String get dropoffTitle => tr.dropOff;`
suggested_fix: Include the title (or the current locale) in the cache key, e.g. `'${kind.name}|${titleOf(kind)}|$value'`, or clear `_cache` when DriverLanguage changes.

title: A screen-reader scroll action on the trip slide runs the trip step with no confirmation dialog
description: PHASE_53 says assistive-technology activation of the slide shows a confirmation dialog before the trip action runs. Only the Semantics onTap (_accessibleConfirm) does that. The inner GestureDetector has onHorizontalDragUpdate/onHorizontalDragEnd and is not excluded from semantics, so Flutter's RawGestureDetector adds SemanticsAction.scrollLeft/scrollRight to the same node. In Flutter (checked in /opt/flutter widgets/gesture_detector.dart:1786-1806 and rendering/proxy_box.dart:4253), scrollRight calls onHorizontalDragUpdate with delta = size.width*0.8 and then calls onEnd straight away. _update sets _fraction = 0.8w/(w-58) >= 0.78, which snaps to 1. _finish() then sees _fraction >= _trigger and awaits widget.onConfirmed(), which is _advanceRide(): Start trip, Complete trip, Go to stop. No dialog is shown. The regression test (test/audit/accessible_confirmation_test.dart) only fires SemanticsAction.tap.
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user focuses the slide ('Complete trip') and does a three-finger horizontal swipe, or a TalkBack user does the scroll gesture. The trip advances (completed, or started before the rider boards) with no 'Confirm this trip action?' dialog.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1670-1681
  return Semantics(
    button:true, enabled:!_confirming,
    label:widget.label.replaceFirst('Slide to ',''),
    onTap:_confirming ? null : _accessibleConfirm,
    child:FocusableActionDetector(...
      child:GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onHorizontalDragUpdate: (details) => _update(details.delta.dx, maxTravel),
        onHorizontalDragEnd: (_) => _finish(),
accept_ride.dart:1619-1624 _update: _fraction = next >= _trigger ? 1 : next;
accept_ride.dart:1631-1637 _finish: if (_fraction < _trigger) {...return;} ... await widget.onConfirmed();
suggested_fix: Pass excludeFromSemantics: true to the slide's GestureDetector (or wrap it in ExcludeSemantics/BlockSemantics), so the only assistive path is the Semantics onTap that opens the confirmation dialog. Add a test that performs SemanticsAction.scrollRight and expects no stage change.

title: While online and waiting, the Home menu and destination search are hidden from screen readers with no other way to reach them
description: When the driver is online with no offer (_waitingForTrips), the island shows the waiting face and `waiting` is true. That sets `tucked`, which wraps both side buttons (Menu, the only openDrawer call on Home, and Search destination) in IgnorePointer plus AnimatedOpacity(opacity: 0). An opacity-0 subtree is dropped from the semantics tree. Sighted drivers get the buttons back because the island Listener calls _islandWaiting.touch() on onPointerDown. A screen-reader double-tap sends SemanticsAction.tap, not a pointer event. The middle InkWell's tap goes to _onIslandEarningsTap, which only cycles the hidden money face, so the waiting state never ends. The Home dock and sheet have no menu or destination entry, and the drawer edge swipe has no semantics action. This is the steady online state, so it lasts as long as no offer arrives.
failure_scenario: A TalkBack/VoiceOver driver goes online. The island now reads 'Finding trips', and Menu (Settings, Ride history, Documents, Log out, Safety) and Search destination are no longer in the accessibility tree. Double-tapping the island never brings them back. The driver must go offline to open the menu or start destination mode.
evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart:1020-1036
  final tucked = _islandMessage != null || reservation != null ||
      exclusive != null || waiting;
  Widget side(Widget button, {bool tuck = false}) => AnimatedContainer(
      width: tucked || tuck ? 14 : 54,
      ... IgnorePointer(ignoring: tucked || tuck,
        child: AnimatedOpacity(opacity: tucked || tuck ? 0 : 1, child: button)
home_map_sheet.dart:1044 onPointerDown: (_) => _islandWaiting.touch(),
home_map_sheet.dart:1297-1299 _onIslandEarningsTap(){ if (_islandWaiting.takeSwallowedTap()) return; ... cycles _islandFace }
suggested_fix: Keep the side buttons in the semantics tree while tucked (for example AnimatedOpacity alwaysIncludeSemantics plus a semantics-only tap path), or call _islandWaiting.touch() from the island's semantic tap too. Another option is a Semantics customSemanticsActions entry for Menu and Search on the island.

title: Radar offer fare is cut mid-number on the Home deck at 320 px / 130% text in French (e.g. '104,' or '1' shown as the price)
description: The big fare is a Text.rich with maxLines: 1 and no overflow handling (default clip, softWrap on) inside an Expanded. The Expanded sits next to a Column holding the upper-cased 'PRISE EN CHARGE' label (letterSpacing 1.4). On Home the deck slot is viewport-28 wide and the header reserves 34 px on the right for the corner ×. If the price does not fit, the paragraph wraps and only line 1 is painted. Money.formatted groups thousands with a plain space, which is a break opportunity. Hand estimate (Inter metrics × 0.93 for Roboto, no build run): at 320 px the fare area is 292-2-20-34 = 236 px. At ×1.3 the FR pickup column is ~134 px, leaving ~102 px. '104,80 kr' needs ~151 px and '104,80' ~118 px with no break inside, so the line breaks by grapheme and shows '104,'. For '1 234,50 kr', '1 234,50' needs ~158 px (still too wide at 360 px in FR ×1.3), so line 1 is just '1'. The l10n layout test renders this card full-width without onClose and only checks for exceptions, so it cannot catch clipping.
failure_scenario: A French driver on a 320-360 px phone with 130% text sees a Radar card whose price reads '104,' instead of 104,80 kr, or '1' instead of 1 234,50 kr, and may match or skip the trip on the wrong fare.
evidence:
radar_offer_card.dart:335-359
  Expanded(
    child: Text.rich(
      TextSpan(text: whole, style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 42, ...),
        children: [TextSpan(text: rest, style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 20, ...))]),
      maxLines: 1,
    ),
  ),
  Column(... Text(driverText(DriverTexts.offerPickup).toUpperCase(), style: TextStyle(fontSize: 10.5, letterSpacing: 1.4)) ...
radar_offer_card.dart:175 padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(20, 16, onClose != null ? 34 : 18, 18)
home_map_sheet.dart:874 width: math.max(0, viewportWidth - 28)
money.dart:209 buffer.write(' ');  // thousands separator
suggested_fix: Wrap the fare in FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown, alignment: centerLeft) as OfferSheetBody already does, or set softWrap: false with an ellipsis, and use a non-breaking space for thousands. Add a layout test that checks the rendered fare width on the Home deck at 320 px ×1.3 fr/sv.

title: The stale-location label above the trip map buttons has unbounded width: it is cut off at the left edge and blocks map gestures
description: _buildMapControls puts a plain Text (tr.demoOffersLiveLocationUnavailableStale while there is no fresh fix) at the top of a Column with crossAxisAlignment.end. That Column is placed with Positioned(right: 14) and no left or width (accept_ride.dart:1328), so it gets unbounded width and the text lays out on one line. FR 'Offres de démo — position en direct indisponible ou ancienne' is ~272 px at 1.0 and ~355 px at 1.3 (hand estimate), wider than the 306 px left of the buttons on a 320 px phone, so the start of the text is clipped off-screen. The Column is also wrapped by _mapOverlay: PointerInterceptor plus Listener(behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque, onPointerDown: _setMapGesturesBlocked(true)).
