The whole Column rectangle (text width × ~204 px: text + 50 + 12 + 56 + 12 + 56) therefore swallows touches and absorbs the map, on web through the interceptor element. This happens whenever live GPS is missing or stale, which is common on web.
failure_scenario: During a trip with no fresh GPS, a driver tries to pan or pinch the map in the band left of the Safety/Google/Recenter buttons (about 230-290 px wide, 200 px tall). Nothing happens. In French at 130% on a 320 px phone the label reads '…de démo — position en direct…' with its start cut off.
evidence:
accept_ride_panel.dart:543-547
  return Column(
    crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end,
    children: [
      Text(_freshRadarLocation ? tr.demoOffers : tr.demoOffersLiveLocationUnavailableStale, style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 10)),
accept_ride_panel.dart:13-21 _mapOverlay: PointerInterceptor(child: Listener(behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque, onPointerDown: (_) => _setMapGesturesBlocked(true), ...
accept_ride.dart:1328-1330 Positioned(key: ValueKey('active-ride-map-controls'), right: 14, bottom: ...
suggested_fix: Move the label out of the hit-tested overlay, or give it a bounded width (ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: viewport-28)) with wrapping or maxLines + ellipsis. Wrap only the buttons in _mapOverlay so the opaque area matches the controls.

title: The Ride check emergency button loses its number in French: 'Appeler le 112' is ellipsized at 130% text on 320-375 px phones
description: The main Ride check step puts 'Call 112' and 'I'm OK' side by side in two Expanded _button()s. Each label is a maxLines: 1, TextOverflow.ellipsis Text (16.5 px w700) after a 19 px icon and an 8 px gap. The card clamps text scale to 1.3. Card width is screen - 20, content width card - 32, so each button is (content - 9)/2 and the label room is that minus 27. Hand estimate: 320 px → 102 px; 375 px → 130 px. 'Appeler le 112' is ~103 px at 1.0 and ~134 px at 1.3 (Roboto estimate); 'Tout va bien' is ~119 px at 1.3. The l10n test checks only for overflow exceptions, which an ellipsis never throws.
failure_scenario: A French driver with 130% text on an iPhone SE/mini-size phone gets the safety card. The red button reads 'Appeler le…' and the white one 'Tout va b…', so the emergency number is not visible on the button that calls it.
evidence:
ride_check_card.dart:486-497
  Row(children: [
    Expanded(child: _button(key: const ValueKey('ride-check-call-112'), label: tr.call112, icon: AppAssets.solarPhoneCalling, ...)),
    const SizedBox(width: 9),
    Expanded(child: _button(key: const ValueKey('ride-check-ok'), label: tr.iMOk, ...)),
ride_check_card.dart:833-844
  _solar(icon, foreground, 19), const SizedBox(width: 8),
  Flexible(child: Text(label, maxLines: 1, overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis, style: TextStyle(fontSize: 16.5, fontWeight: FontWeight.w700)))
ride_check_card.dart:383 MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(maxScaleFactor: 1.3,
app_fr.arb: "call112": "Appeler le 112", "iMOk": "Tout va bien"
suggested_fix: Stack the two buttons vertically when the label does not fit (LayoutBuilder + TextPainter), or let the label scale down with FittedBox. Never ellipsize the emergency label.

title: The demo banner uses the status-bar inset but leaves it in MediaQuery, so every screen below adds the top inset a second time
description: MaterialApp.builder puts DemoModeBanner (SafeArea(bottom:false)) above Expanded(child: navigator) in a Column. SafeArea pads only its own subtree. The sibling navigator still gets the app's MediaQuery with the full padding.top, because LayoutViewport copies media.copyWith(size: surface) and keeps the padding. Every Scaffold/AppBar below the banner pads for the status bar again, Home places its island at paddingOf(context).top - 4, and AcceptRide reserves safeTop + 210 for the banner area. On a notched or Dynamic Island phone that is a 47-59 px empty band under the banner on every screen, and a shorter expanded trip sheet.
failure_scenario: On an iPhone 14/15 (top inset ~47-59 px), Android builds included, the strip 'Demo mode — no account' sits under the status bar. Below it, every AppBar starts with another ~50 px blank band, and the Home and trip islands float that much lower over the map.
evidence:
demo_mode_banner.dart:6-9
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => SafeArea(bottom: false,
   child: Semantics(label: tr.demoModeNoAccount, child: ColoredBox(...
main.dart:163-168
  child: LayoutViewport(
    child: Column(children: [
      const DemoModeBanner(),
      Expanded(child: child ?? const SizedBox.shrink()),
layout_viewport.dart:46 data: media.copyWith(size: surface),
suggested_fix: Wrap the Expanded navigator in MediaQuery.removePadding(removeTop: true), or place the banner inside the safe area without SafeArea and let routes keep the inset.

title: The Radar card's Route button and the Live-list dismiss × have no accessible name (and the × is a 30 px target)
description: The route-preview control (radar-route-<id>) is an InkWell around an SVG, with no Tooltip, Semantics label or text. The full-screen list's dismiss control (radar-offer-dismiss-<id>) is an InkWell around Icons.close_rounded with no semanticLabel, inside a 30×30 SizedBox. Screen readers announce both as an unnamed 'Button'. R07 claims labels for icon controls, but its test only checks IconButton, so these InkWells slip through. The corner × on Home is labelled (tr.closeOffer), which shows the gap.
failure_scenario: A TalkBack user moving through an offer card hears 'Button' for the route preview and 'Button' for dismiss, with no idea which one removes the offer. Sighted drivers must hit a 30 px × to dismiss an offer in the Live list.
evidence:
radar_offer_card.dart:483-497
  Material(color: const Color(0xFFF2F3F5), ... child: InkWell(
    key: ValueKey<String>('radar-route-${offer.id}'),
    onTap: matching ? null : onRoute,
    child: SizedBox(width: 54, height: 54, child: Center(child: _icon(AppAssets.offerRoute, 22, ink))),
radar_offer_card.dart:299-311
  InkWell(key: ValueKey<String>('radar-offer-dismiss-${offer.id}'), customBorder: const CircleBorder(), onTap: onDismiss,
    child: const SizedBox(width: 30, height: 30, child: Icon(Icons.close_rounded, size: 17, ...)))
suggested_fix: Wrap both in Tooltip/Semantics(button: true, label: ...) (e.g. tr.viewRoute / tr.closeOffer) and grow the dismiss hit area to at least 44×44.

title: The Exclusive/Reservation decline control is a 34×34 target
description: ReservationCloseArrow is the only way to take an Exclusive offer or reservation request off Home (onDecline). Its touch area is the 34 px circle with no hit slop, below the 44/48 px minimum. It sits in the sheet's top-right corner next to the 104 px Accept orb.
failure_scenario: A driver at a red light trying to skip an Exclusive offer has to hit a 34 px circle. Misses land on the sheet, and the countdown keeps running.
suggested_fix: Keep the 34 px visual but wrap it in a 48×48 SizedBox/Padding hit area (as IslandSideHitSlop does for the island).

title: Trip options (with Cancel/End trip) open from a 36 px ••• target, and the island's status-face info button is only 24×28
description: The current-trip card's ••• (onMore: _showTripOptions, which holds Cancel trip / End trip early, Safety and Retry route) is a 36×36 InkWell. On the island's status face the only route-options control is an InkWell in a 24 px-wide slot with a 28 px-high SizedBox. Both are below 44 px. While waiting at pickup the island info button is replaced by a timer and long-press is disabled, so the 36 px ••• is the main way to cancel.
failure_scenario: A driver at pickup who needs to cancel must hit a 36 px dot menu in the full sheet. On the 'Routing…'/status island the options icon is a 24×28 px target.
evidence:
trip_card.dart:95-110 Tooltip(message: moreTooltip ?? tr.tripOptions, child: Material(... child: InkWell(key: moreKey, onTap: onMore, customBorder: const CircleBorder(), child: SizedBox.square(dimension: 36, ...
adaptive_trip_island.dart:402-423 SizedBox(width: 24, child: waiting ? Icon(...) : Tooltip(message: tr.tripRouteAndOptions, child: InkWell(onTap: widget.onRoute, child: SizedBox(height: 28, child: Icon(Icons.info_outline_rounded, size: 22)))))
suggested_fix: Make the ••• hit area 48×48. Give the island info button a 44+ px hit box (IslandSideHitSlop-style growth) without changing the paint.

title: The Ride detail back button is an unlabelled ~24 px InkWell
description: The only on-screen way back from DriverRideHistoryDetail (opened from every history card) is an InkWell over a ResSize 24×24 circle holding Icons.arrow_back_ios_rounded with no semanticLabel/Tooltip. Screen readers announce an unnamed button, and the target is about 24 px. The R07 tooltip test covers IconButton only.
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user opening a past trip finds an unnamed 'button' at the top. A sighted driver has to hit a ~24 px circle to go back.
evidence:
history_detail.dart:118-142
  InkWell(
    onTap: () { popOwned(context); },
    child: Container(height: ResSize.h * 24, width: ResSize.w * 24, decoration: BoxDecoration(shape: BoxShape.circle, ...),
      child: Center(child: Icon(Icons.arrow_back_ios_rounded, color: AppColor.black, size: ResSize.h * 18)),
suggested_fix: Use an IconButton with tooltip: tr.back (44-48 px), or wrap it in Semantics(button: true, label: tr.back) and enlarge the hit area.

title: Destination confirm close (×) button has no accessible name
description: The close control on the destination confirmation map (opened from the destination picker) is an InkWell around SvgPicture.asset(AppAssets.solarClose) with no Tooltip, Semantics or semanticsLabel. It is announced as an unlabelled button. The same kind of icon-only close in waiting_time_sheet.dart:464 (36 px, Icons.close_rounded without semanticLabel) has the same problem, although that sheet also has a text 'Close' button.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader driver on the destination confirm map hears 'Button' for the control that backs out of destination mode setup.

  child: InkWell(
    key: const ValueKey<String>('destination-confirm-close'),
    customBorder: const CircleBorder(),
    onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).maybePop(),
    child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(13), child: SvgPicture.asset(AppAssets.solarClose, width: 22, height: 22)),

title: The radar orb's status and hint text is 4-6 px with about 1.5-2.4:1 contrast (OFF / Tap to scan / MATCH)
description: The orb is the main Home control (Go online, Accept, Hold to go offline) and the trip's next-trip toggle. Its status line is fontSize 6.1*s and its subtitle 5.9*s, with s = size/104: 6.1/5.9 px on Home and 4.1/4.0 px on the 70 px TripRadarDock. Colours: offline status E2E9E6 on the ~8F999C-727D80 grey disc is 2.4-3.4:1. The subtitle B7C2BE on the same disc is 1.6-2.3:1. The 'hot' status in offerAccent 969CA1 on 727D80 is 1.5:1. These are the words telling the driver whether Radar is off, live or matching. The Semantics label covers screen readers but not low-vision sighted drivers.
failure_scenario: In daylight an offline driver cannot read 'OFF · Tap to scan' on the radar, and on a trip the dock's 'Hold · OFF · Stop radar' is 4 px text.
suggested_fix: Raise the status/subtitle to at least 10-11 px at the 104 px size and use colours that reach 4.5:1 on the disc, or move the state word outside the orb.

title: The ONLINE/OFFLINE status pill in the menu header has 2.3:1 / 2.8:1 contrast
description: The live-status pill draws 10.5 px w800 text. Online is MoveraRadarOrb.onlineGreen 5FB87D on the same green at 10% over white (≈EFF8F2), 2.3:1. Offline is 8A9390 on F1F2F2, 2.8:1. Both are well below the 4.5:1 needed for small text, on the one place in the menu that states the driver's availability.
failure_scenario: A driver opening the menu in bright light cannot read whether the pill says ONLINE or OFFLINE.
suggested_fix: Use a darker text tone (e.g. 1C6B45 for online, 5F6B72 for offline) on the tinted pill.

title: The enabled 'I've arrived' button is drawn at 2.6:1 contrast until the car is near
description: The primary heading-to-pickup action stays enabled when !_nearArrivalTarget (tapping runs _blockedArrival with a message), but its label is 8E979B on EEEFF1, about 2.6:1. That is under 4.5:1 for an active control, and the semantics give no hint why it looks disabled.
failure_scenario: Approaching pickup, the driver sees a washed-out 'Je suis arrivé' that looks disabled but is tappable, and its label is hard to read in sunlight.
evidence:
accept_ride_panel.dart:893-894
  backgroundColor: near ? const Color(0xFF111614) : const Color(0xFFEEEFF1),
  foregroundColor: near ? Colors.white : const Color(0xFF8E979B),
accept_ride_trip.dart:513-516 if (!_nearArrivalTarget) { _blockedArrival(); return; }
suggested_fix: Keep a readable foreground (≥4.5:1, e.g. 5F6B72) in the not-near state, and add a semantics hint (e.g. 'available within 100 m').

title: The 'All offers' opener is a ~27 px-high badge that is not exposed as a button
description: The Home deck's 'All offers' control is a GestureDetector around LedCountBadge. The badge is padding 5+5 around 14 px DSEG digits with a 1.5 px border, about 27 px tall. LedCountBadge sets Semantics(label, excludeSemantics: true) without button: true, so assistive tech reads 'N all offers' without a button role.
failure_scenario: The driver has to hit a ~27 px strip to open the full offer list, and screen readers do not announce it as actionable.
evidence:
home_offer_radar.dart:1097-1100 top: GestureDetector(key: const ValueKey<String>('radar-home-all-offers'), onTap: _openRideOffers, child: LedCountBadge(count: _radarTripTotal(), label: tr.allOffers, ...
led_count_badge.dart:44-48 Semantics(label: '$count ${label.toLowerCase()}', excludeSemantics: true, child: Container(padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 10, vertical: 5),
suggested_fix: Wrap the badge in Semantics(button: true) and give it a 44 px minimum height hit area (Padding or ConstrainedBox around the GestureDetector child).

title: The slide action is read twice: its Semantics label is merged with the child Text
description: The slide's Semantics sets label: widget.label but does not set excludeSemantics. The child Text shows the same string (or confirmedLabel while confirming), and its label merges into the same node, which has tap, scroll and focus actions. Other controls in the app (Ride check buttons, offer pill, LedCountBadge) use excludeSemantics: true to avoid this.
failure_scenario: TalkBack reads 'Start trip, Start trip, button'. While the action runs, it reads the stale label plus the new confirmed text.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1670-1673 return Semantics(button:true, enabled:!_confirming, label:widget.label.replaceFirst('Slide to ',''), onTap: ...
accept_ride.dart:1712-1718 Text(_confirmed ? widget.confirmedLabel : widget.label, ... maxLines: 1,
suggested_fix: Add excludeSemantics: true (together with removing the GestureDetector's semantics, see the scroll-action finding) and keep the label in sync with the confirmed state.

title: If the first GPS fix fails, the trip screen never subscribes to the position stream, so GPS stays dead until the app is backgrounded and resumed
description: `_startLiveLocation` subscribes to `watchPosition` only after `getCurrentPosition()` succeeds (lines 597-619). The catch branch (621-629) marks location unavailable and asks for a route, but it never calls `watchPosition`. Nothing else re-arms GPS: `_startLiveLocation` is called only from `initState` (accept_ride.dart:655) and `_resumeLiveUpdates` (line 152), which runs on `AppLifecycleState.resumed`. On native, `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition` throws a `TimeoutException` once its 8 s `timeLimit` passes. The `getLastKnownPosition` fallback is used only for a fix that is at most 30 s old and accurate to 50 m or better, so a cold GPS (trip start or crash-restore in a garage or tunnel) rethrows. Home fixed exactly this case: home_map_sheet.dart:52-55 says "A transient one-shot GPS failure must not leave Home without a location subscription" and re-listens in its catch. The trip screen has no such fix. test/audit/location_resume_failure_test.dart 'current GPS failure still blocks arrival' never feeds a later stream fix, so it cannot catch this.
failure_scenario: A driver accepts a trip, or the trip is restored after a crash, while the phone has no fresh fix (underground garage, cold GPS). getCurrentPosition times out after 8 s. The island shows 'Location updating…' for the rest of the pickup leg even after the sky is clear again. The car marker, camera follow and route progress never move. 'Arrived' is refused with 'Location unavailable. Enable location to confirm arrival.' The only recovery is to background and reopen the app.
suggested_fix: In the catch branch, subscribe to `watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)` the same way the success branch does (guarded by the same epoch check), as Home does. Add a test that fails the one-shot request, then emits a stream fix and expects arrival to work.

title: When the first GPS fix fails, the trip asks for and draws a road route from the hard-coded Stockholm placeholder position
description: `_driverPosition` starts as `_fallbackDriverPosition = LatLng(59.3262, 18.0595)` (accept_ride.dart:423 and 543) and changes only when a real fix is applied (`_applyDriverPosition`, line 660). When `getCurrentPosition` fails, the catch calls `_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)`. With external routing on, which is the build default (driver_runtime_config.dart:88-91), that calls `_navigation.ensureRoute(origin: GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition), ...)` (line 704-709). It fetches a route from that placeholder to the pickup and draws it: `_roadGeoPoints`, `_routeDurationSeconds`, the turn banner and the ride-check plan all come from it. Combined with the missing stream subscription above, this route stays on screen.
failure_scenario: A driver in Gothenburg starts a trip with no GPS fix yet. The trip map draws a 470 km road line from Gamla Stan in Stockholm to the pickup. The ETA and turn instructions describe that drive, and the ride-check detector plans against it.
suggested_fix: Do not request a road route until a real, usable fix exists; in the catch, clear the route or show the pickup only. Treat `_driverPosition` as unknown (nullable) until the first accepted fix.

title: With GPS unavailable, Destination mode measures distance and time from the hard-coded city-centre placeholder
description: Home's `_driverPosition` starts at `_fallbackDriverPosition` (home.dart:394-395, Stockholm centre). It is replaced only by a saved or live position. When location is denied or GPS fails, `_startLocationFailed` opens the map 'without a car', but `_openDestinationModePicker` still passes `origin: _driverPosition` to the picker. The picker supports `origin == null` (destination_picker.dart:146-149, skipping the confirm step), but Home never passes null. DestinationConfirmScreen then puts the car at the placeholder, draws the arc from there, and computes `_meters`/`_seconds` from the straight-line distance or a road route from that point (destination_confirm.dart:80-83 and 127-131). It returns those figures. With no live GPS, `_fetchLatestDestinationRoadRoute` returns early (home_map_sheet.dart:356), so `_destinationFigures` falls back to the confirmed figures. The Home bar and details sheet keep showing the wrong 'NN min · NN km'. `_fitDestinationRoute` also frames `[_driverPosition, destination]`.
failure_scenario: A driver outside Stockholm with location blocked (and no saved start position) turns on Destination mode to 'Home, 3 km away'. The confirm screen shows the car in central Stockholm and '412.0 km · 290 min'. After confirming, Home's destination bar keeps showing '290 min · 412 km' for the whole session.
suggested_fix: Pass `origin: _startPositionKnown || _hasLiveDriverLocation ? _driverPosition : null`, or refuse Destination mode until a real position is known, so the picker's no-origin path is used and no figures are invented.

title: Denying location once makes the app ask again straight away (and two denials block location for good on Android)
description: `_ensurePermission` calls `Geolocator.requestPermission()` on every call while the status is `denied`. Both `getCurrentPosition` and `watchPosition` call it. Home calls it again right after a denial on two paths. (1) The catch in `_startDriverLocation` (home_map_sheet.dart:49-55) immediately calls `_listenToDriverLocation()`, whose `watchPosition` (an `async*` stream) runs `_ensurePermission` again. This is the web path, where the browser prompt does not change the app lifecycle. (2) On Android the permission dialog pauses the activity (`inactive`). On `resumed`, `_resumeHomeUpdates` (home.dart:204-207) runs `_startDriverLocation` again, which requests again. The trip screen does the same through `_resumeLiveUpdates` (accept_ride_trip.dart:152). After the driver taps 'Deny', geolocator_android reports `denied` (the system will still show the rationale), so a second dialog appears at once. A second denial on Android 11+ is permanent ('don't ask again'). Chrome auto-blocks a site after repeated dismissals.
failure_scenario: On first launch the driver taps 'Don't allow' on the location dialog. Another identical dialog pops up immediately. Tapping 'Don't allow' again on Android 11+ makes the denial permanent, so the app can never ask again and the driver must find the setting by hand. On web, the browser prompt reappears straight after it is dismissed.
suggested_fix: Request permission only from an explicit user action (going online, recenter) or once per session. In the stream and resume paths use checkPermission only and surface 'location off' instead of prompting again.

title: A failed sound unlock (prime) leaves the radar player at volume 0 for good, so later offers make no sound
description: `prime()` sets volume 0, plays, stops, then sets volume 1, with no try/finally. If `setSource` or `play` throws, `setVolume(1)` never runs. On web, audioplayers_web awaits `player.play().toDart`, which rejects with NotAllowedError outside user activation. Home calls `tap()` from `Listener.onPointerDown` (home.dart:707), and a touch pointerdown is not an activation-triggering event on mobile browsers. The failure is swallowed by `_then`'s queue (`_queue = next.catchError(...)`) and by `tap()`'s `.catchError((Object _) {})`. `_primed` is already true, so prime never runs again. `startLoop()` only sets the release mode and plays; it never restores the volume. Once a later tap gives the page sticky activation, the loop plays, but silently. Home's `RadarOfferSound` lives as long as Home.
failure_scenario: On a phone browser the driver's first touch on Home starts prime. play() rejects (not yet a user activation), so the player stays at volume 0. For the rest of the session, new Radar offers start the looped alert at volume 0. The driver hears nothing and misses offers.
suggested_fix: Wrap the body of prime in try/finally and always `setVolume(1)` in the finally; reset `_primed = false` on failure so a later tap retries, or pass `volume: 1` in `startLoop`'s play call.

title: The 'Could not match' banner after a network error on the Radar screen never clears and covers the Back and Refresh buttons
description: On `ClaimOutcome.networkError` `_claimTrip` sets an error `_matchNotice` and schedules no timer to clear it. Every other notice path does: lost match at line 452 (2800 ms), success through `_matchNoticeTimer`. The notice is drawn as a `TripStatusBanner` in `Positioned(top: 0)` over the whole screen (lines 531-536). It is an elevated opaque Material, 10+pad.top+44+12 px tall, while the header (Back and Refresh) is pad.top+8+44+12 px. It therefore fully covers and absorbs taps on the Back button (`_closeRides`) and the Refresh control. It goes away only when the driver taps Match on another card and that claim resolves.
failure_scenario: The driver taps Match on the full Radar list while connectivity drops. The red 'Could not match · Connection interrupted' banner appears and stays after the connection returns. The header's Back button and the 'new trips' Refresh under it cannot be tapped (no system back on iOS), so the driver is stuck on Radar unless they try another Match.
suggested_fix: Schedule the same 2800 ms `_matchNoticeTimer` that clears `_matchNotice` in the networkError branch, after cancelling any previous one.

title: A failed 'Show traffic on map' save is dropped as an unhandled future: the switch shows the new value, nothing tells the driver, and it reverts on the next start
description: `toggle` calls `MapTrafficSetting.set(value, _settings)` and throws the returned Future away. `set` updates `enabled.value` immediately, then returns `SettingsRepository.save`. That save throws (`StateError('Settings save failed')` or a `LocalWriteSession` StateError) when storage refuses the write. The error is never awaited or caught, so it becomes an uncaught async error (logged by `installGlobalErrorHooks`). The switch shows the unsaved value and no failure message or retry appears, unlike Sound & voice, Accessibility and Preferences, which show `_saveFailed` with Retry. On the next cold start `MapTrafficSetting.restore()` (main.dart:41) loads the old value.
failure_scenario: On web with localStorage full (vehicle photos fill most of the ~5 MB quota), the driver turns traffic off. The switch shows Off and the trip map hides traffic for this run. No error is shown. After the next app start traffic is back on.
suggested_fix: Await the save in the Settings row; on failure revert `enabled.value` and show a SnackBar or retry like the other settings screens.

title: ApiDispatchRepository catches only FormatException around offer parsing: a mistyped optional field aborts a list reload halfway or throws out of the SSE listener
description: `OfferWire.parse` documents that it throws FormatException, but some optional fields are read with casts that throw TypeError: `(json['riderTrips'] as num?)` (line 71), `pickup['address'] as String?` and `dropoff['address'] as String?` (lines 76-77), and `place(stop)['address'] as String?` (line 84). `_upsert` catches only `on FormatException` (306), so a TypeError escapes. In `_load` the maps were already cleared (233-234) before the loop. The exception reaches the outer `catch (_)` ('Offline: the list stays as it was'), `_emit()` is skipped, and `_offers`/`_nextTrips` are left with only the rows parsed before the bad one. The UI keeps the old list, while `claimOffer`'s `_find` and new subscribers' snapshots use the half-filled maps. In the SSE path the TypeError is thrown out of the `listen` onData callback (only FormatException is caught at 267) to the zone, after `_lastSequence` has already moved past the event, so the event is lost and `_emit` never runs.
failure_scenario: The backend sends one open offer with `riderTrips: "12"` (or a numeric address). Refresh clears the cache, stops at that offer, and never emits: the driver sees stale cards, and Match on one of them returns 'unavailable' because `_find` no longer has it. Over SSE the same offer throws an uncaught error and the feed silently skips that event.
suggested_fix: Catch all errors in `_upsert` (or make `OfferWire.parse` type-check every field and throw FormatException). Build the new maps in locals and swap them in only after the loop.

title: Offer claim, decline and list calls have no timeout, so a stalled connection leaves 'Matching' on screen with no end
description: Unlike `RoadRouteService` (`.timeout(timeout)` at road_route_service.dart:96), `ApiDispatchRepository` calls `_client.post`, `_client.get` and `_client.send` with no timeout, and package:http has no default one. Every caller treats only a thrown error as `networkError`: Home `_claimHomeRadarOffer` (home_offer_radar.dart:541-546), `_claimAdminAssign`, `_claimReservation`, `_claimAssignment`, RideRequests `_claimTrip`, and ScheduledRides `_claim`. A request that hangs (half-open TCP on a mobile network) never resolves. `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId` / `_matchingOfferId` / `claimingId` stay set, the Matching spinner never stops, and no other offer can be matched. This class is the contract adapter meant to replace the demo dispatch.
evidence:
api_dispatch_repository.dart:347-351
        response = await _client.post(
          _uri('/offers/${Uri.encodeComponent(offerId)}/accept'),
          headers: await _headers(mutation: true),
          body: jsonEncode({'expectedVersion': version}),
        );   // no .timeout
ride_requests.dart:322-330  try { result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(trip.id); } catch (_) { result = const ClaimResult.networkError(); }
failure_scenario: With the API adapter installed, the driver taps Match as the phone switches from Wi-Fi to cellular. The POST never completes. The card stays on 'Matching trip…' indefinitely, every other Match is ignored because `_matchingOfferId != null`, and the offer expires server-side unseen.
suggested_fix: Apply a bounded `.timeout(...)` to every request and map TimeoutException to `ClaimResult.networkError()` / false. Keep the same Idempotency-Key for the retry.

title: A journal whose cancellation fields have the wrong type is never quarantined; replay fails forever and blocks every later trip finish and Home recovery
description: `_DecodedJournal.parse` is documented as 'Any type or schema problem throws before a single side effect is applied', and only parse errors are quarantined (lines 150-163). But parse never checks the types of `cancellation.actor` or `cancellation.reasonCode`. `_replay` then casts them: `(data['cancellation'] as Map)['actor'] as String?`, `['reasonCode'] as String?` (199, 202) and `cancellationMap?['reasonCode'] as String?` (216-217). A non-string value throws TypeError outside the quarantine try, so the journal stays stored. Every `finish()` first replays an existing journal (lines 94-96) and throws, so every later completion or cancel fails ('Could not finish saving this trip'). Home's `reconcile()` throws as well, so `_restoreActiveRideIfNeeded` lands in its catch, `_recoveryResolved` stays false and `_goOnline` refuses with 'finish or close saved trip'. This contradicts LOCAL_DATA.md: 'A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers'.
evidence:
completion_journal.dart:150-163  try { entry = _DecodedJournal.parse(raw); } catch (error) { await LocalQuarantine.store(...); ... return JournalReplayOutcome.quarantinedCorrupt; }
:198-203  cancellationActor: data['cancellation'] is Map ? (data['cancellation'] as Map)['actor'] as String? : null,
          cancellationReasonCode: data['cancellation'] is Map ? (data['cancellation'] as Map)['reasonCode'] as String? : null,
:324-331  parse only checks cancellation['actor'] == 'driver' for released statuses
failure_scenario: A stored journal has `"cancellation":{"actor":"driver","reasonCode":7}` (hand-edited localStorage, or a writer bug). On every start Home shows 'Saved trip could not be opened · Retry', Retry fails the same way, and the driver can never go online. Every trip already in progress also fails to finish or cancel.
suggested_fix: Validate the `cancellation` map's field types inside `_DecodedJournal.parse` (so a bad value is quarantined), or wrap the whole of `_replay` so an unexpected decode error quarantines the entry instead of propagating.

title: The trip-save error SnackBar fires again on later state changes, and its Retry does not retry the failed slide
description: `_onPersistenceChanged` is an `ActiveRideController` listener that shows 'Trip progress could not be saved' whenever `persistenceError != null`. `persistenceError` is cleared only at the start of a new `_write`. `_end(clearSnapshot: false)` (active_ride_controller.dart:228-231), which completion, cancel and no-show use, notifies listeners without writing. So an old background-save failure re-shows the error SnackBar while the trip is being finished successfully, and the SnackBar is carried to the next route on the root messenger. Separately, when `transitionTo` (Arrive or Start trip) fails its save, the SnackBar's Retry calls `persistNow()`. That re-saves the current stage, not the stage change. It succeeds silently and leaves the trip where it was, so Retry looks like it did something when it did not.
failure_scenario: A 2-minute GPS snapshot save fails once (web storage quota), and the error SnackBar shows. Later the driver finishes the trip and the journal saves fine, but the Ride completed screen shows 'Trip progress could not be saved · Retry'. Or: the 'Start trip' slide's save fails, the driver taps Retry, nothing visible happens, and the trip is still 'Waiting'.
suggested_fix: Show the SnackBar only on the notify that ends a failed write (track the write revision), clear `persistenceError` in `_end`, and make Retry repeat the failed command rather than calling `persistNow`.

title: A driver cancel or no-show never ends the trip in DriverSessionController, so Home stays 'onTrip' and the driver can never go online again
description: Every other way a trip ends calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (= `endTrip()`): authoritative outcome (line 379), release (402), rider cancel (456/469) and RideCompleted Done (ride_completed.dart:71). `_submitTripCancellation`, which runs for every driver cancel and for the no-show reason (accept_ride_panel.dart:532/1126 -> `_confirmCancellationReason` -> line 1354), never calls it. It journals the cancel, marks the trip terminal, discards the waybill and then `navigator.pop()` (1444-1446) or `pushReplacement(nextRide)` (1441). DriverSessionController keeps `_activeTripId` = the cancelled trip and `_status = onTrip`. Back on Home, `_isOnline` = `availableForOffers` (status == online) is false. `_goOnline` (home.dart:883) gets past every guard, but `beginGoingOnline()` returns early because `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129), and so does `completeGoingOnline()` (status is not goingOnline). Nothing else clears it: `didPopNext` only re-runs recovery when `activeTripId == null` (home.dart:182), and `_islandHold` returns null while `activeTripId != null` (home_account.dart:207). With a secured next trip, B's `beginTrip(B)` is refused because `_activeTripId` is still A (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61), so the session names the wrong trip until B completes.
failure_scenario: The driver goes online, accepts a trip and slides 'Cancel trip' with any reason (or 'Rider no-show' after the wait). The trip screen pops to Home. Home shows the offline dock. Tapping Go online shows the island 'online' message (home.dart:924), but after 1.4 s nothing happens: no radar, no offers, no reservation 'Leave now' (`_canStartScheduled` needs availableForOffers, so accepted rides go to the backup driver). `DrivingTimeClock` keeps counting (isOnline is true for onTrip), so after 12 h the driver is forced to rest without ever having been available. Only logout clears it.
suggested_fix: Call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` in `_submitTripCancellation` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before pushing the next ride or popping, the same way the other terminal exits do. Add a widget test that cancels a trip and asserts `session.activeTripId == null` and `availableForOffers`.

title: Logout resets the dispatch reservations to the seed but not ScheduledRideStore, so a reservation still in Accepted is open and claimable again on Radar
description: Two stores hold the same fact, 'reservation R is taken by this driver': `DemoDispatchRepository._reservations` (claim removes R) and the static `ScheduledRideStore._requests/_accepted` (take/answer moves R to Accepted). `_logout` calls `dispatch.reset()`, which restores `_reservations = Map.of(_seedReservations)` (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:763). `ScheduledRideStore.reset()` exists but is `@visibleForTesting` and is never called on logout (scheduled_rides.dart:706). After 'Return to demo' the new Home's dispatch schedules every reservation to join Radar again (`_ensureDemoSchedule` -> `_scheduleRadarJoin`), while ScheduledRideStore still lists R under Accepted. The Live list shows R: `_rideAllowed` -> `_fitsSchedule` returns true precisely when `ride.id == offer.id` (home_scheduled.dart:307). Match then wins the claim. `ScheduledRideStore.take(trip.id)` (ride_requests.dart:326) is a no-op because R is not in `_requests`, so R stays in Accepted and the smart gap later fires 'Leave now' for the same reservation a second time. The previous session's late cancels (`_lateCancels`, which can pause Scheduled rides) and its rider names and addresses also survive the 'local preview data … cleared' logout.
failure_scenario: The driver accepts the 'Gamla vägen' reservation (Scheduled rides or the Home popup), logs out from Profile, then taps 'Return to demo'. Scheduled rides › Accepted still shows Gamla vägen. 15 min before its pickup it also appears in the Live list as an open reservation trip. Matching it opens the trip now, and at its time 'Leave now' opens the same reservation again as a second trip.
suggested_fix: Make ScheduledRideStore.reset() a production API and call it from `_logout` next to `dispatch.reset()` (and DemoReservations.reset() if the demo should rebook). Alternatively, derive 'open' from one store: the Radar/Live list should drop reservations that ScheduledRideStore lists as accepted.

title: A destination set on the trip screen is lost when the trip returns to Home, but it still counts against today's limit
description: Destination mode lives in three places: Home's `_destinationModeActive/_destinationAddress/_destinationPosition`, AcceptRide's `_destinationActive/...` (copied from the widget at mount, accept_ride.dart:471-473), and the `DestinationModeSession.instance` singleton (daily count, `_activeSince`, route). Setting a destination during a trip (R13-18) calls `OnTripDestination.started()`, which adds one use for today and starts the time limit, and then updates only the trip screen's copy. Nothing writes it back to Home. After completion (popUntil first), a cancel (pop) or a rider cancel, Home still has `_destinationModeActive == false`. It never reads `DestinationModeSession` to restore it and never arms its `_destinationLimitTimer`. The next trip in the chain receives the destination, but Home never does.
failure_scenario: Default rules allow 2 destinations per day. During a trip the driver sets destination 'Solna' from the island. On-trip offers follow it. After the trip ends, Home shows no destination: no route and no on-the-way filtering of Radar offers. If the driver sets it again on Home, that is the second use. A third attempt is refused with 'destinations used today', although only one was ever visible on Home.
suggested_fix: Make DestinationModeSession (or a shared notifier) the single owner of the active destination. Home and AcceptRide should read it and listen to it instead of keeping private copies, and Home should pick up a destination set during the trip when it becomes visible again.

title: The 'offline after missed offers' notice posted during a trip is consumed by the hidden Home island, so the driver never sees it
description: `IslandMessages` is a static queue meant for the Home island. Home subscribes in initState (home.dart:487) and never pauses that listener when another route covers it (`_pauseHomeUpdates` does not touch it). `_showNextIslandMessage` (home_map_sheet.dart:1257) takes the next message as soon as it is posted and starts its display timer. It checks only `mounted`, not `_routeVisible`. When the trip screen (pushed over Home) reaches the missed-Exclusive limit, it calls `setOnline(false)`, which during a trip only records offline-after-trip, and posts `HomeIslandNotices.offlineAfterMissed`. The trip screen's own island never reads IslandMessages, so Home, which is not visible, dequeues the message and drops it after 4.5 s.
failure_scenario: During a trip the driver lets 3 next-trip Exclusive offers run out (the admin default auto-offline count). The session records offline-after-trip, but nothing appears on the trip screen. When the trip ends, Home is offline with no explanation, because the 'went offline after N missed offers' message was shown and expired on the covered Home island minutes earlier.
suggested_fix: Have Home stop taking IslandMessages while `!_liveVisible` and drain the queue on didPopNext, and/or show trip-time notices on the trip island or in a SnackBar on the trip screen.

title: The trip's ride type (and so its waiting terms) is derived from the localized 'matched via' label, so the Scheduled-ride waiting rule applies only in English
description: `WaitingRules.typeOf` decides `WaitingRideType.scheduled` by searching `matchedVia` for 'scheduled' or 'reservation'. Home passes translated strings as matchedVia: 'Leave now' uses `tr.scheduledRide` (home_scheduled.dart:236: en 'Scheduled ride', sv 'Bokad resa', fr 'Course planifiée'), and an Exclusive reservation uses `tr.exclusiveReservation` (home_offer_radar.dart:837: sv 'Exklusiv bokning', fr 'Réservation exclusive', where the é stops 'reservation' from matching). In sv and fr the same reservation trip therefore gets the zone's normal terms instead of the scheduled-ride rule (ScheduledRideRules.includedWaitingMinutes plus any admin scheduled-ride values). A reservation matched from Radar (`tr.moveraRadar`) is 'normal' in every language. The persisted snapshot stores the localized label, so a restore after a language switch can change the type again. With the shipped defaults the free minutes happen to coincide (5/5), so today the visible difference is the waiting sheet's 'Rule for this pickup: Scheduled ride' line, which appears only in English. Any admin scheduled-ride rule would change fees by language.
failure_scenario: A Swedish driver taps 'Leave now' for an accepted reservation. `_waitTerms` = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(type: normal), and the waiting sheet shows no 'Bokad resa' rule. The same trip in English shows 'Rule for this pickup: Scheduled ride'. If admin sets a different included wait or no-show fee for scheduled rides, Swedish and French drivers are charged and paid by the normal rule.
suggested_fix: Pass the trip kind explicitly (e.g. `reservation: offer.reservation` / a WaitingRideType field on AcceptRide and PersistedActiveRide) and keep matchedVia as a stable code that is localized only for display.

title: Trips hidden with × in the Live list come back immediately when the list is reopened (hidden state is destroyed with the widget)
description: Q17 says a trip hidden with × comes back only after `hiddenComesBackAfter` (2 min by default), and only if it is still open. The hidden set `_dismissed` and its `_comeBackTimers` live in `_RideRequestsState`. Home mounts RideRequests only while `showRideRequests` is true (home.dart:717/746) and unmounts it when the driver closes the list. Reopening creates a fresh state with an empty `_dismissed` and a new first dispatch snapshot, so every hidden trip is listed again at once. The widget test for Q17 never closes and reopens the list, so it cannot catch this.
failure_scenario: The driver hides 'Hantverkargatan → Bandhagen' with × in the Live list, closes the list and taps the radar orb again 10 s later. The hidden trip is back at the top with Match enabled, instead of staying away for the admin's 2 minutes.
suggested_fix: Keep the hidden-until deadlines outside the widget (on Home's state or a small static store keyed by offer id with its come-back time), and apply them when the list is rebuilt.

title: Logout keeps the previous session's offer and work counters (missed-Exclusive row, Cash switch, driving time) in static singletons
description: `_logout` resets traffic, language, waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and the session, but not the other app-lifetime singletons that hold per-driver state: `ExclusiveAnswers.instance._missedInRow` and `DriverOfferPreferences.acceptsCash` (offer_rules.dart:215-256, where reset() exists but is @visibleForTesting only) and `DrivingTimeClock.instance` (worked time banked, reset() never called). After 'Return to demo' the new session inherits them. This is distinct from the already reported category filter: it covers the auto-offline row, the cash filter and the rest rule.
failure_scenario: Driver A misses 2 Exclusive offers (limit 3), switches Cash off and works 11 h 50 min, then logs out. The next session after 'Return to demo' goes offline on its first missed Exclusive offer, never receives cash trips (the Cash switch shows off without the driver choosing it), and is told to rest after 10 minutes online.
suggested_fix: Reset ExclusiveAnswers, DriverOfferPreferences and DrivingTimeClock (and the other per-driver singletons) in `_logout`, or move them onto an object owned by the composition root that is recreated per session.

title: Pages deploy trusts workflow_run.head_branch == 'main', so a fork pull request from a branch named main gets built with secrets and deployed to the production Pages site
description: deploy-pages.yml runs on `workflow_run` after any completed 'Drider CI' run. Drider CI also runs on `pull_request`, including pull requests from forks. The build job's only check is `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'`. For a fork pull request, head_branch is the fork's branch name, so a fork whose branch is called `main` passes the check. The job then checks out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, which is the fork's commit (GitHub can fetch it through refs/pull). It runs `flutter pub get` and `flutter build web` on that attacker-controlled tree, with `secrets.newmap131189` in the environment and a job token that has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`. `deploy-pages@v4` then publishes the result. A workflow_run event runs in the default-branch context, so the github-pages environment's default-branch rule does not stop it. Nothing checks `workflow_run.event == 'push'` or `workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository`. The concurrency key (`pages-${{ ... github.event.workflow_run.head_branch ... }}`, line 21) also puts that fork run into the `pages-main` group, where `cancel-in-progress: true` lets it cancel a real main deployment.
evidence:
deploy-pages.yml:3-8 `on: workflow_run: workflows: [Drider CI] types: [completed]`
deploy-pages.yml:26-33 `if: ... github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'`
deploy-pages.yml:39 `ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}`
deploy-pages.yml:53 `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.newmap131189 }}`
deploy-pages.yml:11-14 `pages: write`, `id-token: write` (workflow level, so the build job has them too)
drider-ci.yml:9-12 `pull_request: branches: [main, 'audit/phase-*']`
failure_scenario: An outside contributor forks the repository and opens a pull request from their fork's `main` branch, changing web/index.html or lib/ to show a phishing page. If CI runs without approval and passes, deploy-pages builds the fork's head_sha with the maps secret and publishes it to the official Movera Driver Pages URL. Any running main deployment in the `pages-main` concurrency group is cancelled.
suggested_fix: Also require `github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push'` and `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository` in the `if:` and in the concurrency key. Move `pages`/`id-token` permissions to the deploy job only.

title: iOS bundle identifier is still the template com.example.movera, while README and the 16-point record say the bundle id is se.movera.driver
description: Android uses applicationId/namespace `se.movera.driver`. README.md:7 says 'Bundle id `se.movera.driver` is unchanged', and FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md (F04/F15) says the application and bundle id were kept. The Runner target's Debug, Release and Profile configurations all set PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER to the Flutter template value `com.example.movera`, and RunnerTests uses `com.example.movera.RunnerTests`. Flutter's own `build ipa` validation flags this ('Your application still contains the default "com.example" bundle identifier'). Apple does not register App IDs under the reserved example domain, so the iOS release cannot be signed or uploaded under the intended identity. The `ios-release-preflight` job uses `--no-codesign` and never sees this. release_metadata_test.dart checks only the Android gradle file for 'se.movera.driver', so the mismatch passes CI.
evidence:
ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:371 `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.example.movera;` (also :550, :572; RunnerTests :387, :404, :419)
android/app/build.gradle.kts:9,23 `namespace = "se.movera.driver"` / `applicationId = "se.movera.driver"`
README.md:7 `Bundle id \`se.movera.driver\` is unchanged.`
test/audit/release_metadata_test.dart:29-32 checks only android/app/build.gradle.kts for 'se.movera.driver'
failure_scenario: The owner archives the iOS release for TestFlight or the App Store. Signing fails because the com.example.movera App ID cannot be registered, or a build goes out under a throwaway identifier that does not match the Android/README identity, so later updates cannot carry over to the real se.movera.driver listing.
suggested_fix: Set PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER to se.movera.driver (RunnerTests: se.movera.driver.RunnerTests) in all three configurations. Extend release_metadata_test to assert it in project.pbxproj.

title: Device-to-device transfer rules leave the 'root' domain (app_flutter) included, so Ride-check audio recordings move to a new phone despite 'saved only on this phone'
description: For apps targeting Android 12+ (targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion = 36), `android:allowBackup="false"` no longer turns off device-to-device migration. Only the `<device-transfer>` rules control it. Those rules exclude only `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` (getFilesDir()). NativeRideCheckRecorder writes recordings to `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `PathUtils.getDataDirectory` = `context.getDir("flutter")`, that is /data/data/se.movera.driver/app_flutter. That directory is in the `root` domain, which is not excluded. The recordings are therefore copied to a new device during setup. That contradicts the XML comment ('Driver data ... is excluded from cloud backup and device-to-device transfer'), the RECORD_AUDIO rationale in docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md ('saved only on this phone and never sent'), and the Ride-check UI copy. privacy_storage_test only checks that a `<device-transfer>` tag exists, so it cannot catch this. (The iOS Documents backup issue is already known; this is the Android counterpart, a different mechanism.)
evidence:
data_extraction_rules.xml:10-14 `<device-transfer> <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." /> <exclude domain="database" path="." /> <exclude domain="file" path="." /> </device-transfer>` (no `root`)
lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 `'${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio'` ... `path: '${directory.path}/$recordingId.m4a'`
path_provider_android PathProviderPlugin.getApplicationDocumentsPath -> `PathUtils.getDataDirectory(context)` -> `applicationContext.getDir("flutter", MODE_PRIVATE)`
test/audit/privacy_storage_test.dart:60-62 only `contains('<device-transfer>')`
failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check on an Android 12+ phone, then sets up a new phone with Google's 'copy apps & data' cable or wireless transfer. The rider-incident recordings in app_flutter/ride_check_audio/*.m4a are copied to the new device, although the app promised they stay only on the original phone.
suggested_fix: Add `<exclude domain="root" path="." />` (and `external`) to both `<device-transfer>` and `<cloud-backup>`, or store recordings under noBackupFilesDir. Make the test assert the domains.

title: Approximate-only location (Android 'Approximate', iOS 'Precise: Off') passes the permission check, but every fix is then rejected as >50 m, so Home never gets GPS and arrival is impossible in release builds, with a message telling the driver to enable location
description: The manifest declares both ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, and geolocator requests both. On Android 12+ the system dialog therefore offers 'Approximate'. geolocator_android.checkPermissionStatus returns `whileInUse` when either declared permission is granted, coarse alone included. iOS 14+ similarly lets the user turn Precise off, and the status stays whenInUse. `_ensurePermission` checks only denied/deniedForever, so it passes. The fixes then have accuracy of about 1–3 km. `DriverLocation.isUsableAt` rejects anything with `accuracy > 50`, so Home sets `_hasLiveDriverLocation = false` on every fix, the trip never follows the car, and `_nearArrivalTarget` returns false in every release build (simulatedArrival is false there). The code never calls `Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy()` or `requestTemporaryFullAccuracy`, and Info.plist has no `NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary`, so the reduced-accuracy state is never detected or explained. docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md says ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION is kept as a 'Coarse fallback for the same when-in-use location', but the code cannot use a coarse fix at all.
evidence:
driver_location_service.dart:115-128 only checks `LocationPermission.denied` / `deniedForever`
driver_location_repository.dart:48-55 `accuracy > 50) { return false; }`
home_map_sheet.dart:93 `_hasLiveDriverLocation = location.isUsableAt(DateTime.now());`
accept_ride.dart:765-768 `if (_arrivalDemo) { return true; } if (!_hasLiveLocation || _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(DateTime.now()) != true) { return false; }`
AndroidManifest.xml:4-5 FINE + COARSE; docs/ANDROID_PERMISSIONS.md 'ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION | Coarse fallback for the same when-in-use location'
geolocator_android PermissionManager.checkPermissionStatus: any granted declared permission -> whileInUse
failure_scenario: On an Android 13 phone the driver taps 'Approximate' in the location dialog (or turns 'Precise Location' off on iOS). Home stays on 'Finding your location' with no car marker. On an accepted trip, tapping Arrived at the pickup shows 'Location unavailable. Enable location to confirm arrival.' although location is enabled. The trip cannot progress in a release APK/IPA or the CI web release.
suggested_fix: After the permission check, call Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy(). On reduced accuracy, show a 'Precise location required' state with a settings link. On iOS, add NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary and call requestTemporaryFullAccuracy. Alternatively drop COARSE from the manifest and fix the doc.

title: An iOS build without GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY skips GMSServices.provideAPIKey, so the first Google map crashes; unlike Android there is no fail-closed release gate, and the docs claim one for every native release
description: Info.plist sets `GoogleMapsApiKey` to `$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)`. No xcconfig or CI step defines that setting, so in the CI preflight and any local build without the env var it expands to empty. AppDelegate then deliberately skips `GMSServices.provideAPIKey`. The Google Maps SDK for iOS throws an uncaught GMSServicesException ('must be initialized via [GMSServices provideAPIKey:...] prior to use') when the first GMSMapView is created. That happens when Home's map mounts, so the app crashes rather than showing a blank map as Android does. Android has a `MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY` gate and a CI step that proves it, and FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md F04 says '`MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY=true` fails a native release when `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` is blank'. iOS has no such check: `ios-release-preflight` builds a keyless release and reports success.
evidence:
ios/Runner/Info.plist:5-6 `<key>GoogleMapsApiKey</key><string>$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)</string>`
AppDelegate.swift:11-15 `if let mapsKey = ..., !mapsKey.isEmpty, mapsKey != "$(GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)" { GMSServices.provideAPIKey(mapsKey) }`
drider-ci.yml:148-149 `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` (no key, no MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY check)
android/app/build.gradle.kts:85-91 Android-only `MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY` gate
docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md:49 'fails a native release when GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is blank'
failure_scenario: The owner archives an iOS release from a shell where GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is not exported (as in CI). The archive succeeds. On device, the driver signs in, Home mounts the GoogleMap, and the app terminates with GMSServicesException. CI stayed green because nothing checks the key for iOS.
suggested_fix: Add an iOS Run Script build phase (or a CI step) that fails a Release build when MOVERA_REQUIRE_MAPS_KEY=true and GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is empty. Have it exercised in ios-release-preflight like the Android step, and narrow the docs claim until then.

title: Info.plist has no NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription (or NSAppleMusicUsageDescription) although the linked image_picker and file_picker reference those APIs; a test asserts the key stays absent
description: image_picker's README (pubspec image_picker 1.2.0) says NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription must be in Info.plist even if the photo library is never requested: 'This permission will not be requested if you always pass false for requestFullMetadata, but App Store policy requires including the plist entry.' file_picker 10.3.2's iOS podspec builds by default with PICKER_MEDIA (DKImagePickerController/PhotoGallery, Photos framework) and PICKER_AUDIO (MPMediaPickerController, which needs NSAppleMusicUsageDescription). No Podfile sets `Pod::PICKER_MEDIA=false` or `PICKER_AUDIO=false`. App Store Connect's static scan rejects uploads that reference these APIs without the purpose strings (ITMS-90683). ios_camera_privacy_test.dart explicitly asserts the plist does NOT contain NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, which locks the defect in.
evidence:
ios/Runner/Info.plist:7-12 only NSCamera/NSMicrophone/NSLocationWhenInUse keys
pubspec.yaml:47-48 `image_picker: ^1.2.0`, `file_picker: ^10.3.1`
file_picker-10.3.2/ios/file_picker.podspec: `if !Pod.const_defined?(:PICKER_MEDIA) || PICKER_MEDIA ... s.dependency 'DKImagePickerController/PhotoGallery'`; `PICKER_AUDIO=1`
image_picker README: 'App Store policy requires including the plist entry'
test/audit/ios_camera_privacy_test.dart:33 `expect(plist, isNot(contains('NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription')));`
failure_scenario: The owner uploads the iOS archive to App Store Connect. Processing returns ITMS-90683 'Missing purpose string in Info.plist' for NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription (and NSAppleMusicUsageDescription), and the build cannot be submitted. Adding the key makes the audit test fail.
suggested_fix: Either add accurate NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription/NSAppleMusicUsageDescription strings, or add an ios/Podfile with `Pod::PICKER_MEDIA = false` and `Pod::PICKER_AUDIO = false` for file_picker and pass requestFullMetadata: false. Update ios_camera_privacy_test to match.

title: Ride-check audio stops capturing when the app is backgrounded (no iOS background audio mode, no Android microphone foreground service), but the counter and the saved length keep counting wall-clock time
description: The Ride-check main step offers 'Call 112' and 'Record audio' side by side. Tapping Call 112 hands off to the dialer, which backgrounds the app; so does locking the screen. Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes `audio`, so iOS suspends the app and the record session stops or is interrupted. Android 9+ gives silence to apps in the background, and the manifest has no microphone-type foreground service. AcceptRide.didChangeAppLifecycleState (accept_ride.dart:715-727) persists the trip and pauses GPS but does nothing about the recording. The controller computes `audioSeconds` as `now - _audioStartedAt`. When the driver comes back and taps stop, that wall-clock duration is shown ('Audio saved 3:12') and written to the Ride-check record (`copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds)`), although the file holds only the foreground part or silence.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:90-92 `int get audioSeconds => _audio == RideCheckAudio.recording ? services.now().difference(_audioStartedAt!).inSeconds : ...`
ride_check_controller.dart:277-287 `final seconds = audioSeconds; ... _record = _record?.copyWith(audioSeconds: seconds);`
ride_check_card.dart:491-495 Call 112 and :512 `_RecordAudio` on the same main step
accept_ride.dart:720-726 paused/hidden only `persistNow()` + `_pauseLiveUpdates()`
ios/Runner/Info.plist: no UIBackgroundModes; AndroidManifest.xml: no FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE / service
failure_scenario: During a frightening ride the driver taps Record audio, then Call 112 (or locks the phone). After 3 minutes they return and stop the recording. The card says 'Audio saved 3:12' and the trip detail stores 192 s, but the .m4a holds about 5 s (iOS) or 3 minutes of silence (Android). That evidence is missing when it matters.
suggested_fix: Stop (or pause and mark) the recording on paused/hidden and tell the driver. Take the saved duration from the file or the recorder's own amplitude/duration, not the wall clock. If background capture is wanted, add UIBackgroundModes audio and an Android microphone foreground service, with product and store sign-off.

title: The 'Keep trip' tests still pass if Keep trip actually ends the trip, because AcceptRide is the root route
description: Two tests claim to prove that dismissing the cancel confirmation with 'Keep trip' leaves the trip running: the CI 'Critical lifecycle' test 'driver cancel reason can be dismissed without ending the trip' and widget_test.dart:2617 'On-trip options allow safe early cancellation with reasons'. Both mount `MaterialApp(home: AcceptRide(...))`, so AcceptRide is the only route. When a driver cancel really completes, `_submitTripCancellation` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1439-1446) only pops `if (navigator.canPop())`, and canPop is false here, so the trip screen stays mounted. The stage marker `ValueKey('active-ride-panel-${_stage.name}')` (accept_ride_panel.dart:687) still reads `onTrip` after `cancel(clearSnapshot:false)`, because a terminal outcome is kept apart from the stage. Nothing in the build depends on `terminal`. AcceptRide never pushes DriverHome, so `find.byType(DriverHome), findsNothing` holds whatever happens. Each assertion passes whether the trip continued or was cancelled.
evidence:
integration_test/driver_lifecycle_test.dart:178 `await tester.pumpWidget(const MaterialApp(home: AcceptRide(locationRepository: _ScriptedLocation())));` ... :200-203 `await tester.tap(find.text('Keep trip')); ... expect(find.byType(AcceptRide), findsOneWidget); expect(find.byType(DriverHome), findsNothing);`
test/widget_test.dart:2622 `await tester.pumpWidget(const MaterialApp(home: AcceptRide()));` :2675-2681 `await tester.tap(find.text('Keep trip')); ... expect(find.byKey(const ValueKey<String>('active-ride-panel-onTrip')), findsOneWidget);`
lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride_trip.dart:1444 `if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }`
lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride_trip.dart:1328 `onPressed: () => popOwned(sheetContext, false),` (Keep trip)
failure_scenario: Regression: change the Keep trip button at accept_ride_trip.dart:1328 to `popOwned(sheetContext, true)`, or drop the `confirmed != true` check at :1349. Tapping 'Keep trip' would then journal the trip as cancelled_by_driver, mark it terminal and show 'Trip ended early'. Both tests stay green: AcceptRide is still found, the onTrip marker is still found and DriverHome is never built. CI's lifecycle gate would ship a build where 'Keep trip' ends the rider's trip. Verified by reading the code; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Push AcceptRide over a stand-in Home route, as rider_cancel_returns_home_test does. After Keep trip, assert that the trip is still not terminal: no history row in PrefsTripHistoryRepository, the active snapshot is still present and the 'Trip ended early' SnackBar is absent.

title: D-05 'counts down the rest after resume' passes even if resume gives the offer its full lifetime again
description: The test says an on-trip Exclusive offer that is hidden and then shown again 'counts down the rest' (it resumes with the time it had left). It hides for 2 s, shows, pumps 300 ms, then pumps the full `exclusiveAcceptTime` and expects the offer gone. Suppose resume restarted a fresh full lifetime. The new timer would fire at resume + L, and the test has pumped to resume + 0.3 s + L by then, so the offer still disappears and still counts as a miss. The test never checks that the offer is gone before a full lifetime has passed since resume, so it cannot tell the remaining time from a fresh full window. This is the D-05/D-04 'time left, not a fresh window' rule.
evidence:
test/audit/offers_lifecycle_test.dart:230-238 `_hide(tester); await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 2)); _show(tester); await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 300)); expect(find.byKey(_offerCard), findsOneWidget); await _pumpFor(tester, DriverOfferRules.current.exclusiveAcceptTime); expect(find.byKey(_offerCard), findsNothing); expect(ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missedInRow, 1);`
lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride_trip.dart:161-165 `final deadline = _nextTripOfferDeadline; final left = deadline?.difference(_offerNow()); if (left != null && left > Duration.zero) { _armOnTripOfferExpiry(left: left); return; }`
failure_scenario: Regression: change accept_ride_trip.dart:164 to `_armOnTripOfferExpiry();`, which resets to the full lifetime and writes a new deadline. Every background/foreground cycle would then give the offer a fresh 15 s, so a driver who keeps switching apps keeps the offer alive indefinitely. All three D-05 tests still pass. Worked by hand with lifetime L = 15 s: the regressed timer fires at resume + 15 s and the test checks at resume + 15.3 s. No tests were run.
suggested_fix: After resume, pump only (L − 2 s − 0.3 s + a small margin) and expect the offer to be gone. A fresh-window implementation would still be showing it at that point.

title: D-04 'a pause before the end keeps the window' cannot fail: the Home deadline uses the real wall clock and the test pumps a full window after resume
description: Home's Radar pick window stores a deadline from `DateTime.now()` (home_offer_radar.dart:429-432). In a widget test that is the real wall clock, not the test's fake clock, so the 300 ms fake-time pause and all the earlier fake time cost almost nothing off the window. The test then pumps `radarTime + 1 s` after resume and expects Match to be disabled. That is true whether the deadline survived the pause or a fresh full window was started at resume. The test is named for D-04 (keep one deadline across pause/resume) but would pass with that rule removed.
evidence:
test/audit/offers_lifecycle_test.dart:164-170 `tester.binding.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(AppLifecycleState.inactive); await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 300)); ...resumed...; expect(enabled(), isTrue); await tester.pump(DriverOfferRules.current.radarTime); await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1)); expect(enabled(), isFalse);`
lib/presentation/driver/home/home_offer_radar.dart:429-432 `final now = DateTime.now(); final deadline = _radarOfferDeadlines.putIfAbsent(offer.id, () => now.add(_DriverHomeState._radarOfferPickWindow)); final left = deadline.difference(now);`
lib/presentation/driver/home/home_offer_radar.dart:805-810 `// D-04: a pause (preserveClaim) keeps each pick window's deadline ... if (!preserveClaim) { _radarOfferExpired.clear(); _radarOfferDeadlines.clear(); }`
failure_scenario: Regression: in `_cancelAllOfferTimers`, move `_radarOfferDeadlines.clear()` out of the `if (!preserveClaim)` block. Every pause/resume (notification shade, app switch) would then hand each Radar card a fresh 15 s pick window. 'a pause before the end keeps the window, then it ends' still passes, because 15 s + 1 s after resume is past the regressed window too. 'an expired Radar offer stays expired' still passes, because `_radarOfferExpired` is untouched. Verified by reading the code; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Inject a clock into Home's pick-window deadline (as AcceptRide does with waitNow) so fake time counts. Pause for a large part of the window, then assert Match fades after the remaining time, well before a full window has passed since resume.

title: 'Routing failure keeps the driver on the active trip' never runs the failing route repository
description: The test injects `_FailingRouteRepository`, which throws on `drivingRoute`. But flutter_test_config.dart sets `externalRouting: false` for every test, and `_refreshRoadRoute` returns before reaching `_navigation.ensureRoute` when external routing is off. That is the only call that would hit the repository. The failure path the test is named after is never exercised. Its assertions (AcceptRide present, headingToPickup marker, guidance island present) hold with any route repository, or none.
evidence:
test/flutter_test_config.dart:23-25 `const testRuntimeConfig = DriverRuntimeConfig(simulatedArrival: true, externalRouting: false, ...`
test/widget_test.dart:3108-3110 `await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: AcceptRide(routeRepository: _FailingRouteRepository())));`
lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride_trip.dart:690-692 `Future<void> _refreshRoadRoute({bool force = false}) async { ... if (!_allowExternalRouting) { return; }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:704 is the only `ensureRoute` call in the trip screen.
failure_scenario: Regression: make NavigationController.ensureRoute rethrow in its catch block, or make `_refreshRoadRoute` pop the trip when routing fails. Offline drivers would then lose the trip or hit an uncaught async error, and the test stays green because the repository is never called. Verified by reading the code; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Set `DriverRuntimeConfig.current` with `externalRouting: true` inside this test (restore it in tearDown). Feed a location so `_refreshRoadRoute` runs. Assert the repository was called and the trip is still active with the 'route unavailable' status.

title: Backup-exclusion test only checks that tags exist; the real rules leave ride-check audio (root domain) in device-to-device transfer
description: The test 'Android excludes app data from backup and device transfer' only asserts that `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>` are present. It never checks what they exclude. The rules exclude the `sharedpref`, `database` and `file` domains only. Ride-check audio is written under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, which on Android is `context.getDir("flutter")`, i.e. `<dataDir>/app_flutter`. That is in the `root` domain, not `file`. For apps targeting Android 12+, `allowBackup="false"` does not stop device-to-device migration, so the recordings leave the phone when the driver moves to a new device. The rules file's own comment says driver data stays on this device, and the ride-check UI says the recording is saved only on this phone. The test cannot catch this, or any rule that includes data.
evidence:
test/audit/privacy_storage_test.dart:61-63 `final rules = File('android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml').readAsStringSync(); expect(rules, contains('<cloud-backup>')); expect(rules, contains('<device-transfer>'));`
android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml: `<device-transfer> <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." /> <exclude domain="database" path="." /> <exclude domain="file" path="." /> </device-transfer>` (no `root`)
lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-32 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio');`
failure_scenario: A driver records audio in a Ride check, then sets up a new Android phone with device transfer. The .m4a files under app_flutter/ride_check_audio are copied to the new device. A rules file containing `<include domain="root" path="."/>` would also pass this test. Worked from the Android backup-domain rules and path_provider_android behaviour; nothing was run.
suggested_fix: Add `<exclude domain="root" path="."/>` to cloud-backup, device-transfer and full-backup-content (or store recordings under getFilesDir). Make the test parse the XML and assert every domain the app writes to is excluded in both sections.

title: home_scheduled_test's shared _end helper discards any exception from all 9 scheduled-ride flow tests; offer_rules_flow_test does the same 7 times
description: Every test in home_scheduled_test.dart ends with `await _end(tester)`, which calls `tester.takeException()` and ignores the result. None of these tests asserts `takeException() isNull`. In flutter_test, takeException clears the pending error, and with it the 'multiple exceptions' failure, so overflows, setState-after-dispose or assertion errors during 'Leave now', the backup-driver handoff, assigned-ride claims and Exclusive reservations can never fail these tests. offer_rules_flow_test.dart does the same in 7 tests, including the cash 'Collect cash → Finish' completion path (line 484), as do reservation_near_pickup_test (5) and radar_offer_gone_test (3). These sites are separate from the already-reported account_flow_test.
evidence:
test/widget/home_scheduled_test.dart:164-167 `Future<void> _end(WidgetTester tester) async { tester.takeException(); await tester.pumpWidget(const SizedBox()); }` (called at :211, :233, :251, :299, :356, :368, :394, :426, :455)
test/widget/offer_rules_flow_test.dart:483-484 `expect(find.byType(DriverRideCompleted), findsOneWidget); tester.takeException();`
failure_scenario: Regression: a 'Leave now' push that calls setState on a disposed Home, or a reservation sheet overflow, throws a FlutterError during the test. `_end` swallows it and the test passes. Verified by reading the flutter_test takeException semantics; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Replace the bare calls with `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)`. Where an exception is truly expected, assert its type.

title: 'clear wins over an in-flight save' awaits the save first, so there is never an in-flight save
description: The test is named for the race where a clear() issued while a save() is still running must win, so a cancelled trip cannot come back. It does `await store.save(...)` and only then `await store.clear()`, which is fully sequential. Any repository that removes the key passes, including one with no write queue at all. The ordering is actually provided by the static `_enqueue` queue in PrefsActiveRideRepository, and this test does not exercise it.
evidence:
test/core/active_ride_persistence_test.dart:134-144 `await store.save(const PersistedActiveRide(tripId: 'trip-cancel', stage: ActiveRideStage.headingToPickup)); await store.clear(); expect(await store.read(), isNull);`
lib/core/ride/prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:46-64 `Future<T> _enqueue<T>(Future<T> Function() operation) { final previous = _pending; ... previous.then((_) => operation()) ...`
failure_scenario: Regression: make `clear()` call its body directly instead of through `_enqueue`. A clear issued while a GPS-snapshot save is still awaiting `_load()` could then run first, and the save would write the cancelled trip back. Home would then offer to restore the cancelled trip. This test stays green because the save already finished before clear started. Verified by reading the code; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Gate `_load` with a Completer (as the next test does). Start `save()` without awaiting it, call `clear()`, release the gate, and assert `read()` is null.

title: 'rounds to öre' uses only values where rounding and truncating agree
description: The test is meant to guard pickup-pay rounding to öre. Its inputs are 1.234 km × 3 kr = 370.2 öre and 2.1 × 2.5 + 7 × 0.8 = 1085.0000000000002 öre, and both give the same result with `.floor()` and `.round()`. The other expectations in the file land on whole öre too. With the code's `+ 1e-6` epsilon, `floor(kronor*100 + 1e-6)` reproduces every expected string in the file. A switch to truncation, which underpays the driver by up to 1 öre per offer, goes unnoticed.
evidence:
test/core/pickup_pay_test.dart:71-75 `test('rounds to öre', () { expect(_pay(_config(), km: 1.234, minutes: 0), '3,70 kr'); ... expect(_pay(_config(rate: rate), km: 2.1, minutes: 7), '10,85 kr'); });`
lib/core/dispatch/pickup_pay.dart:81 `final ore = (kronor * 100 + 1e-6).round();`
failure_scenario: Regression: change pickup_pay.dart:81 to `.floor()`. A 1.235 km leg at 3 kr/km gives 370.5 öre, which should show 3,71 kr but would show 3,70 kr, and every test still passes. Worked by hand; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Add a case whose öre value has a fractional part of .5 or more, e.g. km: 1.235, minutes: 0 → '3,71 kr', and one just below .5.

title: Regression guards assert findsNothing on keys no code builds ('radar-reserve-icon', 'home-reservation-barrier', 'radar-home-refresh', 'island-radar')
description: Several assertions check that UI is absent by looking for a ValueKey that appears nowhere in lib/, so they pass whatever the widget tree contains. The clearest case: 'the normal Radar-offer orb ... no icon' checks `radar-reserve-icon` findsNothing. The orb's only icon carries the key `radar-exclusive-icon` and appears when `tinted` (`exclusive && !reserve`) is true. If an icon were added to the reservation orb, it would carry that key, and this assertion would not see it. The same holds for 'home-reservation-barrier' ('no map is dimmed', no Home code has such a key), 'radar-home-refresh' (radar_offer_gone_test.dart:173, the real refresh pill key is 'radar-refresh-new') and 'island-radar' (adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:291).
evidence:
test/widget/reservation_request_popup_test.dart:575-576 `expect(find.byKey(const ValueKey<String>('radar-reserve-icon')), findsNothing);` and :557 `expect(find.byKey(const ValueKey<String>('home-reservation-barrier')), findsNothing);`
lib/widgets/movera_radar_orb.dart:124 `final tinted = exclusive && !reserve;` :345-349 `if (tinted) ...[ SvgPicture.asset(AppAssets.solarCheckCircle, key: const ValueKey<String>('radar-exclusive-icon'),`
`grep -rn "radar-reserve-icon\|home-reservation-barrier\|radar-home-refresh\|island-radar'" lib` → no hits.
failure_scenario: Regression: change movera_radar_orb.dart:124 to `final tinted = exclusive || reserve;`. The reservation orb on Home then shows the white check icon (and the Exclusive spacing), and reservation_request_popup_test still passes. Verified by grep and by reading the code; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Assert absence with the key the real widget would carry (e.g. `radar-exclusive-icon` scoped to the reservation orb, `radar-refresh-new`), or with a type/predicate finder (ModalBarrier, SvgPicture inside the orb).

title: 'arrival action remains wired' is satisfied by a doc comment, not by the arrival button
description: The source-grep test checks `rideSource.contains("I've arrived")` across accept_ride.dart, accept_ride_trip.dart and accept_ride_panel.dart. The button label now comes from `driverText(DriverTexts.tripArrived)`. The only occurrence of the literal is a doc comment on `_rideMiddleTotal` (accept_ride_panel.dart:93). This clause therefore stays true even if the arrived button and its label are removed from the panel.
evidence:
test/core/driver_realtime_test.dart:212 `expect(rideSource.contains("I've arrived"), isTrue);`
lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/accept_ride_panel.dart:93 `/// Middle sheet height: down to the stage's main action (I've arrived,`
accept_ride_panel.dart:900 `driverText(DriverTexts.tripArrived),`
