failure_scenario: Regression: delete the `if (arrival) { ... FilledButton(key: 'active-ride-arrived-button' ...) }` branch from `_buildPrimaryAction`. This clause still passes because the comment remains (the other clauses check only identifier names). Verified by grep; no tests were run.
suggested_fix: Drop the literal check, or replace it with a widget assertion that `active-ride-arrived-button` shows the localized tripArrived text.

title: Scheduled-ride waiting rule is matched against a translated label, so in Swedish and French a reservation gets the wrong free wait, waiting fee and no-show time
description: AcceptRide works out its waiting terms with `WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)` (accept_ride.dart:989-996). typeOf looks for the English words `scheduled`/`reservation` in matchedVia. Home passes a translated string as matchedVia: 'Leave now' on a scheduled ride calls `_openOfferTrip(..., tr.scheduledRide)` (home_scheduled.dart:234-237), and an Exclusive reservation passes `tr.exclusiveReservation` (home_offer_radar.dart:835-838). In sv these are 'Bokad resa' and 'Exklusiv bokning'. In fr they are 'Course planifiée' and 'Réservation exclusive' ('réservation' does not contain 'reservation'). None of them match, so the trip is typed `WaitingRideType.normal` and the scheduled rule (free minutes = ScheduledRideRules.includedWaitingMinutes, the 'Scheduled ride' rule label) is skipped. English works because 'Scheduled ride' contains 'scheduled'. Swedish is the default language for the SE market.
failure_scenario: An XL reservation started with 'Leave now' while the app is in Swedish. XL rule: free 3, no-show 3. English gets the scheduled rule: free 5 (includedWaitingMinutes), no-show raised to 5. Swedish gets typeOf -> normal, so free 3 and no-show 3. The paid wait starts 2 minutes earlier (2 x 12,26 kr = 24,52 kr more on the fare and the waybill), and the 'Rider didn't show' button appears at 3:00 instead of 5:00. The same booking costs a different amount depending on the phone's language. Worked by hand from waiting_rules.dart:194-238.
evidence:
waiting_rules.dart:250-252: `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled; }`
home_scheduled.dart:234-237: `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide,);`
home_offer_radar.dart:836-837: `offer.reservation ? tr.exclusiveReservation : tr.exclusiveOffer,`
app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`, app_sv.arb:90 `"exclusiveReservation": "Exklusiv bokning"`
accept_ride.dart:989-996: `_waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: widget.category, type: WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...), pickupKm: widget.pickupKm);`
suggested_fix: Pass a language-neutral source id (for example WaybillRecord-style stored constants or a WaitingRideType) into AcceptRide and persist that. Translate only when displaying it.

title: Waybill takes Movera's 25% fee on the waiting fee, although the app tells the driver the waiting fee is 100% theirs, and lists it as 'Base price'
description: At completion `_paidWaybill()` folds the driver's waiting fee into the waybill fare (`fare: _fareWithWaiting`, accept_ride_trip.dart:72-80, 912-913). The completed-trip waybill (`showMoveraWaybillSheet` from DriverRideCompleted) runs `WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)`. It takes the service fee on `_riderOre = fare - bonus`, which now includes the waiting fee. The Movera bonus is deliberately kept out of the commission; the waiting fee is not. So 'Your earnings' keeps only 75% of the waiting money. Meanwhile the waiting sheet says 'You get 100% of the wait time' (driverShareWaitPercent = 100), the completion screen says 'Includes X waiting fee', and the code comments say 'Q43: the waiting fee is the driver's, in the trip's earnings'. The same sheet also shows the waiting fee inside 'Base price · <service>' and 'Paid by the passenger'. 'Paid by the passenger' is the driver's share, not the rider's full fee, when the share is below 100%.
failure_scenario: Card trip, fare '100,00 kr', 6:30 at pickup (90 paid seconds, 18,39 kr). Waybill fare is '118,39 kr'. fromFare: fee = round(11839 x 0.25) = 2960, shown as 'Movera fee −29,60 kr' and 'Your earnings 88,79 kr'. Without the wait the earnings are 75,00 kr, so the driver keeps 13,79 kr of the 18,39 kr waiting fee the app promised in full. 'Base price · Movera' reads 118,39 kr, although the base price was 100,00 kr. Worked by hand.
evidence:
waybill.dart:317-326: `int get _riderOre => _fareOre - _bonusOre; int get _feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round(); ... String get earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:72-80: `String get _fareWithWaiting => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.fare, _waitTerms.driverWaitingFee(_paidWaitTotal)); ... copyWith(fare: _fareWithWaiting, waitingFee: ...)`
waybill_sheet.dart:89-94: `_Row(tr.paidByPassenger, payment.fare), ... _Row(tr.basePriceService(record.service), payment.fare), _Row(tr.moveraFee, '−${payment.serviceFee}'), ... _Row(tr.yourEarnings, payment.earnings)`
waiting_time_sheet.dart:251: `tr.youGetDriverShareWaitPercent(terms.driverShareWaitPercent)` ('You get 100% of the wait time.')
suggested_fix: Pass the waiting fee to WaybillPayment as its own amount, the way the bonus is passed. Leave it out of the base price and the commission base, add it to the earnings, and show it on its own row.

title: Card trips are archived with no payment method, so History detail shows 'Payment Method —' while Ride completed says 'Card'
description: _completeCurrentTrip journals the trip with `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null`. For a card trip the journal record has no 'paymentMethod' key. history.archive therefore writes none, and TripHistoryRecord falls back to '—'. A few lines later the same method opens DriverRideCompleted with `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'`. The history layer supports 'Card' (prefs_trip_history_test and history_record_handoff_test store and expect it), so the information is simply dropped.
failure_scenario: Complete a card-paid trip. Ride completed shows 'Payment: Card'. Open Ride history and tap the trip: 'Payment Method' shows '—' with no wallet icon (history_detail.dart:373 hides it for '—'). This happens on every card trip.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:914-917: `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(paid, next: next, paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null, cashCollected: ...);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:966: `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card',`
prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:52: `paymentMethod: data['paymentMethod'] as String? ?? '—',`
history_detail.dart:420: `_detailRow(tr.paymentMethod, _ride.paymentMethod, paymentIcon: true),`
suggested_fix: Pass `widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'` to CompletionJournal.finish as well.

title: Waybill always states 'Payment: In the app', including for cash trips
description: WaybillRecord has no payment method field, and the sheet hard-codes `_Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp)` whenever the fare parses. Every waybill opened from the trip card, the next-trip card or Ride completed therefore says the trip was paid in the app. On a cash trip (paidByCash = true) the rider paid cash in the car (Q23/Q24); the Ride completed screen of that same trip shows 'Payment: Cash'.
failure_scenario: Cash trip, fare '250 kr'. Collect the cash and finish, then tap Waybill > Open on Ride completed. The waybill shows 'Paid by the passenger 250,00 kr' and 'Payment: In the app', while the screen behind it says 'Payment: Cash'.
evidence:
waybill_sheet.dart:89-90: `_Row(tr.paidByPassenger, payment.fare), _Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp),`
app_en.arb:807 `"inApp": "In the app"`
waybill.dart:5-22: WaybillRecord has no payment field
suggested_fix: Carry the payment method (and the cash collected) on WaybillRecord and show it on the waybill.

title: Waiting fee is dropped from the completion journal and history, so History cannot show or break down a fee the trip earned
description: The completed waybill carries `waitingFee` (the 'Includes X waiting fee' line on Ride completed). The journal record only copies tripId, riderName, fare, service, pickup, dropoff, paymentMethod, cashCollected and driverBonus. archive() has no waiting-fee parameter, and TripHistoryRecord has no field for it. After completion the fee survives only folded into the fare string. History detail shows 'Ride Cost' with the fee hidden inside it and no 'includes waiting fee' note. The earnings breakdown says 'Tips and fees: Not available' for a trip that earned a waiting fee. Once archived the split cannot be recovered.
failure_scenario: Card trip of 100,00 kr with 7 minutes at pickup and 90 s at a stop (210 paid s, 42,91 kr). Ride completed shows 142,91 kr and 'Includes 42,91 kr waiting fee'. History detail for the same trip shows 'Ride Cost 142,91 kr' with no waiting line. Earnings history shows 'Tips and fees: Not available'. Worked by hand: round(1226 x 210 / 60) = 4291.
evidence:
completion_journal.dart:105-119: record map has no 'waitingFee' key
completion_journal.dart:170-188: archive(WaybillRecord(... fare: row['fare'] ...)) with no waitingFee
ride_completed.dart:175-179: `if (record?.waitingFee case final fee?) ... tr.includesFeeWaitingFee(fee)`
ride_history.dart:615: `_BreakdownRow(label: tr.tipsAndFees, value: tr.notAvailable)`
suggested_fix: Store waitingFee in the journal record and the history row. Show it in History detail and in the earnings breakdown.

title: Stop arrival and stop departure saves are silently dropped when a background save is in flight, so a crash-restore rewinds the stop and bills the drive as paid stop wait
description: Arriving at a stop (`_onArrivedTap`: `_paidStopWait = true; ...; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow()`) and leaving it (`_advanceRide`: `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow()`) save only through persistNow. persistNow is a `_write(background: true)`, and `_write` returns false at once when `_writing` is set. Nothing checks the result or retries. A background save can be in flight at that moment: the GPS save every 2 minutes in `_applyDriverPosition`, the lifecycle save, or the post-frame init save. In that case the stop change is not saved until the next 2-minute GPS save or lifecycle event. Unlike transitionTo/complete/cancel, which wait for a background save (D-09), these stop commands are lost. DECISIONS.md records Safari kill + reload restore as a real main-path scenario.
failure_scenario: The driver finishes a 1-minute stop wait and slides 'Go to drop-off' while the 2-minute GPS snapshot is being written. The snapshot keeps paidStopWait = true, the old stopIndex, waitSeconds 60 and the old paidWaitSeconds. Safari then kills the tab 90 s later and the trip is restored. initState adds `now - savedAt` to `_waitSeconds` because `_paidStopWait` is true. The driver is shown waiting at the stop they already left, and the 90 s of driving is billed as paid stop wait (about 18,39 kr extra at 12,26 kr/min). The arrival case loses the stop wait in the same way. Traced by reading the code; not run.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:276-278: `if (_disposed || _writing) { return false; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:317-320: `return _write(() => _repository.save(_snapshot(_stage)), background: true);`
accept_ride_trip.dart:857-862: `_paidWaitSeconds += _paidWaitNow; _paidStopWait = false; _waitTimer?.cancel(); _stopCursor += 1; await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
accept_ride_trip.dart:525-529: `_paidStopWait = true; _waitSeconds = 0; ... await _rideLifecycle.persistNow();`
accept_ride.dart:613-617: restore adds `DateTime.now().difference(restored!.savedAt!)` to `_waitSeconds` when `_paidStopWait`
suggested_fix: Make stop arrival and departure wait for an in-flight background save and then write, as transitionTo does. Or re-persist when persistNow returns false.

title: Waybill payment rows are always formatted as 'kr' and read with SEK decimals, so EUR and TND trips get kronor amounts
description: WaybillPayment.fromFare pulls the first number with `\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?` and `_format` always appends ' kr'. The trip flow supports EUR and TND fares (waiting fees are added in euros and millimes; see test/round3/driver_trip_earnings_test.dart). For those trips the waybill shows 'Paid by the passenger', 'Movera fee' and 'Your earnings' in kronor. For TND, a 3-decimal fare like '12,500 DT' is cut to 2 decimals.
failure_scenario: EUR zone, fare '24,50 €'. The waybill shows 'Paid by the passenger 24,50 kr', 'Movera fee −6,13 kr' and 'Your earnings 18,37 kr' under a 'Fare 24,50 €*' row.
evidence:
waybill.dart:296: `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);`
waybill.dart:331-334: `return '${_comma ? text.replaceAll('.', ',') : text} kr';`
suggested_fix: Parse the fare with Money.parseLabel and format the results with Money.formatted in the fare's own currency.

title: Ride completed chip shows the raw stored source ('Exclusive offer', 'Demo Radar') in English in the Swedish and French UI
description: WaybillRecord documents that `source` is stored in English and that screens must show `sourceText`; the waybill sheet does this. The Ride completed chip joins `record.source` directly. A queued next trip is built with `matchedVia: WaybillRecord.exclusiveOfferSource` ('Exclusive offer'), and a bare AcceptRide defaults to `WaybillRecord.demoRadarSource` ('Demo Radar'). Both reach this chip untranslated.
failure_scenario: In Swedish, secure a next trip during a ride, then complete that next trip. The chip under the fare reads 'Comfort · Exclusive offer' instead of 'Exklusivt erbjudande'.
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:340-343: `final label = [record?.service ?? 'Movera', if (record != null && record.source.trim().isNotEmpty) record.source,].join(' · ');`
waybill.dart:69-75: `String get sourceText => switch (source) { exclusiveOfferSource => tr.exclusiveOffer, ... }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:942: `matchedVia: WaybillRecord.exclusiveOfferSource,`
suggested_fix: Use record.sourceText in the chip.

title: System Back on the Ride completed screen skips _finish(): the session stays on_trip and Home can never go online again (a secured next trip is dropped too)
description: _completeCurrentTrip (accept_ride_trip.dart:965) uses pushReplacement to put DriverRideCompleted over Home. Only the Done button runs _finish(), and _finish() is the only code on this path that calls sessionController.stayOnlineAfterTrip() (-> endTrip(), which clears _activeTripId), promotes or clears the next waybill, and pushes the queued next ride. The screen's Scaffold has no PopScope (a grep of lib finds PopScope only in accept_ride, ride_check_card, profile, ride_history, emergency_contacts, app_update_sheet, home_back and support_inbox), and BottomToTopTransition is a plain ModalRoute. So Android Back pops straight to Home. After that, DriverSessionController keeps _activeTripId set to the completed trip with status onTrip. On Home, _isOnline needs availableForOffers (status == online), so it is false and the radar shows 'OFF · Tap to scan'. Tapping it runs _goOnline(), which calls _driverSession.beginGoingOnline(). That method returns at once because _activeTripId != null, yet Home still posts IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.online). completeGoingOnline() then does nothing because the status is not goingOnline. didPopNext only re-runs recovery when activeTripId == null, so nothing repairs this. DrivingTimeClock.sync(online: isOnline) also keeps counting driving time, because isOnline is true for onTrip.
failure_scenario: The driver finishes a cash trip, sees Ride completed and presses the Android Back button instead of Done. Home shows the radar OFF. Each tap on it shows the 'online' island notice, but the driver never goes online and gets no offers until the app is killed and restarted. If a next trip had been secured, CompletionJournal already handed its snapshot into storage, but that trip never opens and the waybill keeps showing it as 'Next trip secured'.
evidence: ride_completed.dart:61-71 `void _finish() { ... widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); if (nextRide != null) { _waybills.promoteNextToCurrent(); navigator.pushReplacement(...` ; ride_completed.dart:117 `return Scaffold(` (no PopScope around it) ; driver_session_controller.dart:128-131 `void beginGoingOnline() { if (_disposed || _activeTripId != null || isSuspended) { return; }` ; home.dart:335 `bool get _isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers;` ; home.dart:191 `if (_recoveryResolved && _driverSession.activeTripId == null) {`
suggested_fix: Wrap the DriverRideCompleted Scaffold in PopScope(canPop: false, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) _finish(); }) so Back takes the same exit as Done.

title: Home passes translated text as matchedVia, so waiting rules for reservations and scheduled rides depend on the UI language and stored sources are no longer English
description: _openOfferTrip passes matchedVia from tr.exclusiveReservation / tr.exclusiveOffer (line 837), ExclusiveReasons.text(assigned), which is tr.assignedByMovera (line 860), and tr.scheduledRide (home_scheduled.dart:236). AcceptRide builds its waiting terms from that string: _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(type: WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)) (accept_ride.dart:988-995). typeOf only matches the English substrings 'scheduled' / 'reservation' (waiting_rules.dart:251). Swedish 'Exklusiv bokning' / 'Bokad resa' and French 'Réservation exclusive' (accented é) / 'Course planifiée' never match, so in sv/fr a reservation or scheduled ride falls back to WaitingRideType.normal. The same string is stored as WaybillRecord.source and as PersistedActiveRide.matchedVia. waybill.dart:46-47 documents that source values 'stay in English in storage', and sourceText only translates the English constants.
failure_scenario: An XL reservation is accepted from its Exclusive card. In English, termsFor applies the scheduled rule (includedWaitingMinutes = 5) on top of the XL rule (3 free minutes, no-show at 3): 5 free minutes, no-show from 5:00. In Swedish the same trip gets 3 free minutes, the waiting fee starts 2 minutes earlier and 'Rider didn't show' unlocks at 3:00. The rider's charge and the driver's no-show right depend on the phone's language. If an admin raises includedWaitingMinutes (say to 10), every sv/fr reservation loses the extra free minutes. The 'Scheduled ride' rule line also disappears from the waiting sheet.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:835-838 `_openOfferTrip(offer, offer.reservation ? tr.exclusiveReservation : tr.exclusiveOffer,);` ; home_scheduled.dart:236 `tr.scheduledRide,` ; waiting_rules.dart:250-252 `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled;` ; app_sv.arb:90 `"exclusiveReservation": "Exklusiv bokning"`, app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`
suggested_fix: Pass stable English source constants (as ride_requests.dart does with 'Movera Radar') or an enum, decide the waiting ride type from offer.reservation / scheduled flags rather than display text, and translate only for display through WaybillRecord.sourceText.

title: The waybill of a cash trip says the passenger paid 'In the app' and shows the full fare as 'Paid by passenger'
description: On the Ride completed screen, Waybill › Open calls showMoveraWaybillSheet(context, record) for _waybills.last. _rows always prints `_Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp)` and `_Row(tr.paidByPassenger, payment.fare)`, and WaybillRecord carries no payment method. For a cash trip (paidByCash, Collect cash flow) the waybill therefore says the payment was made in the app. On a cash trip with a promotion (cashToCollect differs from fare) it also shows the fare, not the cash the rider handed over, as 'Paid by passenger'.
failure_scenario: The driver takes the demo cash Exclusive (fare 176,20 kr, cash to collect 150,00 kr), collects 150 kr in cash and opens the waybill on Ride completed. It reads 'Paid by passenger 176,20 kr · Payment: In the app'. The rider paid neither that amount nor in the app.
evidence: waybill_sheet.dart:70 `final payment = WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus);` ; waybill_sheet.dart:89-90 `_Row(tr.paidByPassenger, payment.fare), _Row(tr.payment, tr.inApp),` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:916-917 the cash method and cash collected go only to the journal, not to the waybill record
suggested_fix: Carry the payment method (and cash collected) on WaybillRecord from _paidWaybill() and print it, for example tr.cash plus the cash amount, instead of the fixed tr.inApp.

title: Waybill earnings take Movera's 25% fee from the waiting fee, which the trip screens say is all the driver's
description: _completeCurrentTrip folds the driver's waiting fee into the waybill fare (_paidWaybill -> fare: _fareWithWaiting, documented 'Q43: the waiting fee is the driver's, in the trip's earnings'). Ride completed (line 182 comment 'Q43: the waiting fee is all the driver's') and the waiting sheet both tell the driver the same. WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare) then computes _feeOre = riderOre * 0.25 over the whole fare, waiting fee included. So 'Your earnings' on the waybill loses 25% of the waiting fee.
failure_scenario: Comfort trip, fare 104,80 kr, driver waits 7 minutes (120 s paid at 12,26 kr/min). waitingFee = round(1226*120/60) = 2452 öre = 24,52 kr, so the waybill fare is 129,32 kr. fromFare: fee = round(12932*0.25) = 3233, so 'Movera fee −32,33 kr' and 'Your earnings 96,99 kr'. Without the wait, earnings would be 78,60 kr, so the driver is shown 18,39 kr for a waiting fee the completed screen says is fully theirs (24,52 kr). Worked by hand; no code was run.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:72-73 `String get _fareWithWaiting => WaitingTerms.addFee(widget.fare, _waitTerms.driverWaitingFee(_paidWaitTotal));` ; waybill.dart:373 `int get _feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round();` ; waybill.dart:380 `String get earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre);` ; ride_completed.dart comment `// Q43: the waiting fee is all the driver's.`
suggested_fix: Store the waiting fee separately (WaybillRecord.waitingFee already exists) and leave it out of the fee base in WaybillPayment, or pass it in as a commission-free extra the way the bonus is handled.

title: Dragging across the rating stars queues one SnackBar per pointer move; dozens of 'Rating not sent' SnackBars then cover Home for minutes
description: The RatingBar has updateOnDrag: true, and onRatingUpdate calls ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar on every call. In flutter_rating_bar 4.0.1, _onDragUpdate calls widget.onRatingUpdate on every drag update (each pointer move) and _onDragEnd calls it once more. Each call adds another SnackBar to the root ScaffoldMessenger queue (default 4 s each). The queue survives Done and popUntil and keeps showing over Home's bottom dock.
failure_scenario: The driver slides a finger from the first to the fifth star (about 0.5 s, about 30 move events), then taps Done. Home's dock and radar orb sit under 'Rating not sent (demo)' SnackBars, one after another, for about 2 minutes.
evidence: ride_completed.dart:388-394 `onRatingUpdate: (rating) { setState(() => _rating = rating); ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(SnackBar(content: Text(tr.ratingNotSentDemo)),); }, updateOnDrag: true,` ; flutter_rating_bar-4.0.1/lib/src/rating_bar.dart:379 `if (widget.updateOnDrag) widget.onRatingUpdate(iconRating);`
suggested_fix: Show the notice once (hideCurrentSnackBar before showing, or show only when the rating first goes from 0 to a value), or set updateOnDrag: false.

title: Payment method shows raw English 'Cash'/'Card' on Ride completed and History detail in sv/fr, and a card trip reads '—' in history
description: _completeCurrentTrip passes paymentMethod: paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card' to DriverRideCompleted (accept_ride_trip.dart:966), which prints it verbatim. The journal stores 'Cash' or null (accept_ride_trip.dart:916), and DriverRideHistoryDetail prints `_ride.paymentMethod` verbatim (history_detail.dart:420). Swedish and French drivers see English 'Cash'/'Card' (tr.cash is 'Kontant' in sv). The same card trip shows 'Card' on the completed screen and '—' under Payment method in its history detail.
failure_scenario: Language set to Svenska, finish a cash trip: Ride completed shows 'Betalning  Cash' and the trip detail shows 'Betalningsmetod  Cash'. Finish a card trip: the completed screen says 'Card' and the history detail says '—'.
evidence: ride_completed.dart:215 `_row(tr.payment, Text(widget.paymentMethod ?? '—', style: _value)),` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:966 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card',` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:916 `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null,` ; history_detail.dart:420 `_detailRow(tr.paymentMethod, _ride.paymentMethod, paymentIcon: true),`
suggested_fix: Keep the stored wire value, but show a translated label (tr.cash / a card string) on both screens, and record 'Card' in the journal for card trips too.

title: The Ride completed chip shows the raw stored source ('Exclusive offer', 'Demo Radar') instead of the translated sourceText
description: _chip joins record.service with record.source. The stored source values are the English constants WaybillRecord.exclusiveOfferSource ('Exclusive offer', used for every queued next trip in accept_ride_trip.dart:948/_buildNextWaybill) and demoRadarSource ('Demo Radar', the AcceptRide default), and WaybillRecord.sourceText exists to translate them. The waybill sheet uses sourceText (waybill_sheet.dart:80). The completed screen does not.
failure_scenario: In Swedish, finish a queued next trip secured during a ride: the completed screen chip reads 'Comfort · Exclusive offer', while its waybill reads 'Exklusivt erbjudande'.
evidence: ride_completed.dart:340-343 `final label = [record?.service ?? 'Movera', if (record != null && record.source.trim().isNotEmpty) record.source,].join(' · ');` ; waybill.dart:70-75 `String get sourceText => switch (source) { exclusiveOfferSource => tr.exclusiveOffer, ...`
suggested_fix: Use record.sourceText in _chip.

title: Home's offer→trip handoff replaces an unknown rider rating with a made-up 4.9 (same defect as the known ride_requests.dart:379, on the Home path)
description: _openOfferTrip, used by every Home Exclusive, Radar-deck and scheduled acceptance, passes riderRating: double.tryParse(offer.rating) ?? 4.9. A dispatch offer whose rating string is not numeric (new rider, '—') opens the trip with a 4.9 rating. That value is shown in the rider profile (tr.ratingAndRides), persisted into the snapshot, and sent in SafetyAlertTrip. The known finding covers only the Radar screen's copy at ride_requests.dart:379.
failure_scenario: An API offer with rating '—' or '' is accepted from Home's deck. The rider sheet on the trip says '4.9 ★', and a safety alert reports a 4.9 rider rating that dispatch never sent.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:952 `riderRating: double.tryParse(offer.rating) ?? 4.9,`
suggested_fix: Make AcceptRide.riderRating nullable and show 'New'/'—' when it is unknown, as the fix for ride_requests.dart:379 should.

title: A driver cancel or no-show never ends the session's trip, so the driver cannot go online again; with a secured next trip, trip B's beginTrip is refused
description: Every other terminal exit calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (endTrip): authoritative outcome (line 379), release (402), rider cancel (456/469) and Ride completed Done (ride_completed.dart:71). `_submitTripCancellation` (lines 1356-1447) does not call it on either branch. Without a next trip it pops straight back to Home. With a secured next trip it pushes the next AcceptRide (line 1441). DriverSessionController keeps `_activeTripId = A` and `_status = onTrip`. On Home, `_isOnline` needs `_driverSession.availableForOffers` (status == online), so the driver shows as offline. `_goOnline` calls `beginGoingOnline()`, which returns at once while `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129), yet Home still shows `IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.online)`. didPopNext's restore check (`_driverSession.activeTripId == null`, home.dart:182) is also skipped. On the next-trip branch, trip B's post-frame `beginTrip(B)` (accept_ride.dart:620) is refused because `_activeTripId` is still A, so the session tracks the wrong trip for all of B. If B is then also driver-cancelled, the driver is stuck the same way.
failure_scenario: The driver accepts a trip from Home, then uses End trip early (or Cancel trip, or No-show) and confirms. The app pops to Home. The radar stays at 'OFF · Tap to scan'. Tapping it shows the 'online' island notice, but the session never leaves onTrip, so no offers come until the app is restarted. Second case: the driver ends trip A early while next trip B is secured. B starts, but the session still says trip A. Cancelling B the same way leaves the driver stuck offline.
suggested_fix: Call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` in `_submitTripCancellation` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds, before pushing the next trip or popping, as the other terminal exits do.

title: System/browser Back on Ride completed skips _finish: the session stays on the finished trip and a secured next trip is never started
description: DriverRideCompleted replaces the trip route (`pushReplacement`, accept_ride_trip.dart:959), so Home is the route underneath. The page has no PopScope, so Android Back, an iOS back swipe or browser Back pops it without running `_finish`. Only `_finish` calls `stayOnlineAfterTrip()`, `promoteNextToCurrent()`/`clearNext()` and pushes `nextRide`. After the pop the session still holds the completed trip as `_activeTripId` with status onTrip. Home therefore shows offline, `beginGoingOnline` is refused, and didPopNext skips the persisted-trip restore because `activeTripId != null` (home.dart:182). With a secured next trip, the completion journal has already handed the active-ride snapshot to trip B and `_waybills.next` still holds B. But B's AcceptRide is never pushed and Home does not restore it, so the trip dispatch assigned sits hidden until the app restarts.
failure_scenario: The driver finishes trip A, which has a secured Exclusive next trip, and presses Android Back on Ride completed instead of Done. Home appears offline with no trip. Next trip B, which the rider is waiting for, never opens. Tapping the radar does not bring the driver online, because the session is still on trip A. Without a next trip the same Back leaves the driver unable to go online.
suggested_fix: Wrap the page in `PopScope(canPop: false, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) _finish(); })` so Back does the same as Done.

title: An Exclusive next trip accepted while its match is still resolving is silently dropped when the current trip finishes or ends
description: `_acceptNextTripRadar` sets `matching`, counts the answer as accepted (`ExclusiveAnswers.instance.accepted()`) and starts a 900 ms timer. That timer moves to `secured` and calls `_waybills.secureNext` + `persistNow`. It checks only `mounted && _stage == onTrip`, not terminal or completion in flight. `_completeCurrentTrip` decides `queuedNext` from the state before its awaits (`secured` only), so a trip still in `matching` gives `next = null`. The match timer is cancelled only after the journal and lifecycle awaits (line 932). If the timer has not fired yet, the accepted trip is cancelled and vanishes. If it fired during the awaits, `_waybills.next` gets B, the background save is refused ('Cannot revive a terminal trip', which shows the 'Trip progress could not be saved' SnackBar), and Ride completed gets `nextRide: null`, so `_finish` calls `clearNext()`. The same pattern exists in `_handleRiderCancelled` (secured read at 422, timer cancelled at 446) and `_drainProjection` (314 / 374). The island long-press menu can also stop the radar during `matching` (`_onTripRadarOn` includes matching), and `_stopOnTripRadar` then cancels the match timer. In every case the driver gets no notice that the trip they accepted is gone.
failure_scenario: Near the drop-off an Exclusive next trip appears. The driver taps Accept and within the 0.9 s match window slides Finish (or the rider of the current trip cancels at that moment). Ride completed shows no next trip and Done returns Home. The driver was told nothing, the accept was counted, and the trip dispatch assigned to them is lost.
suggested_fix: Block Finish, cancel and the radar toggle while `_onTripRadarState == matching`, or wait for the match to resolve before computing `next`. Make the match timer a no-op once `_completionInFlight`, `_cancellationInFlight`, `_handlingRiderCancellation` or `_rideLifecycle.terminal` is set, and tell the driver when an accepted trip is dropped.

title: A cancelled next trip is offered again with the same trip id, so completing it later never reaches history (the row stays 'cancelled by driver')
description: Every next-trip offer on a trip gets the fixed id `'${widget.tripId}-next'` (or `-next-destination` in destination mode). `_cancelNextTrip` archives the secured next trip in history under that id with status `searching` and the driver's reason. It also puts the radar back to `scanning`, so the next GPS fix brings the same offer, with the same id, 2.2 s later. If the driver accepts it and it is handed off and completed, `CompletionJournal._replay` calls `history.archive(... status: completed, authoritative: false)`. `PrefsTripHistoryRepository.archive` returns early when a row with that tripId already exists and the write is not authoritative. The completed trip is never recorded: history keeps showing it as a driver cancel, with no fare in earnings, and it counts in the cancel rate.
failure_scenario: On trip T the driver secures the next trip T-next, then cancels it ('Current trip is taking longer'). A few seconds later the radar offers the same trip again. The driver accepts it, finishes T, then drives and completes T-next. Ride history lists T-next only as 'Cancelled by driver · reassigned'. Its completed fare is missing from history and earnings.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:963-964: `_NextTripRadarOffer get _uniqueDemoNext => _NextTripRadarOffer(
    id:'${widget.tripId}-next', ...`
accept_ride_sheet.dart:264-283: state back to scanning; `PrefsTripHistoryRepository().archive(record, status: TripTransitions.apply(TripStatus.accepted, TripCommand.cancel, TripActor.driver), cancellationActor: 'driver', ...)`
prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:201-204:
      if (rows.whereType<Map>().any((row) => row['tripId'] == record.tripId)) {
        if (!authoritative) return;
        ...
completion_journal.dart:197: `authoritative: data['authoritative'] == true,` (false for a driver completion)
suggested_fix: Give each presented offer a fresh occurrence id (as Home does with tripOccurrenceId), or after a cancel do not offer again an id already archived as terminal.

title: Next-trip offers still arrive and expire while another screen covers the trip, counting as missed Exclusive offers (against the code's own D-05 rule)
description: The code says (D-05, lines 122-123 and 1123) that no next-trip offer comes or runs out while the driver cannot see the trip. The only gate is `_liveUpdatesPaused`, and `_pauseLiveUpdates` runs only on app lifecycle changes and terminal exits. `_AcceptRideState` is not RouteAware (mixins are TickerProviderStateMixin and WidgetsBindingObserver only), unlike Home, which pauses in didPushNext. While a full route covers the trip (the island's History, `pushSingle(... DriverRideHistory)` at accept_ride.dart:1307, or Chat from the trip options), GPS keeps flowing into `_applyDriverPosition`, which calls `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer`. An offer is presented and its 15 s expiry runs. `_denyNextTripRadar` then counts it as missed through `ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()`; at the admin's limit that calls `setOnline(false)` and shows 'offline after missed'. It also sets `_onTripRadarDeclined`, which stops further offers.
failure_scenario: On the last leg the driver opens Ride history from the island and reads it for 20 s. An Exclusive next trip appears behind the covering route and times out. The driver returns to an ordinary trip screen, but the offer was counted as missed. After enough of these, the driver is taken offline at the end of the trip for offers they never saw.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:122-125: `// D-05: no next-trip offer comes or runs out while the driver cannot
      // see the trip; ...`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1072-1074: `if (!mounted || _liveUpdatesPaused || _stage != ActiveRideStage.onTrip || ...`
accept_ride_trip.dart:684-685: `if (_stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); ...`
accept_ride.dart:365-366: `class _AcceptRideState extends State<AcceptRide> with TickerProviderStateMixin, WidgetsBindingObserver {`
accept_ride.dart:1307-1308: `onHistory: () => pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => const DriverRideHistory())),`
accept_ride_trip.dart:1226-1227: `if (ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()) { widget.sessionController?.setOnline(false);`
suggested_fix: Subscribe the trip screen to driverRouteObserver. In didPushNext, pause the offer timers and keep the deadline (as `_pauseLiveUpdates` does for offers); in didPopNext, call `_resumeOnTripOffer`.

title: After one declined or expired next-trip offer, the trip radar still shows ON and sweeping but never offers again
description: `_denyNextTripRadar` (used by Deny and by expiry) sets `_onTripRadarDeclined = true` and puts the state back to `scanning`. `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer` and `_onRideCheckGate` return early while `_onTripRadarDeclined` is true, and only `_toggleOnTripRadar` clears it. The dock and island get `on: _onTripRadarOn`, which is true for `scanning`, so they keep showing the active sweeping orb with 'Stop radar' and 'Turn Exclusive offers off'. The D-05 comment says that after an offer leaves, 'Radar then looks for the next one'.
failure_scenario: The driver lets one Exclusive next-trip offer run out, or denies it. For the rest of the trip the radar dock keeps sweeping and reads 'Stop radar', but no other next-trip offer ever comes, unless the driver holds the radar off and on again.
suggested_fix: Either show the radar as paused while declined, or clear the latch and keep scanning after a decline or expiry, as the D-05 resume path does.

title: Island menu offers 'Turn Exclusive offers off' while a next trip is secured, and choosing it does nothing
description: The island menu labels the radar item from `radarOn: _onTripRadarOn`, which is true for `secured`. Choosing it calls `_toggleOnTripRadar`, which returns at once when the state is `secured`. The driver gets a menu action that silently has no effect.
failure_scenario: With a next trip secured, the driver opens the island menu and taps 'Turn Exclusive offers off'. The menu closes and nothing changes, with no feedback.
suggested_fix: Hide or disable the radar item while a next trip is secured, or pass `radarOn` excluding `secured` and have the toggle explain why.

title: The next trip's rider card shows an invented '312 rides'
description: `_NextTripRadarOffer` has no rider trip count, and the hand-off AcceptRide built in `_completeCurrentTrip` (and in `_submitTripCancellation` at line 1395) passes no `riderTrips`. It falls back to the constructor default `riderTrips = 312`. The snapshot hand-off (`_snapshotForOffer`) also leaves it null, and `fromPersisted` turns that into 312. The rider details row shows `tr.ratingAndRides(..., widget.riderTrips)` (accept_ride_panel.dart:985), so every next trip shows the same made-up count as fact.
failure_scenario: After finishing trip A, the driver goes straight into the secured next trip with Maya. Her details read '4.9 · 312 rides', a number no source provided.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:113: `this.riderTrips = 312,`
accept_ride.dart:258: `riderTrips: snapshot.riderTrips ?? 312,`
accept_ride_trip.dart:936-940: `AcceptRide(tripId: offer.id, riderName: offer.riderName, riderRating: offer.rating, fare: offer.fare, ...` (no riderTrips)
accept_ride_panel.dart:985: `tr.ratingAndRides(widget.riderRating.toStringAsFixed(1), widget.riderTrips),`
suggested_fix: Carry the rider's trip count on the next-trip offer and snapshot, and hide the count when it is unknown.

title: A radar the driver held off comes back on after a crash or reload restore
description: Holding the trip radar sets `_OnTripRadarState.stopped`, but the persisted snapshot (`_buildSnapshot`) does not save the radar state. On restore the state starts as `off`, and `_resumeStageSideEffects` calls `_startOnTripRadar`, whose only guard is `stopped`. The radar therefore scans again, and the driver gets Exclusive next-trip offers they turned off; letting them run out counts as misses.
failure_scenario: On the last leg the driver holds the radar to stop next-trip offers. Safari reloads the PWA and the trip is restored. A few seconds later an Exclusive next-trip offer pops up, and ignoring it counts toward the auto-offline limit.
suggested_fix: Persist whether next-trip offers were stopped in PersistedActiveRide and restore `stopped` from it.

title: If the first one-shot GPS fix fails, the trip screen never subscribes to the GPS stream, so GPS stays dead until the next app pause/resume
description: _startLiveLocation subscribes to watchPosition only after getCurrentPosition succeeds (lines 597-619). If getCurrentPosition throws, the catch block (621-629) only sets the warning, flips _hasLiveLocation to false and asks for one route. It never subscribes to the stream and never retries. On native, getCurrentPosition has an 8 s timeLimit (driver_location_service.dart:25). geolocator_apple/android enforce it with .timeout(timeLimit). After a timeout the service falls back to the last known fix only when that fix is under 30 s old and within 50 m accuracy, and otherwise rethrows (driver_location_service.dart:37-48). _ensurePermission also throws while permission is revoked or location services are off. This is exactly the journey: the driver revokes permission or turns off location, then comes back (resume calls _startLiveLocation at line 152). Or the app resumes while GPS has been silent for 2 minutes (tunnel, garage), so the cached fix is stale. In both cases, once GPS works again no fix ever reaches the screen. The only recovery is another lifecycle pause/resume.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:597-605 `final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(` ; 621-629 `} catch (_) { ... _navigation.keepLastKnown(status: tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis); _rebuild(() { _hasLiveLocation = false; _locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis; }); unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)); }` (no subscription, no retry timer); driver_location_service.dart:25 `timeLimit: const Duration(seconds: 8)`; 44-48 `if (fallback != null) { return fallback; } ... rethrow;`
failure_scenario: A driver heading to a pickup enters a 2-minute tunnel, or revokes location and then grants it again, and switches apps to call the rider. On resume, getCurrentPosition times out after 8 s (no fresh fix yet) and the last-known fix is older than 30 s, so the call rethrows. The island says 'Location updating…' for the rest of the trip, the car and route stay frozen, and 'Arrived' always shows 'Location unavailable. Enable location to confirm' (_nearArrivalTarget needs _hasLiveLocation). The driver cannot arrive at the pickup or at any stop, so a multi-stop trip cannot be finished without backgrounding the app. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Subscribe to watchPosition in the failure path too (or always before the one-shot). Alternatively retry _startLiveLocation with backoff while _hasLiveLocation is false.

title: Without any GPS fix, the trip route, turn banner and ETA are computed from a hard-coded Stockholm point
description: _driverPosition starts at _fallbackDriverPosition (59.3262, 18.0595) (accept_ride.dart:423,543). AcceptRide gets no starting position from Home and ignores DriverStartPosition.cached. When the first GPS attempt fails (permission denied or revoked, services off, timeout), the catch block calls _refreshRoadRoute(force: true), which asks for a road route from that fallback (line 705). NavigationController's own vehicle is the same constant (NavigationSnapshot.stockholm), so progress and the next-turn banner are measured from it. On success, _routeDurationSeconds is set, so the island and sheet show a real-looking 'N min · HH:MM' ETA and a polyline that starts at a place the car is not. On the onTrip stage, _rideCheckPlan also passes this fake route to RideCheckDetector.planLeg, which fixes the trip's expected duration once (only the first plan counts). That skews the 'trip taking longer than expected' check for the rest of the trip.
evidence: accept_ride.dart:423 `static const LatLng _fallbackDriverPosition = LatLng(59.3262, 18.0595);` 543 `LatLng _driverPosition = _fallbackDriverPosition;` accept_ride_trip.dart:628 `unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute(force: true));` 704-706 `await _navigation.ensureRoute(origin: GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition), ...` 714 `if (drawn) { _rideCheckPlan(route); }` 723 `_routeDurationSeconds = route.durationSeconds;` ride_check_detector.dart:43 `if (wholeTrip && _expectedSeconds == null && durationSeconds > 0) { _expectedSeconds = durationSeconds; }`
failure_scenario: A trip is restored after a crash or reboot while location is off or denied, or a trip is accepted and the first fix times out. The map draws a route from Gamla Stan to the pickup with 'Turn left in 300 m' and '9 min · 14:32', although the driver may be kilometres away. On a restored on-trip leg, the RideCheck expected time is locked to the fake route, so the 'longer than expected' card can fire wrongly. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Do not request a route (or show an ETA) until a usable fix exists. Or seed _driverPosition from DriverStartPosition.cached or the persisted snapshot, and mark the route as provisional.

title: A GPS outage counts as 'standing still': the Ride check 'Long stop' card fires during a 2-minute tunnel, and safety alerts carry a minutes-old position as current
description: _hasLiveLocation is cleared only by a stream error, an unusable fix or a pause. When the stream simply goes quiet (tunnel, garage), it stays true indefinitely. The 20 s ride-check ticker passes it as `gps:` to RideCheckDetector.tick. That method treats gps=true plus no new fix as 'the car stands still' and runs _longStop against the last fix's time. The admin default longStopMinutes is 2 (ride_check_admin_config.dart:10). Native streams use a 1 s interval with distanceFilter 0, so a parked car still gets fixes and 2 minutes of silence means lost GPS, not a stop. Elsewhere the screen treats a fix older than 30 s as unusable (_nearArrivalTarget, _approachDistanceMeters, _rideCheckFarDrop use isUsableAt). The tick and _safetyAlertTrip (line 1470) do not. During the silence nothing calls keepLastKnown either, so the island keeps showing the frozen 'Turn right in 120 m' and ETA with no location warning.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1489 `_openRideCheck(_rideCheckDetector.tick(_rideCheckNow, gps: _hasLiveLocation, ...` ; 1470 `position: _hasLiveLocation ? GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition) : null` ; ride_check_detector.dart:81-82 `if (!gps) return _longer(at); return _longStop(at, place) ?? _longer(at);` ; 131-133 `final stopped = at.difference(since); if (stopped <= Duration(minutes: rules.longStopMinutes)) return null;` ; ride_check_admin_config.dart:10 `static const int defaultLongStopMinutes = 2;`
failure_scenario: On a trip, the driver goes through a 4 km tunnel (about 3 minutes, no fixes). About 2 min 20 s in, the 'Long stop' Ride check opens. It covers and hides the navigation island (opacity 0 while covering) as the driver leaves the tunnel, and it uses up the one long-stop check for this trip. If the driver raises an alert, the position sent is the tunnel entrance from minutes earlier. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Pass `gps: _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(now) == true` (fresh GPS) to tick. Send the alert position only when it is fresh, or with its timestamp. Start a staleness timer that calls keepLastKnown after 30 s without a fix.

title: Once the car is off route, the ETA and leg progress jump back to the full leg until the reroute arrives
description: _rebuildBanner sets _progressAlong to null for an off-route fix. routeFraction then reads `(_progressAlong ?? 0) / length` = 0. AcceptRide's _routeEtaText computes `seconds * (1 - routeFraction)` and _remainingMeters computes `total * (1 - routeFraction)`, so the old route's full duration and distance are shown again. _legFraction then gets remaining == _legTotalMeters and the progress bar drops to 0. This holds for the whole reroute window: a 2 s debounce plus the request, up to the 8 s routing timeout when routing is failing, as in this journey. The same happens right after an accepted GPS jump off the route.
evidence: navigation_controller.dart:481 `_progressAlong = progress.offRoute ? null : progress.alongMeters;` ; 156 `return ((_progressAlong ?? 0) / length).clamp(0.0, 1.0);` ; accept_ride.dart:927-929 `final left = seconds * (1 - (_navigation.routeFraction ?? 0)); final minutes = math.max(1, (left / 60).ceil()); return '$minutes min';` ; 920 `return total * (1 - (_navigation.routeFraction ?? 0));` ; road_route_service.dart:29 `this.timeout = const Duration(seconds: 8)`
failure_scenario: On an 18-minute leg with 3 minutes left, the driver misses a turn, or GPS jumps more than 50 m off the polyline. For about 10 s while the reroute request hangs or fails, the island shows '18 min · <arrival 15 minutes later>' and the leg progress bar resets to empty. Then it shows the real value again, or 'En route' once the failed reroute clears the route. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Keep the last on-route progress while off route (keep _progressAlong, or a separate value for display), or hide the ETA while recalculating.

title: A GPS stream error never leads to a resubscribe; on web a revoked permission ends the watch for good
description: The onError handler only shows 'Location updating…' and sets _hasLiveLocation = false. It never cancels and re-creates the subscription and never schedules _startLiveLocation. On web, geolocator_web uses navigator.geolocation.watchPosition. Under the Geolocation spec a PERMISSION_DENIED removes the watch, so no more callbacks arrive even after the driver grants permission again in the site settings. The trip then depends entirely on a later lifecycle resume to restart GPS. The async* watchPosition also ends its stream when _ensurePermission throws inside it, with the same result.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:611-618 `onError: (Object error) { if (!mounted || _liveUpdatesPaused || epoch != _locationEpoch) { return; } _navigation.keepLastKnown(status: tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis); _rebuild(() { _hasLiveLocation = false; _locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis; }); },` ; geolocator_web html_geolocation_manager.dart:68-70 `(web.GeolocationPositionError error) { controller.addError(convertPositionError(error)); }`
failure_scenario: In the web PWA, the driver blocks and then re-allows location from the browser's site controls without the page being hidden. The island stays on 'Location updating…', and arrival at the pickup or stops is refused for the rest of the trip. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: On a stream error, schedule a bounded retry of _startLiveLocation (new epoch, new subscription) while the screen is live.

title: When the last fix is over 30 s old, 'Arrived' says 'Move within 100 m of the pickup' although the real problem is stale GPS
description: _nearArrivalTarget refuses when `!_hasLiveLocation || _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(now) != true`. _blockedArrival only checks `!_hasLiveLocation` before falling through to the distance message. After GPS goes silent (no error, so _hasLiveLocation stays true) and the fix ages past 30 s, the driver is told to move closer even when the last fix was at the pickup. Nothing rebuilds the screen during silence (_fixView is re-evaluated only per fix), so the button can still look enabled (dark) until the tap.
evidence: accept_ride.dart:768 `if (!_hasLiveLocation || _lastLocation?.isUsableAt(DateTime.now()) != true) { return false; }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:497-506 `if (!_arrivalDemo && !_hasLiveLocation) { ... locationUnavailableEnableLocationToConfirm ... } final where = ...; ... Text(tr.moveWithin100MOfWhere(where))`
failure_scenario: The driver reaches an airport pickup in a parking garage and GPS goes quiet. 40 s later they tap 'Arrived', which still looks enabled, and get 'Move within 100 m of pickup' while parked at the pickup. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: In _blockedArrival, use the same freshness test as _nearArrivalTarget and show the location-unavailable message when the last fix is stale.

title: Recenter or auto-resume during a GPS outage switches the trip to 'following' but never moves the camera
description: recenter() sets _mode = following, cancels the resume timer, then calls _request. _request returns early when the last location is older than 30 s (isUsableAt). The map stays where the driver panned. Meanwhile the screen treats the camera as following: _exitBrowse stops the browse pulse and springs the sheet back, the map padding and anchor switch to the 0.75 driving anchor, and the 12 s auto-resume (onAutoResume calls _exitBrowse) does the same on its own. locate() also latches _policy._locating, so the next fix, possibly minutes later, flies to the locate zoom unexpectedly.
evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:599-608 `void recenter() { ... _mode = DriverCameraMode.following; _resumeTimer?.cancel(); ... _request(immediate: true); }` ; 713-716 `if (!_canFollow || location == null || !location.isUsableAt(_now())) { return; }` ; accept_ride.dart:1236-1237 `cameraAnchor: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following ? .75 : .5`
failure_scenario: In a tunnel with no fixes for over 30 s, the driver pans the map and taps Recenter. The pulse disappears and the map shifts with the padding change but stays on the panned area, not the car, until GPS returns and the camera suddenly jumps. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: When there is no usable fix, recenter to the last known pose (or keep browse mode and show the location warning) instead of switching mode without moving.

title: A new route is split into driven/remaining at the previous route's progress until the next GPS fix
description: _onNavigationChanged puts the new route into _roadGeoPoints and _rebuild calls _syncRouteLines(_roadGeoPoints, _camera.alongMeters, ...). _camera.alongMeters is DriverCameraPolicy._along, which still refers to the old route: it resets only in the next camera.update, which needs a new usable fix. The reroute timer and 'Retry route' deliver routes outside any fix. Their new polyline (starting at the car) is drawn with its first N metres (N = old route progress) faded as already driven, and the remaining line starts far ahead of the car. This lasts until a fix arrives, which can be a long time when GPS is silent.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:572-580 `_rebuild(() { if (pointsChanged && mappedRoute != null) { _roadGeoPoints = mappedRoute.points; ...` ; accept_ride.dart:499 `void _rebuild(VoidCallback update) { setState(update); _AcceptRideTrip(this)._syncRouteLines(); }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:637-638 `_routeLines.sync(_roadGeoPoints, _camera.alongMeters, _routeZoomStep);` ; driver_camera_controller.dart:87 `double get alongMeters => _along ?? 0;` (reset only inside resolve at 221-222)
failure_scenario: 4 km into the leg the driver leaves the route and the reroute arrives from the timer. The first 4 km of the new route draw grey 'travelled' and the blue route starts 4 km ahead of the car until the next fix, which never comes while GPS is silent. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Reset the split to 0 when the polyline identity changes (or have the camera policy take the new route at once), and sync the lines after _followVehicle.

title: With approximate-only location (iOS 'Precise' off, Android 12 coarse), every fix is rejected and the trip shows 'Location updating…' forever
description: isUsableAt rejects any accuracy above 50 m, and _applyDriverPosition maps every non-displayable fix to keepLastKnown('Location updating…'). The app never checks Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy() and never asks for temporary full accuracy. When a driver re-grants location after revoking it (this journey) and the OS re-grants it as approximate (iOS 14+ toggle, Android 12 'Approximate'), every fix of about 1-3 km accuracy is dropped. The screen promises an update that will never come, and arrival is never allowed.
evidence: driver_location_repository.dart:50-55 `if (at == null || accuracy == null || !accuracy.isFinite || accuracy < 0 || accuracy > 50) { return false; }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:645-651 `if (!location.isDisplayableAt(DateTime.now())) { _navigation.keepLastKnown(status: tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis); ...`
failure_scenario: The driver revokes and re-allows location on iOS with 'Precise Location' off. Fixes arrive every second with accuracy around 1,500 m. The island shows 'Location updating…' indefinitely and 'Arrived' keeps refusing, with nothing telling the driver to enable precise location. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Detect reduced accuracy (getLocationAccuracy, or a run of fixes above 50 m) and show a dedicated 'turn on precise location' message, or request temporary full accuracy.

title: An out-of-order GPS fix is ignored by navigation but returned as drawable, so the car, camera and arrival check jump back to an older position
description: setVehicle returns true for a fix older than the last accepted one. Its contract says true means 'the caller should draw it'. _applyDriverPosition then writes that older fix into _driverPosition and _lastLocation, feeds it to the camera (which accepts any fix under 30 s old) and moves the marker. Navigation progress and the banner stay on the newer fix, so the screen and navigation disagree until the next fix.
evidence: navigation_controller.dart:221-226 `if (at != null && _lastMeasuredAt != null && at.isBefore(_lastMeasuredAt!)) { return true; }` ; accept_ride_trip.dart:655-669 `if (!_navigation.setVehicle(location)) { return; } ... _driverPosition = next; ... _camera.update(location: location, ...); _vehicle.moveTo(...)`
failure_scenario: After a resume, the provider delivers a batched or cached fix stamped earlier than the last accepted one. The marker and camera snap back along the road while the banner distance stays put, and _nearArrivalTarget is evaluated from the older point. Verified by reading the code; not run.
suggested_fix: Return false for out-of-order fixes (as for held jumps) so the caller drops them too.

title: formatDistance shows '10.0 km' for distances between 9,950 m and 10,000 m instead of '10 km'
description: The decimals are chosen from the unrounded km value (km < 10 gives 1 decimal), but toStringAsFixed(1) rounds 9.95 to 9.999 up to '10.0'. Every other value of 10 km or more is shown without a decimal, so the banner and island step from '10.0 km' to '10 km' as the car gets further from the maneuver. This is a separate boundary from the known 999.5-1000 m issue.
evidence: route_instruction.dart:542-545 `final km = meters / 1000; return l.navKilometers(km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0).replaceAll('.', l.navDecimalMark));`
failure_scenario: meters = 9,970 gives km 9.97, which is below 10, so toStringAsFixed(1) = '10.0' and the banner reads 'Continue 10.0 km' ('10,0 km' in sv/fr). Worked by hand; not run.
suggested_fix: Round first, then choose the format: `final tenths = (meters / 100).round() / 10; tenths < 10 ? one decimal : none`.

title: Setting a destination leaves non-matching offers on the Home deck and in the pending queue
description: Destination mode is meant to show only trips heading the driver's way. The filter (_followsDestination) runs only when an offer is first added (_showRadarHomeOffer, _showOutsideRadarOffer). _activateDestinationMode never re-filters what is already on Home: it leaves _radarHomeOffers and _pendingRadarHomeOffers alone, then seeds the demo trips. Later, _refreshRadarHomeOffers moves every pending offer onto the deck without checking the filter. The dispatch listener (_watchDispatchRadar) only removes offers that dispatch dropped. The other offer filters on Home do re-filter when they change: _onCategoriesChanged (home_offer_rules.dart:26-38) and _setAcceptsCash (home_offer_rules.dart:42-59) dismiss offers on the deck and in the queue that no longer pass. Destination mode has no equivalent. The full Radar list (ride_requests.dart:137-139) does hide these trips, so the deck and the list disagree.
failure_scenario: The driver is online with two demo Radar cards on the deck whose drop-offs are south of the city. They tap the island search button, which is not tucked while only deck cards are up, and confirm Arlanda (north). Both southern cards stay on the deck and can still be matched. The 1.5 s seed timer cannot raise the destination Exclusive (Sofia, 'Near ...') because _showOutsideRadarOffer returns while _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty, so _showDispatchOfferAt(0) only appends way-1 behind the southern cards. The 'All offers' list hides the southern trips (followsDestination false), so the deck shows trips the list does not. Found by reading the code; nothing was run.
suggested_fix: In _activateDestinationMode, after the route is known, remove deck and pending offers (and a non-reservation Exclusive) that fail _followsDestination, the same way _onCategoriesChanged does. Also apply _followsDestination in _refreshRadarHomeOffers before moving pending offers onto the deck.

title: 'Destination mode until HH:MM' shows the arrival ETA, not when the mode actually ends
description: The details sheet (showDestinationDetailsSheet) prints tr.destinationModeUntilUntil(until) from _destinationUntil. That value is the confirm time plus the route's travel time (result.durationSeconds), which is the arrival time. The mode actually ends when the admin time limit runs out: _destinationLimitTimer is armed with DestinationModeSession.timeLeft(), which is started + timeLimitHours (default 2 h). With the time limit off, the mode never ends, yet the sheet still names an end time.
evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart:325-326:
        _destinationUntil = result.durationSeconds == null ? null
            : DateTime.now().add(Duration(seconds: result.durationSeconds!.round()));
home.dart:373: DateTime? _destinationUntil; // "Destination mode until 02:40".
home_map_sheet.dart:311-313: final left = session.timeLeft(); ... _destinationLimitTimer = Timer(left, ...)
destination_island.dart:153: if (until != null) tr.destinationModeUntilUntil(until),
failure_scenario: At 10:00 the driver confirms Kista centrum with a 25 min route, under the default rules (2 h limit). Tapping the island shows 'Destination mode until 10:25'. The mode actually stays on, and keeps filtering offers, until 12:00. If the admin sets a 0.25 h limit, it ends at 10:15 while the sheet still says 10:25. Worked out by hand from the code.
suggested_fix: Set _destinationUntil from DestinationModeSession.instance.timeLeft() (now + left), or null when there is no time limit.

title: The daily destination limit lives only in memory, so restarting or reloading the app resets it
description: usedToday() counts entries in _started, an in-memory list on a process-wide singleton. Nothing persists it, and LOCAL_DATA.md lists no key for it. refusal() is the only enforcement of the admin's destinationsPerDay, and it is checked when the picker opens on Home (home_map_sheet.dart:273) and on the trip (next_trip_gate.dart:65). The admin limit is described as 'How many destinations one driver can set per day', but a cold start, PWA reload or crash recovery brings the count back to 0.
failure_scenario: Under the defaults (2 per day) the driver sets Solna at 09:00 and Kista at 11:00. A third try shows 'Today's destinations are used'. They close and reopen the app (or reload the web page) and can set two more destinations the same day, with no limit on how often they repeat this. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Store the day's start times (for example a dated list in SharedPreferences, added to localDataInventory) and load them when DestinationModeSession is created, or take the count from the backend.

title: Logout does not reset DestinationModeSession, so the next driver inherits the previous driver's destination count and state
description: _logout resets the waybills, the dispatch demo, safety alerts and the session controller. It never touches DestinationModeSession.instance, and neither does clearLocalUserData. That process-wide singleton keeps the previous driver's _started list (the daily count), _activeSince, _timedOut and the kept route. Home.dispose only cancels _destinationLimitTimer; it does not call ended(). The next driver who signs in on the same running app gets the previous driver's daily count, and OnTripDestination.follows reads that driver's leftover expired()/route state.
failure_scenario: Driver A sets two destinations today, then logs out from Profile. Driver B logs in on the same app instance and taps the destination search on Home. The island says 'Today's destinations are used' (DestinationRefusal.usedToday) although B has set none. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Add a reset (DestinationModeSession.instance = DestinationModeSession()) to _logout and to the fallback logout path in profile.dart.

title: Home's time-limit timer for the old destination ends a destination the driver set later during a trip
description: Home arms _destinationLimitTimer for its own destination, and the timer stays armed while AcceptRide covers Home. On the trip, the driver can set a new destination (accept_ride_panel.dart:184), which calls DestinationModeSession.started() and restarts the shared session's clock. When Home's old timer fires, Home is still mounted and _destinationModeActive is still true, so it calls _endDestinationMode() (which calls session.ended()) and then session.timedOut(). That ends the new on-trip destination long before its own limit. From then on OnTripDestination.follows returns true for every offer.
failure_scenario: At 10:00 the driver sets Kista on Home, so the 2 h timer is due at 12:00. They accept a trip at 11:40 and, at 11:50 on the trip, set Södertälje from the trip menu (a daily use; it should last until 13:50). At 12:00 Home's timer fires: the session is marked timed out, the island announces that the destination ended, and next-trip offers are no longer filtered toward Södertälje, 1 h 50 min early. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Keep one timer, owned by the session and re-armed by started(), or have Home's callback check that the session's _activeSince is still the one it armed for before ending it.

title: A destination set or changed during a trip is dropped when the driver returns to Home
description: On the trip screen, _openDestinationPicker counts a daily use (OnTripDestination.started) and stores the new destination only in AcceptRide's local fields (_destinationActive/_destinationAddress/_destinationPosition). DestinationModeSession is documented as 'the driver's destination today ... shared by Home and the trip screen', but nothing hands the new destination back to Home. _openOfferTrip ignores the pushed route's result, and Home only reads its own _destinationPosition. After the trip, Home either has no destination (offers unfiltered) or keeps filtering toward the old one. Home also overwrites the session's route with keepRoute(old destination).
failure_scenario: Home has Kista set (use 1 of 2). On a trip, the driver changes the destination to Södertälje (use 2 of 2). After drop-off, Home's island still shows 'Kista centrum · N min' and Radar and Exclusive offers are filtered toward Kista. Trying to set Södertälje again on Home is refused with 'Today's destinations are used'. If Home had no destination before the trip, Home shows none and every offer passes, although a daily use was spent. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Return the trip's destination to Home when the trip ends (through the session or the session controller), and have Home adopt it with _activateDestinationMode-like state without counting another use.

title: After a restart, a restored trip filters next-trip offers by its destination with no time limit
description: AcceptRide.fromPersisted restores destinationModeActive, the address and the point from the snapshot (accept_ride.dart:288-290). The restarted process has a fresh DestinationModeSession, so _activeSince is null and _timedOut is false. timeLeft() returns null, and expired() is false because null != Duration.zero. OnTripDestination.follows therefore keeps applying the destination filter, along a straight line because routeTo() is empty, indefinitely. The admin time limit, which otherwise turns the filter off after it expires, can no longer apply. The flag is also copied to every secured next trip (accept_ride_trip.dart:954-956, 973-975).
failure_scenario: At 08:00 the driver sets a destination (2 h limit) and accepts a trip. The browser tab is killed at 09:50 and reopened at 10:30, inside the 6 h freshness window. The trip restores with destination mode on. Although the limit ended at 10:00, next-trip offers whose drop-off is not toward the old destination are still suppressed, and that carries into the next secured trip. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Persist the destination's start time in the snapshot and restore it into DestinationModeSession, or treat a restored destination whose start time is unknown or past the limit as expired.

title: The destination Exclusive offer is offered again after the driver accepted it, and on every return to Home after declining it
description: _scheduleVisibleOffers runs on every resume of Home (didPopNext, app resume, going online). In destination mode it re-shows _destinationDemoExclusive after 2.2 s. That field is cleared only when destination mode ends (_clearDemoDestinationTrips), never when the offer is accepted or declined. _acceptOutsideRadarOffer sets _exclusiveDemoTaken, but only the non-destination path reads that flag (to switch to the cash offer); the 'toward' branch wins whenever destination mode is on. The Sofia trip ('Near <destination>', 248 kr, demo-destination-final) the driver just completed is therefore offered again with its island message and a new Notifications entry. A declined one returns after every screen change.
failure_scenario: In the demo, the driver sets Kista and accepts the Exclusive 'Sofia · Near Kista centrum'. They drive and complete the trip, then come back to Home with destination mode still on. 2.2 s later the same Sofia offer, with the same pickup 'near you' computed from the old position, slides up again as a new Exclusive. Declining it with × and then opening Scheduled rides and coming back brings it up once more. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Clear _destinationDemoExclusive when it is accepted or dismissed (in _acceptOutsideRadarOffer / _outsideRadarOfferGone when gone.id == DemoDestinationTrips.exclusiveId).

title: Home destination summary rounds the distance to whole km, so it shows '0 km' near the destination
description: destinationTimeDistanceLabel formats the distance as (meters / 1000).round() km. Home's details sheet (_destinationSummary) uses it with the live road route. Any distance under 500 m prints '0 km', and 1.4 km prints '1 km', while the minutes are clamped to at least 1.
failure_scenario: The driver is 420 m from the destination. Tapping the island shows '1 min · 0 km · Destination mode until ...'. Worked out by hand: (420 / 1000).round() = 0.
suggested_fix: Use one decimal below 10 km (or metres below 1 km), with the localized decimal mark.

title: The destination confirm sheet prints the distance with a '.' decimal in French and Swedish
description: destinationDistanceTimeLabel uses toStringAsFixed(1), which always gives '38.1 km', while fr/sv use a decimal comma. This is a separate formatter from the known driver_distance.dart one, so fixing that one will not fix this.
failure_scenario: With the app in Swedish, confirming Arlanda shows '38.1 km · 34 min' instead of '38,1 km'. Worked out from the code.
suggested_fix: Format through the same localized number formatter as the rest of the app.

title: Re-setting a destination while the previous road-route fetch is still running seeds the demo trips along a straight line
description: _refreshDestinationRoadRoute goes through CoalescingMapRouteRefresh.request. When a fetch is already running, request() only stores the new one as pending and returns at once. _endDestinationMode calls cancelPending() but cannot stop the running fetch. If the driver turns the destination off and sets a new one before that fetch ends, 'await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute()' in _activateDestinationMode completes before any new route arrives. _fitDestinationRoute and _seedDemoDestinationTrips then run with _cameraRoute == null and place the demo trips along the straight driver-to-destination line. When the real road route arrives, the filter uses the road corridor instead.
failure_scenario: On a slow routing service, the driver turns off Kista and sets Södertälje while the last Kista refresh is still in flight. The demo trips 'On your way · 35 %/60 %' are placed off the straight line, and the camera fits the straight line. Once the road route arrives, those trips may fall outside the road corridor and silently disappear from the list. Inferred from reading the code.
suggested_fix: In _activateDestinationMode, wait for the new destination's own fetch (for example await a dedicated fetch rather than the coalesced request), or re-seed the demo trips when the first route for the new destination arrives.

title: A driver cancel or no-show never ends the session's trip, so the driver is stuck 'on trip' on Home: they cannot go online and the driving clock keeps counting
description: Every other way a trip ends calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (endTrip) before leaving: _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome:379, _leaveAfterRelease:402, _handleRiderCancelled:456/469, and DriverRideCompleted._finish:71. `_submitTripCancellation` (the driver's own cancel, and the no-show path) does not. It journals the outcome, calls `_rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow`, discards the waybill and then runs `navigator.pop()` (or pushReplacement for a queued next trip). Nothing calls endTrip. ActiveRideController does not touch the session, and AcceptRide.dispose does not either (grep finds only the 5 endTrip callers listed). So after the pop, DriverSessionController keeps `_activeTripId = <cancelled trip>` and `_status = onTrip`. On Home: `_isOnline` needs `availableForOffers` (status == online), which is false, so Home draws the OFF orb. Tapping it runs `_goOnline` -> `beginGoingOnline()`, which returns at once because `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129). `completeGoingOnline` then does nothing as well, yet `_goOnline` still posts `HomeIslandNotices.online`. didPopNext also skips recovery because `activeTripId != null` (home.dart:182). Meanwhile `isOnline` (online || onTrip) stays true, so `DrivingTimeClock.instance.sync(online: true)` keeps the 12 h count running. After 12 h `_drivingLimitReached` takes the `activeTripId != null` branch and only sets offline-after-trip. The rest never starts, because the clock only stops when isOnline turns false. With a queued next trip, the new AcceptRide's beginTrip(next) is also ignored (`_activeTripId != null && != tripId`), so the session keeps the old trip's id for the whole next trip.
failure_scenario: Shift trip 9: heading to pickup, the driver cancels with 'Rider not at pickup' and confirms. The trip screen pops to Home. The radar orb reads 'OFF · Tap to scan'. A tap shows 'Radar online' on the island, but the orb stays OFF and no offers come for the rest of the shift until the app is killed. The Driving time row keeps counting worked hours the whole time, and the 12 h limit never turns into a 6 h rest.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1384-1389 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) {...} _waitTimer?.cancel(); ... _waybills.discardCurrent();` then :1439-1446 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (nextRide != null) { navigator.pushReplacement(...); return; } if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }`. There is no stayOnlineAfterTrip/endTrip call, whereas :379, :402, :456, :469 and ride_completed.dart:71 all call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip();`. driver_session_controller.dart:129 `if (_disposed || _activeTripId != null || isSuspended) { return; }`; :84-86 `bool get isOnline => _status == DriverOnlineStatus.online || _status == DriverOnlineStatus.onTrip;`
suggested_fix: Call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before the pop/pushReplacement, as the other terminal exits do. Add a widget test that checks `session.activeTripId == null` and `availableForOffers` after a driver cancel.

title: Driving-limit warnings ('30/10 min left', 'Rest until') posted during a trip are taken and shown by the covered Home island, so the driver never sees them
description: The 30 and 10 minute warnings and the limit notice are Dart timers in Home (`_syncDrivingLimit` -> `_drivingWarning` / `_drivingLimitReached`). They post through `IslandMessages.show`. Home is the only consumer of that queue (grep: only home_map_sheet.dart:1247/1259 call peek/take). `_onIslandMessagesChanged`/`_showNextIslandMessage` check only `mounted`, not `_routeVisible`, and `_pauseHomeUpdates` does not stop them. While AcceptRide is pushed over Home (as it is for most of a shift with 25 trips), Home stays mounted underneath. It takes the message off the queue at once and plays it for 3 to 4.5 s on its own hidden island. The trip screen's AdaptiveTripIsland never reads IslandMessages. When the driver returns to Home the message is gone. `_drivingWarning` also adds the minutes to `warned`, so the warning is never shown again. The same applies to the 'Rest until' notice from `_drivingLimitReached` and to `offlineAfterMissed` posted by `_denyNextTripRadar` during a trip.
failure_scenario: The driver is 11 h 25 min into the shift and driving a rider. At 11 h 30 and 11 h 50 the 30-minute and 10-minute warnings fire, each consumed by the Home island under the trip screen. At 12 h 'Rest until 04:30' is consumed the same way. The driver finishes the trip, lands on Home already offline and blocked, and was never warned.
