evidence: home_account.dart:120-123 `void _drivingWarning(int minutes) { if (!mounted || !_account.warned.add(minutes)) { return; } IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.drivingLeft(minutes)); }`; home_map_sheet.dart:1244-1268 `void _onIslandMessagesChanged() { if (!mounted) { return; } ... _showNextIslandMessage(); } void _showNextIslandMessage() { if (!mounted || _islandMessage != null) { return; } final next = IslandMessages.take(); ...`; home.dart:173 `void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }` (the pause does not touch the island message queue).
suggested_fix: Do not take messages from the queue while Home is covered (`!_liveVisible`); drain the queue on didPopNext/resume. Alternatively, let the trip screen's island show driving-limit warnings while a trip is open.

title: On-trip Radar keeps offering and securing next trips after the 12 h limit, so the forced rest can be postponed indefinitely
description: When the limit is reached during a trip, Home only records offline-after-trip: `_drivingLimitReached` -> `_driverSession.setOnline(false)` sets `_offlineAfterTrip`, and `availableAfterTrip` becomes false. The trip screen never reads that state. `_maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer` checks admin rules, stage, radar state, distance and NextTripGate, but not `sessionController.availableAfterTrip` or the driving clock. So next-trip offers keep arriving after the limit, and Accept secures one. On completion, DriverRideCompleted._finish calls endTrip, which turns the driver offline as recorded, and then immediately pushReplacement's the next AcceptRide. Its beginTrip puts the session back to onTrip and the clock running. On that trip the radar again scans and offers another next trip. Home's limit timer fires again with left == 0, but it only re-sets offline-after-trip. Nothing in the chain stops a driver who keeps accepting a next trip.
failure_scenario: At 11 h 58 the driver starts a trip. At 12 h 00 the limit is reached (offline-after-trip set). 2.2 s later the on-trip Radar shows an Exclusive next trip; the driver accepts it and it is secured. After drop-off they tap Done and the next trip opens and runs another 25 minutes. During it another next trip is offered and secured, and so on, all past the 12 h work limit that admin set as blocking.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1065-1103 `void _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer() { if (!DriverOfferRules.current.exclusiveWhileDriving || ...) { return; } if (!mounted || _liveUpdatesPaused || _stage != ActiveRideStage.onTrip || _onTripRadarState != _OnTripRadarState.scanning || _onTripRadarDeclined || ...) { return; } ... _nextTripRadarDemoTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 2200), ...` (no availableAfterTrip/driving-limit check); home_account.dart:133-136 `if (_driverSession.activeTripId != null) { _driverSession.setOnline(false); return; }`; ride_completed.dart:71-75 `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); if (nextRide != null) { _waybills.promoteNextToCurrent(); navigator.pushReplacement(BottomToTopTransition(nextRide));`
suggested_fix: Gate next-trip offers (and the Accept action) on `widget.sessionController?.availableAfterTrip != false`. Listen to the session so an offer already up is withdrawn when it flips. A driver who has reached the limit should not start a new trip from a secured slot either.

title: The forced break (and _goOffline generally) leaves the full Radar list open, and a Match there still opens a trip
description: `_drivingLimitReached` (not on a trip) calls `_goOffline()`. `_goOffline` cancels Home's own dispatch subscription and clears Home's offer lists, but never sets `showRideRequests = false`. While the full Radar page is open, Home's body is the `RideRequests` Stack (home.dart:717), so the SlidingUpPanel and its `_closeHomeFloatingPopupsForSheet` are not mounted, and `_closeDriverSheet()` cannot close the page. RideRequests has its own dispatch subscription and offer list. `_matchTrip`/`_claimTrip` never check the session's availability. On a won claim it pushes AcceptRide, whose post-frame `beginTrip` puts the offline, limit-blocked driver onto a trip with the driving clock running again.
failure_scenario: At 11 h 59 m 50 s the driver opens the Radar list to compare trips. At 12 h 00 the limit fires: the island says 'Offline' and the session goes offline, but the Radar list stays on screen with live Match buttons. The driver taps Match and gets a new trip although they are supposed to be resting for 6 h.
evidence: home.dart:939-971 `Future<void> _goOffline() async { ... setState(() { _driverSession.setOnline(false); _hasRideOffers = false; _outsideRadarOffer = null; _radarHomeOffers.clear(); ... }); ... await _HomeMapSheet(this)._closeDriverSheet(); }` (no `showRideRequests = false`); home.dart:717 `body: showRideRequests ? Stack(... RideRequests(...` ; ride_requests.dart:301-318 `_matchTrip` checks only visibility/state/_matchingOfferId; home_account.dart:137 `unawaited(_goOffline());`
suggested_fix: Set `showRideRequests = false` in `_goOffline`. Also make RideRequests refuse to claim when `sessionController.availableForOffers` is false.

title: The island's TODAY earnings face always shows the hard-coded '183.25 kr', whatever the driver earned today
description: Tapping the Home island cycles through hidden -> LAST TRIP -> TODAY -> history. The TODAY face always renders `DigitalIslandParts.sampleToday` ('183.25 kr'), and so does the trip screen's TripIsland. It has no demo label, although the app records every completed fare locally (PrefsTripHistoryRepository) and History computes a real 'Today' total from them. The constant is only marked as sample in a code comment. LAST TRIP likewise falls back to the sample '126 kr' before any trip has been driven. The figure also uses a '.' decimal, unlike Money's '183,25 kr'.
failure_scenario: After 25 trips worth about 3 100 kr, the driver taps the island and sees 'TODAY 183.25 kr'. Opening Ride history -> Today shows the real recorded total. On the first launch of a shift, 'LAST TRIP 126 kr' is shown before any trip.
evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:1222-1224 `case _IslandFace.today: return DigitalIslandParts.amountFace('island-today', tr.todayCaps, DigitalIslandParts.sampleToday);`; digital_island.dart:673-675 `// Sample figures until earnings come from the backend. static const String sampleToday = '183.25 kr'; static const String sampleLastTrip = '126 kr';`; trip_island.dart:100-104 same sampleToday; home_map_sheet.dart:1349 `if (fare == null || !fare.contains(RegExp(r'\d'))) { return DigitalIslandParts.sampleLastTrip; }`
suggested_fix: Compute today's total from the local history, as Ride history does, or label the face as sample/unavailable. Show '—' for the last trip when there is none.

title: History keeps only the newest 500 receipts, so a high-volume driver's month total (and older week data) is silently truncated
description: Both `_decode` and `archive` keep only `rows.take(maxReceipts)` with maxReceipts = 500, counting completed and cancelled rows alike. Older rows are dropped from storage on the next archive. Ride history's 'Month' period sums `_periodRidesList`, filtered by calendar month from that truncated list, and labels it 'October 2026' with no hint that older trips were evicted. At the journey's 25 trips a day (plus cancels), 500 rows cover about 19 days, so from around the 20th of the month the month's 'Recorded fares' and ride count are too low, and the dropped receipts are gone for good.
failure_scenario: The driver does 25 trips a day from 1 October. On 22 October, about 550 rows have been archived, so the 1-2 October trips are deleted from storage. History -> Month shows 'October 2026' earnings and ride count without them. The money shown for the month is wrong, and the old receipts cannot be recovered.
evidence: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:79 `static const maxReceipts = 500;` :150 `return _HistoryDecode(unique.take(maxReceipts).toList(), invalid: invalid);` :245 `'rows': rows.take(maxReceipts).toList(),`; ride_history.dart:108 `_HistoryPeriod.month => at.year == now.year && at.month == now.month,`
suggested_fix: Evict by age (for example older than the period views need) rather than by count, or keep per-period aggregates. At minimum, mark a period total as partial when its oldest row may have been evicted.

title: Logout resets every in-memory singleton except DrivingTimeClock, so the next login inherits the previous worked hours or rest block
description: `_logout` (and Profile's fallback path) clears local data and resets the waybills, dispatch, safety alerts, language, traffic setting and session. It never calls `DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset()`, which exists and is used only by test config. `session.reset()` notifies Home, which stops the clock and keeps `_banked`. The next DriverHome in the same app run (a re-login, or a different driver on a shared phone) starts with the previous account's worked time, and with 'Rest until HH:MM' if that account had hit the limit.
failure_scenario: Driver A works 11 h 50 min and logs out. Driver B logs in on the same phone and goes online. The Driving time row shows '0 h 10 min' left; ten minutes later B is forced offline with 'Rest until …' for A's hours.
evidence: main.dart:180-195 `Future<void> _logout() async { ... MapTrafficSetting.reset(); DriverLanguage.reset(); _activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository(); _waybills.reset(); ... dispatch.reset(); _safetyAlerts.reset(); _session.reset(); }` (no DrivingTimeClock reset); driving_time_clock.dart:68-72 `void reset() { _banked = Duration.zero; _since = null; _offSince = null; }` used only in test/flutter_test_config.dart:64.
suggested_fix: Call `DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset()` in `_logout` and in Profile's fallback logout path, next to `session.reset()`.

title: A cash trip is 'Settled' in History while its waybill shows a 25 % Movera fee the driver kept in cash
description: The waybill sheet treats `fare` as what the rider pays: WaybillPayment takes a 25 % Movera fee and shows 'Your earnings' = fare − fee. History's cash balance treats the same `fare` as the driver's money: CashBalance.balance = fare − cashCollected. For a cash trip where the rider paid exactly the fare, History says 'Settled · cash matched your fare', but by the waybill the driver holds Movera's 25 % and owes it. The two screens give contradictory money for the same trip, and 'Other earnings' sums the History version.
failure_scenario: Cash trip, fare 128,40 kr, the rider pays 128,40 kr in cash. The latest waybill shows Movera fee −32,10 kr, your earnings 96,30 kr. Ride history -> Other earnings shows +0,00 kr 'Settled' and does not show the 32,10 kr owed to Movera.
evidence: waybill.dart:285 `static const double serviceFeeRate = 0.25;` :319 `int get _feeOre => (_riderOre * _feeRate).round();` :326 `String get earnings => _format(_fareOre - _feeOre);`; cash_balance.dart:86 `Money get balance => fare - cashCollected;`; trip_history.dart:172-174 `CashBalance? get cashBalance => paidByCash && status == TripStatus.completed ? CashBalance.fromLabels(fare: fare, cashCollected: cashCollected ?? fare) : null;`
suggested_fix: Use one money model: either compute the cash balance from the driver's earnings (fare − fee) or drop the fee from the waybill for these trips. Until pricing comes from the backend, make both screens read the same definition.

title: Logout does not reset DrivingTimeClock, so the next driver inherits the previous driver's worked hours and rest block
description: Profile logout calls runtime.logout, which is _MoveraAppState._logout (main.dart:180-195). It resets traffic, language, waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and the session, but never calls DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset(). DrivingTimeClock (lib/core/session/driving_time_clock.dart:15) is a process-wide singleton holding _banked/_since/_offSince. The new DriverHome built from DriverStarter's 'Return to demo' (starter.dart:106-112) reads the same instance: _HomeAccount._blocksGoingOnline (home_account.dart:174-178) and _onlineHold/_islandHold use clock.restUntil, and the sheet's driving-time row shows clock.worked/left. test/flutter_test_config.dart:64 resets this clock before every test because it is per-driver state, but the app never does this at logout.
evidence: main.dart:180-195 `Future<void> _logout() async { ... await clearLocalUserData(); MapTrafficSetting.reset(); DriverLanguage.reset(); _activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository(); _waybills.reset(); ... _safetyAlerts.reset(); _session.reset(); }` (no DrivingTimeClock reset); driving_time_clock.dart:68 `void reset() {` is called only from test/flutter_test_config.dart:64; home_account.dart:175-178 `final rest = _drivingClock.restUntil; if (rest != null) { IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.restUntil(clockLabel(rest))); return true; }`
failure_scenario: Driver A is online for 12 h (or some hours), logs out from Profile, and driver B signs in on the same phone. B's Home shows A's 'time left to drive'. If A reached the limit, B taps the radar and is refused with 'Rest until 04:30' although B has not driven at all.
suggested_fix: Call DrivingTimeClock.instance.reset() in _logout, and put every per-driver in-memory store behind one reset hook that logout calls.

title: Logout leaves the previous driver's scheduled rides in ScheduledRideStore; 'Leave now' then opens driver A's reservation as driver B's active trip
description: ScheduledRideStore keeps _requests, _accepted, _lateCancels, reminder and backupNote in static memory (scheduled_rides.dart). Its only reset is @visibleForTesting (scheduled_rides.dart:706-707) and logout never calls it. After logout, the next DriverHome's _startScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:66-74) plans the old driver's accepted ride. _planScheduled -> _leaveNow -> _startScheduledTrip (home_scheduled.dart:218-239) removes it from the store and opens it through _openOfferTrip as the new driver's active trip, or gives it to a backup with a 'went to a backup driver' note. Driver A's late cancels also stay, so pausedUntil() can block scheduled rides for driver B. The accepted rows hold rider names and pickup addresses, so this is also a privacy leak.
evidence: scheduled_rides.dart:706-707 `@visibleForTesting static void reset() { _requests..clear()..addAll(_seedRequests()); _accepted..clear()..addAll(_seedAccepted()); ... _lateCancels.clear();` (never called from lib/); home_scheduled.dart:157-161 `if (state.lateSince != null || !now.isBefore(start)) { _leaveNow(ride); } else { at(start, () => _leaveNow(ride)); }`; home_scheduled.dart:233-237 `final offer = RideOffer.reservation(ride); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide);`
failure_scenario: Driver A accepts a reservation for 08:15 and logs out. Driver B signs in and goes online. At A's leave time, B's Home shows 'Leave now' and opens A's reservation, with A's rider name and address, as B's trip. If B is offline, the island says 'Head to your 08:15 pickup' and later 'given to backup'. If A had made late cancels, Scheduled rides are paused for B.
suggested_fix: Expose a non-test ScheduledRideStore reset (or a logout hook) and call it from _logout, together with cancelling Home's scheduled timers.

title: Logout keeps the previous driver's notifications and document-renewal state (DriverNotificationFeed, DocumentExpiryStore)
description: DriverNotificationFeed.instance and DocumentExpiryStore.instance are process singletons, and both have reset() methods ('Back to the demo list at the next reading'). No code in lib/ calls them, and _logout does not. Notifications that Home adds while driver A works stay in the feed for driver B: scheduled-ride reminders carrying the pickup address (home_scheduled.dart:271-282), Exclusive offers, rest-over notices. A's read/unread state stays too. A's document uploads ('in review' via uploadNew) and approvals stay in DocumentExpiryStore, so B's Documents screen, the going-online block and the island hold show A's document status. The test harness resets both before every test (flutter_test_config.dart:65-68) because they are per-driver state.
evidence: driver_notifications.dart:170 `void reset() { _items = null; _read.clear(); _popups.clear(); arrivals = DriverNotices.demoArrivals; ...}`; document_expiry.dart:190 `void reset() { _documents = null; _warned.clear(); _changes.value++; }`; neither is called from lib/ (grep). home_scheduled.dart:272-280 adds `DriverNotices.scheduledReminder(at: feed.now, title: title, body: body /* ride.pickupAddress */ ...)`
failure_scenario: Driver A gets 'Head to your 08:15 pickup · Södermalm, Stockholm' and uploads a new insurance letter (now 'in review'), then logs out. Driver B opens Notifications and sees A's reminders with A's rider pickup addresses, already marked read. B's Documents screen shows A's insurance in review.
suggested_fix: Call DriverNotificationFeed.instance.reset() and DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset() from _logout.

title: Cash-rides switch, missed-Exclusive counter and destination-mode daily uses survive logout and apply to the next driver
description: DriverOfferPreferences.acceptsCash and ExclusiveAnswers.instance._missedInRow (offer_rules.dart:203-256) and DestinationModeSession.instance._started (destination_mode_session.dart:11-47) are static and only reset by tests (flutter_test_config.dart:62,76). After logout, driver B inherits A's cash-off choice, so _offerAllowed/_rideAllowed (home_offer_rules.dart:11-22) silently filter every cash offer. B also inherits A's missed-in-row count, so with the default limit B can be sent offline after their very first missed Exclusive (_exclusiveMissed, home_offer_rules.dart:65-77). A's destinations set today count against B's daily limit, and refusal() returns usedToday. The known finding about DriverCategoryChoice covers only the category filter, not these.
evidence: offer_rules.dart:206-213 `static final ValueNotifier<bool> acceptsCash = ValueNotifier<bool>(true); @visibleForTesting static void reset() { acceptsCash.value = true; ExclusiveAnswers.instance.reset(); }`; destination_mode_session.dart:34-36 `if (r.dailyLimitOn && usedToday() >= r.destinationsPerDay) { return DestinationRefusal.usedToday; }`; main.dart:180-195 resets none of them
failure_scenario: Driver A turns Cash rides off, misses two Exclusive offers and uses today's destinations, then logs out. Driver B signs in. B never receives cash trips (the sheet shows Cash off), is sent offline after one missed Exclusive, and tapping destination search shows 'destinations used today'.
suggested_fix: Reset DriverOfferPreferences (non-test API), ExclusiveAnswers.instance and DestinationModeSession.instance in _logout.

title: Denying the location prompt on Android re-prompts at once (and on Android 10 and below in a loop) because every resume calls requestPermission again
description: On first launch, initState calls _startDriverLocation, then getCurrentPosition, then _ensurePermission, which calls Geolocator.requestPermission() when the status is denied (driver_location_service.dart:115-118). The Android permission dialog is a separate activity, so the Flutter activity pauses and reports inactive. didChangeAppLifecycleState marks Home not foreground and bumps _locationEpoch. When the driver taps Deny, the app resumes and _resumeHomeUpdates calls _startDriverLocation again, which calls requestPermission again and shows the dialog again. On Android 10 and below a plain Deny never becomes deniedForever, so this repeats until the driver ticks 'Don't ask again' or allows. If the epoch did not change, the catch branch (home_map_sheet.dart:49-55) calls _listenToDriverLocation -> watchPosition -> _ensurePermission and asks a second time anyway. The known inactive-as-offline finding is about rendering, not this re-prompt.
evidence: home.dart:188-190 `_foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed; if (_liveVisible) { _resumeHomeUpdates(); } else { _pauseHomeUpdates(); }`; home.dart:207 `unawaited(_HomeMapSheet(this)._startDriverLocation());`; driver_location_service.dart:115-118 `var permission = await Geolocator.checkPermission(); if (permission == LocationPermission.denied) { permission = await Geolocator.requestPermission(); }`; home_map_sheet.dart:55 `_listenToDriverLocation();` in the catch, and watchPosition (driver_location_service.dart:92) calls _ensurePermission again
failure_scenario: New install on an Android phone: Home asks for location, the driver taps Deny, and the same system dialog appears again right away. On Android 10, Deny -> dialog -> Deny -> dialog repeats with no way out except allowing or ticking 'Don't ask again'.
suggested_fix: Request permission only on an explicit user action (first launch once, Go online, Recenter). Use a check-only path for resume and for the fallback stream.

title: Fallback location subscription after a failed first fix cannot recover; on web, granting location later leaves Home without GPS
description: The catch branch in _startDriverLocation says 'Continuous updates can recover when permissions/provider return' and calls _listenToDriverLocation. But DriverLocationService.watchPosition is an async* generator that first awaits _ensurePermission. When permission is denied or location services are off, that throws, the stream emits one error and closes. The onError handler only sets _startLocationFailed and does not resubscribe. Nothing retries until a lifecycle resume, a Recenter tap or Go online. On web, enabling location in the browser's site settings fires no lifecycle event, so Home keeps the grey GPS dot and no car.
evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:52-55 `// Continuous updates can recover when permissions/provider return. _listenToDriverLocation();`; driver_location_service.dart:91-97 `Stream<DriverLocation> watchPosition(...) async* { await _ensurePermission(); yield* Geolocator.getPositionStream(...)`; home_map_sheet.dart:74-77 onError only `_rebuild(() { _hasLiveDriverLocation = false; _startLocationFailed = true; });`
failure_scenario: Web/PWA first launch: the driver blocks location, then allows it from the address-bar permission icon. Home stays without a car and with a grey GPS indicator until they tap Recenter or go online.
suggested_fix: Retry the location subscription with backoff after an error (or listen to permission changes), or correct the comment and offer an explicit retry.

title: When the device's storage cannot be opened, recovery never resolves and the driver can never go online; the app says there is a saved trip that does not exist
description: _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded runs CompletionJournal.reconcile() and repo.read(). Both call SharedPreferences.getInstance(), which throws when the browser blocks localStorage (Safari 'Block all cookies', some private modes). Any non-ActiveRideUnreadable error lands in the generic catch, which shows 'The saved trip could not be opened' and leaves _recoveryResolved false. _goOnline refuses while !_recoveryResolved and shows 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online' with 'Open saved trip', which only retries the same failing read. On a first launch with no storage there is no saved trip, yet the driver is blocked from going online for the whole session.
evidence: home.dart:519-525 `} catch (_) { _didAttemptActiveRideRestore = false; if(mounted) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryFailed, tr.savedTripCouldNotBeOpened); } return; }`; home.dart:890-895 `if(!_recoveryResolved) { _HomeMapSheet(this)._tripProblem(HomeIslandNotices.recoveryPending, tr.finishOrCloseSavedTripBefore, action: tr.openSavedTrip); return; }`; prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:71 `final prefs = await _load();`
failure_scenario: Fresh install opened in a browser with site storage blocked: Home shows 'The saved trip could not be opened'. Every radar tap answers 'Finish or close the saved trip before going online', and 'Open saved trip' fails again. The driver can never go online.
suggested_fix: Tell 'storage unavailable' apart from 'a saved trip exists but failed'. When the store cannot be opened, nothing can be recovered: resolve recovery (with a warning) instead of blocking going online.

title: Logout leaves Ride-check audio recordings of trips on the phone
description: NativeRideCheckRecorder writes in-trip audio (rider and driver voices) to <documents>/ride_check_audio/<id>.m4a. clearLocalUserData removes the Ride-check log rows that point at those files but never deletes the directory. The logout dialog says local data on this device will be cleared. Afterwards the recordings stay on disk, orphaned, with no UI to reach or delete them, and they keep piling up across drivers on a shared phone.
evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio'); ... path: '${directory.path}/$recordingId.m4a'`; local_data.dart:123-151 removes only SharedPreferences keys; app_en.arb profLogOutClears: 'Local preview data on this device will be cleared, including trip history, contacts, and drafts.'
failure_scenario: Driver A records audio during a Ride check, then logs out and hands the phone to driver B. The .m4a files of A's trip stay in the app's documents folder (and in device backups) with no reference left and no way to remove them from the app.
suggested_fix: Delete the ride_check_audio directory in clearLocalUserData (native only), or record in LOCAL_DATA.md that recordings survive logout and give the driver a delete action.

title: A brand-new (or newly signed-in) driver sees invented earnings on the island: 'Last trip 126 kr' and 'TODAY 183.25 kr'
description: _lastTripFareLabel falls back to DigitalIslandParts.sampleLastTrip when there is no last trip, and the Today face always shows the constant sampleToday. On first install, or right after logout when _waybills.reset() cleared the last trip, tapping the island shows a last-trip and today total the driver never earned. After real trips, 'Last trip' shows the real fare while 'Today' stays fixed at 183.25 kr. The sample uses a '.' decimal ('183.25 kr'), while Money formats '104,80 kr' (DECISIONS D6), so the two faces disagree in format too.
evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:1347-1350 `final fare = _waybills.last?.fare; if (fare == null || !fare.contains(RegExp(r'\d'))) { return DigitalIslandParts.sampleLastTrip; }`; home_map_sheet.dart:1223-1224 `DigitalIslandParts.amountFace('island-today', tr.todayCaps, DigitalIslandParts.sampleToday)`; digital_island.dart:674-675 `sampleToday = '183.25 kr'; sampleLastTrip = '126 kr';`
failure_scenario: New install, first Home: the driver taps the island and reads 'LAST TRIP 126 kr', then 'TODAY 183.25 kr', with zero trips driven. After logout, the next driver sees the same invented amounts.
suggested_fix: Show an empty/zero state ('No trips yet', '0,00 kr') when there is no last trip, and compute Today from local history or mark it clearly as sample.

title: Create account: Continue works with the Terms/Privacy checkbox unticked
description: isAccept is toggled by the checkbox but never read by the Continue button, which always pushes DriverCreateAccountPhone. In the legacy registration flow (MOVERA_ENABLE_LEGACY_AUTH), a driver can sign up without accepting the Terms of use and Privacy policy that the screen asks them to accept.
evidence: create_acc.dart:44 `bool isAccept = false;`; create_acc.dart:174-181 `CustomButton(centerContent: tr.navContinue, onPressed: () { Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverCreateAccountPhone())); },)`
failure_scenario: Legacy registration build: the driver leaves 'By continuing I agree to Terms of use and Privacy policy' unticked, taps Continue and moves on to phone entry.
suggested_fix: Disable Continue (onPressed: isAccept ? ... : null) until the checkbox is ticked.

title: System Back during onboarding leaves the whole flow instead of going to the previous step
description: The on-screen back arrow calls controller.moveToPreviousStep, which goes back one PageView step. The route has no PopScope, so Android system Back or the iOS back swipe pops AdditionalInfoNavigation from any step. The driver is thrown out of vehicle onboarding, and the controller (with its pages) is disposed. The known finding at line 139 is about losing fields when moving forward, not this.
evidence: navigation.dart:117-131 `return Scaffold(body: ... IconButton(tooltip: tr.back, onPressed: () => controller.moveToPreviousStep(context), ...` with no PopScope/WillPopScope around the Scaffold; navigation.dart:68-74 moveToPreviousStep only pops the route at index 0
failure_scenario: Legacy onboarding on Android: the driver is on step 3 (Insurance) and presses system Back expecting step 2. The whole onboarding closes back to sign-in, and the vehicle details and documents are lost.
suggested_fix: Wrap the Scaffold in PopScope(canPop: currentPageIndex == 0, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) controller.moveToPreviousStep(context); }).

title: Phone entry screens default to the United States (+1) in the Swedish market
description: All three phone screens (sign-in phone, create account, create account phone) set the default country to US/+1, with a comment saying so. The market is SEK/Stockholm (DECISIONS P2) and the account country is 'SE' (DriverAccountRules.country), so every Swedish driver must change the country before entering a +46 number.
evidence: sign_in_phone.dart:30-33 `// Set default country (United States) selectedCountry = CountryPickerUtils.getCountryByIsoCode('US'); selectedCountryCode = '+1';`; same in create_acc.dart:33-34 and create_acc_phone.dart:33-34; driver_account_rules.dart `this.country = 'SE'`
failure_scenario: Legacy sign-up in Sweden: the phone field shows the US flag, and a number typed as '070…' would be taken as +1.
suggested_fix: Default to the zone's country (DriverAccountRules.current.country).

title: 'Continue with Apple/Google' opens vehicle onboarding as if sign-in succeeded, with no sign-in at all
description: Both social buttons push AdditionalInfoNavigation directly. No auth runs and nothing says it is unavailable, unlike the phone path, which shows 'phone sign-in needs a service'. REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES 'Product truth gate' says production authentication is not connected and the UI must not claim such actions succeeded.
evidence: sign_in.dart:79-85 `centerContent: tr.continueWithApple, onPressed: () { Navigator.push(context, BottomToTopTransition(const AdditionalInfoNavigation())); },` and sign_in.dart:98-104 the same for Google
failure_scenario: Legacy auth build: the driver taps 'Continue with Google' and lands on 'Add vehicle step 1 of 4' as if signed in, although no Google account was used.
suggested_fix: Disable the social buttons or show the same 'needs a service' message as phone sign-in.

title: Home Radar cards and the Exclusive sheet never show the CASH badge in Swedish or French
description: _radarOfferView turns the offer's wire payment into the display word before building the RadarOfferView: `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment`. RadarOfferView then works out the cash flag from that same string: `bool get cash => isCash(payment);` with `isCash(String payment) => payment.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash'` (lib/widgets/radar_offer_card.dart:87-89). In sv tr.cash is 'Kontant' and in fr it is 'Espèces', so `offer.cash` comes out false. Both Home surfaces gate the badge on it: RadarOfferCard `if (show.badges && offer.cash) OfferBadge.cash(...)` (radar_offer_card.dart:224) and ExclusiveRequestSheet `if (show.badges && offer.cash)` (exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80). RadarOfferView.payment is used nowhere else, so swapping in tr.cash has no visible benefit. The Radar list screen passes the raw value (`payment: offer.payment`, ride_requests.dart:164/730) and keeps the badge, so the two lists disagree. The Swedish zone defaults to sv, so most drivers are affected.
failure_scenario: The app is in Svenska (the Stockholm zone default) or the driver switches to Français. A cash offer reaches Home (demo dispatch offers have payment: 'Cash'). The Radar card and the Exclusive sheet show no CASH chip, so the driver accepts without knowing they must collect cash. In English the same offer shows the chip.
evidence:
home_offer_radar.dart:1052  `payment: offer.cash ? tr.cash : offer.payment,`
radar_offer_card.dart:87-89  `bool get cash => isCash(payment);` / `static bool isCash(String payment) => payment.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash';`
radar_offer_card.dart:224  `if (show.badges && offer.cash)`
exclusive_request_sheet.dart:80  `if (show.badges && offer.cash)`
app_sv.arb:94 `"cash": "Kontant"`, app_fr.arb:94 `"cash": "Espèces"`
suggested_fix: Pass the raw `offer.payment` (or carry the bool) into RadarOfferView and translate only where a payment word is displayed.

title: Trip source (matchedVia) is saved in the display language, so fr/sv scheduled rides lose their scheduled waiting terms and the waybill 'Via' row freezes in the old language
description: Home opens trips with a translated matchedVia: `_openOfferTrip(..., tr.scheduledRide)` (Leave now, home_scheduled.dart:234-237), `offer.reservation ? tr.exclusiveReservation : tr.exclusiveOffer` (home_offer_radar.dart:835-838) and `ExclusiveReasons.text(ExclusiveReasons.assigned)` = tr.assignedByMovera (home_offer_radar.dart:860). This string is (a) persisted in the active-ride snapshot (`matchedVia: widget.matchedVia`, accept_ride_trip.dart:28), (b) used as the waybill `source` (accept_ride_trip.dart:188), and (c) parsed by WaitingRules.typeOf, which looks only for English substrings: `if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation'))` (waiting_rules.dart:251). In sv the strings are 'Bokad resa' and 'Exklusiv bokning'. In fr they are 'Course planifiée' and 'Réservation exclusive'; 'réservation' with an accent does not contain 'reservation'. So in fr/sv every scheduled ride falls back to WaitingRideType.normal. The 'Scheduled ride' rule (free wait = ScheduledRideRules.includedWaitingMinutes) is not applied, and the waiting sheet's 'Rule for this pickup: Scheduled ride' line is missing. WaybillRecord.sourceText maps only the English constants (waybill.dart:70-75), even though waybill.dart:45-46 says stored values 'stay in English in storage'. A localized source is therefore shown as written, in the language that was active when the trip opened.
failure_scenario: In Svenska, the driver accepts an XL reservation. The XL rule gives 3 free minutes and a no-show at 3 min. The scheduled rule would raise the free wait to 5 min, and the no-show then follows it to 5 min. In English the trip gets 5 free minutes and a no-show at 5 min. In Swedish, the paid wait (12.26 kr/min) starts and the no-show option appears at minute 3. The same happens for any category once admin sets a different reservation included wait. Separately, a driver who accepts in sv and switches to fr mid-trip sees 'Via: Bokad resa' on the waybill.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:234-237  `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide,);`
home_offer_radar.dart:837  `offer.reservation ? tr.exclusiveReservation : tr.exclusiveOffer,`
accept_ride.dart:989-994  `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: widget.category, type: WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...`
waiting_rules.dart:250-252  `final via = matchedVia.toLowerCase(); if (via.contains('scheduled') || via.contains('reservation')) { return WaitingRideType.scheduled; }`
app_sv.arb:57 `"scheduledRide": "Bokad resa"`, app_fr.arb:90 `"exclusiveReservation": "Réservation exclusive"`
suggested_fix: Pass a language-neutral source id (e.g. WaybillRecord constants 'Scheduled ride'/'Exclusive reservation'), or an enum, as matchedVia. Map it to tr.* only in WaybillRecord.sourceText, and derive the waiting type from the id or from offer.reservation, not from text.

title: Island strip says 'Prise en charge côté left' / 'Upphämtning på left sida': the English 'left'/'right' goes into the localized pickup-side message
description: _stripInput sets `pickupSide: b?.symbol == NavigationBannerSymbol.arriveLeft ? 'left' : ... 'right'`. TripStripController passes it straight into the localized template: `_say(tr.pickupOnPickupSideSide(next.pickupSide!))` (trip_island_controller.dart:351). The fr template is 'Prise en charge côté {pickupSide}' and the sv one is 'Upphämtning på {pickupSide} sida'. Neither language has a translation for the side word. This is not the known '<stop> next' finding at trip_island_controller.dart:322.
failure_scenario: In French or Swedish, while heading to pickup, the route's arrive step has modifier left or right (arriveLeft/arriveRight symbol). The island strip shows 'Prise en charge côté left' or 'Upphämtning på right sida'.
evidence:
adaptive_trip_island.dart:277-281  `pickupSide: b?.symbol == NavigationBannerSymbol.arriveLeft ? 'left' : b?.symbol == NavigationBannerSymbol.arriveRight ? 'right' : null,`
trip_island_controller.dart:351  `_say(tr.pickupOnPickupSideSide(next.pickupSide!));`
app_fr.arb:526 `"pickupOnPickupSideSide": "Prise en charge côté {pickupSide}"`
app_sv.arb:526 `"pickupOnPickupSideSide": "Upphämtning på {pickupSide} sida"`
suggested_fix: Add two messages (pickupOnLeftSide / pickupOnRightSide), or translate the side word, and pick one from the enum.

title: Ride completed and History detail show the raw English 'Cash'/'Card' as the payment method in fr/sv
description: The trip screen passes the language-neutral `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card'` to DriverRideCompleted (accept_ride_trip.dart:966) and journals `'Cash'` for cash trips (accept_ride_trip.dart:916). Storing English is correct, because TripHistoryRecord.paidByCash compares with 'cash'. But both screens display the stored word without translating it: `_row(tr.payment, Text(widget.paymentMethod ?? '—'))` and `_detailRow(tr.paymentMethod, _ride.paymentMethod, paymentIcon: true)` (history_detail.dart:420). tr.cash ('Kontant'/'Espèces') and tr.inApp exist but are not used here.
failure_scenario: The driver uses Svenska and finishes a cash trip. Ride completed shows 'Betalning: Cash'. Ride history › trip detail shows 'Betalningsmetod Cash'. A card trip shows 'Card' on Ride completed.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:966  `paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : 'Card',`
ride_completed.dart:215  `_row(tr.payment, Text(widget.paymentMethod ?? '—',`
history_detail.dart:420  `_detailRow(tr.paymentMethod, _ride.paymentMethod, paymentIcon: true),`
suggested_fix: Map the stored id to tr.cash / tr.inApp when displaying it, and keep the stored value in English.

title: 'New scheduled ride' notification body uses the raw English pickup day ('Today 07:40 · … · Tryck för att visa')
description: When the reservation sheet rises, Home adds a notification with `day: request.pickupDay`. pickupDay is the stored English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' (driver_home_admin_content.dart:492). DriverNotices.newScheduledRide passes it unchanged into `tr.noticeScheduledBody(day, time, fare)`. Elsewhere the code translates the day with `ReservationWhen.dayWord(request.pickupDay)` (reservation_route_map.dart:427). This is a separate surface from the known Scheduled-rides-card finding (scheduled_rides.dart:1134).
failure_scenario: The app is in Swedish and the demo reservation sheet rises on Home. Notifications shows 'Ny bokad resa · Today 07:40 · 126.75 kr · Tryck för att visa'.
evidence:
home_reservation.dart:212-217  `DriverNotices.newScheduledRide(at: feed.now, day: request.pickupDay, time: request.pickupTime, fare: request.fare,)`
driver_notifications.dart:202  `body: tr.noticeScheduledBody(day, time, fare),`
app_sv.arb:1289 `"noticeScheduledBody": "{day} {time} · {fare} · Tryck för att visa"`
suggested_fix: Pass `ReservationWhen.dayWord(request.pickupDay)` (or ReservationWhen.ofRequest(...).label).

title: Ride check reason is saved to local storage in the display language, unlike its answers, so Trip details mix languages after a switch
description: RideCheckRecord answers and questions are saved as English keys and translated when shown (rideCheckAnswerWords / rideCheckQuestionWords in ride_check_l10n.dart). The reason, however, is saved as rendered text: `reason: event.reason.text`. The text is built from tr.rcStoppedLead, tr.rcMinutes, tr.rcLongerLead and so on in RideCheckDetector. PrefsRideCheckLog persists it (`'reason': reason`, ride_check.dart:298), and History shows it as stored: `'${check.trigger.text} · ${check.reason}'` (ride_check_history_entry.dart:117). The trigger is translated when shown; the reason is frozen in the language of the trip.
failure_scenario: A Ride check fires mid-trip while the app is in Swedish. Later the driver switches to French and opens the trip in History. The line reads '<French trigger> · Bilen har stått stilla i 4 min' while the answers below are in French.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:120-126  `_record = RideCheckRecord(... trigger: event.trigger, reason: event.reason.text, openedAt: event.at,);`
ride_check_detector.dart (longStopReason)  `RideCheckReason(tr.rcStoppedLead, tr.rcMinutes(minutes), ...)`
ride_check_history_entry.dart:117  `'${check.trigger.text} · ${check.reason}',`
suggested_fix: Store the trigger with its numbers (minutes, metres, percent, place) and build the reason when it is displayed, as the answers already are.

title: Waybill driver, vehicle and plate (and placeholder rider name) are saved in the language active at trip start and shown unchanged after a language switch
description: waybill.dart:45-46 states that stored waybill values 'stay in English in storage; the screens show them in the driver's language'. The trip screen nevertheless fills the record with translated text: `driverName: tr.moveraDriver`, `vehicle: _vehicleLabel` and `licensePlate: _vehiclePlate`, whose defaults are `tr.vehicleDataUnavailable` / `tr.plateUnavailable` (accept_ride.dart:553-554). Home's restore does the same: `riderName: snapshot.riderName ?? tr.riderDataUnavailable, driverName: tr.demoDriverIdentityUnavailable, vehicle: tr.vehicleDataUnavailable, licensePlate: tr.plateUnavailable` (home.dart:631-637, 653-655). waybill_sheet.dart:84-85 prints these fields as stored. The same frozen strings go into the safety alert (accept_ride_trip.dart:1468). AcceptRide.fromPersisted also turns a missing riderName into `tr.riderDataUnavailable` (accept_ride.dart:257), and that text is then persisted as if it were the rider's name.
failure_scenario: The driver accepts a trip in Svenska, switches to Français from the trip's side menu › Settings, and opens the current-trip waybill. All labels are in French but 'Chauffeur: Movera-förare'. Without a saved vehicle it also shows 'Fordonsuppgifter saknas' / 'Registreringsnummer saknas'. The Ride completed 'last waybill' shows the same mix.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:189-191  `driverName: tr.moveraDriver, vehicle: _vehicleLabel, licensePlate: _vehiclePlate,`
accept_ride.dart:553-554  `String _vehicleLabel = tr.vehicleDataUnavailable; String _vehiclePlate = tr.plateUnavailable;`
home.dart:635-637  `driverName: tr.demoDriverIdentityUnavailable, vehicle: tr.vehicleDataUnavailable, licensePlate: tr.plateUnavailable,`
waybill_sheet.dart:84  `_Row(tr.driver, record.driverName),`
suggested_fix: Store null or a sentinel for unknown values, store the brand driver name as a constant id, and translate in waybill_sheet.

title: Notifications made while the app runs (exclusive offer, new scheduled ride, reminders, Leave now, rest over, document approved, scheduled paused) keep the old language
description: DriverNotice holds only rendered strings: title, body, island and actionLabel. Every DriverNotices factory renders them with tr at add time, for example `title: tr.noticeNewScheduledRide, body: tr.noticeScheduledBody(day, time, fare), island: driverText(...), actionLabel: tr.view`. Home's _noteRideAlert passes already-rendered `tr.pickupTimePickupInLeft(...)` / `tr.leaveNowForPickupTimePickup(...)` (home_scheduled.dart:266, 228-231). The feed keeps these objects for the session, and the screen renders `notice.title` / `notice.body` directly (driver_notifications_screen.dart:256/280). The known document_expiry.dart:110 finding covers the cached demo list; this one is the runtime notices.
failure_scenario: While in Swedish, the driver gets an Exclusive offer and a 'Leave now' reminder, then switches to French. The Notifications screen still lists 'Exklusivt erbjudande · 8 s att acceptera' and 'Åk nu till upphämtningen 14:00' with a 'Visa' button, under a French header.
evidence:
driver_notifications.dart:201-206  `title: tr.noticeNewScheduledRide, body: tr.noticeScheduledBody(day, time, fare), at: at, island: driverText(DriverTexts.islandNewReservation), action: ..., actionLabel: tr.view,`
driver_notifications.dart:214-215  `title: tr.exclusiveOffer, body: tr.noticeSecondsToAccept(seconds),`
home_scheduled.dart:266  `_noteRideAlert(tr.pickupTimePickupInLeft(ride.pickupTime, left), ride.pickupAddress);`
suggested_fix: Store the notice kind and its arguments, and render the title, body and action label with tr when they are displayed.

title: Scheduled rides reminder/backup notes and ride card time/distance strings are frozen in the language they were made in
description: ScheduledRideStore.reminder and backupNote are static ValueNotifier<String?> that hold rendered text: `tr.pickupAtPickupTimeInLeft(...)`, `tr.headToYourPickupTimePickup(...)`, `tr.goOnlineNowForYourPickup(...)` (home_scheduled.dart:198, 264, 287) and `tr.schedBackupNote(ride.pickupTime)` (scheduled_rides.dart:647). The Scheduled rides screen shows them under translated titles (tr.reminder / tr.islandGivenToBackup). Each _ScheduledRide also caches `time: tr.schedSeedTime(...)` and `distance: driverDistanceKm(...)` once, in the static store that lives for the whole app run (scheduled_rides.dart:1117-1119, 1134-1144). The sv template is '{day} {time}' while en/fr use '{day}, {time}', so the cards keep the first language's format.
failure_scenario: In English, a '1 h before pickup' reminder fires. The driver switches to Swedish and opens Scheduled rides › Accepted. The note titled 'Påminnelse' still reads 'Pickup at 14:00 in 1 h · …', and the cards keep 'Today, 07:40–07:45'.
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart:264-265  `ScheduledRideStore.reminder.value = tr.pickupAtPickupTimeInLeft(ride.pickupTime, left, ride.pickupAddress);`
scheduled_rides.dart:647-648  `backupNote.value = tr.schedBackupNote(ride.pickupTime);`
scheduled_rides.dart:1134  `var time = tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime);`
suggested_fix: Store the ride and the reminder kind/minutes, and format the text in build.

title: The GPS-lost status keeps the old language after a switch, and the 'GPS restored' notice is then skipped
description: When the GPS stream errors, the trip saves the rendered text both in `_locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis` and in NavigationController `_locationWarning` (keepLastKnown, navigation_controller.dart:298). Both stay until a usable fix arrives. Covering the trip with Settings does not pause GPS (live updates pause only on app lifecycle, accept_ride.dart:713-726), so returning does not refresh the text, and the island keeps showing the old-language warning. When GPS comes back, TripIslandController decides whether to say 'GPS restored' by comparing the stored old-language text with the new language: `fault == tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis || fault.contains('Location')`. Neither test matches a Swedish string while the app is in French, so the notice is never shown.
failure_scenario: In Swedish, GPS drops during the trip and the island shows 'Platsen uppdateras…'. The driver switches to French via the side menu and returns. The island still shows Swedish, and when the fix returns the island goes straight back to guidance without 'GPS rétabli'.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:614-617  `_navigation.keepLastKnown(status: tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis); _rebuild(() { _hasLiveLocation = false; _locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis; });`
navigation_controller.dart:298  `_locationWarning = status ?? tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis;`
trip_island_controller.dart:96-97  `static bool _isLocationFault(String fault) => fault == tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis || fault.contains('Location');`
suggested_fix: Keep the warning as an enum or flag (as NavigationRouteStatus does) and render it with tr when building the status; test the enum, not the text.

title: Waiting sheet 'Rule for this pickup' label stays in the language the trip opened in
description: WaitingTerms.rule is built when the terms are worked out, from translated labels: `_shown(label)` (tr.waitingRule*) and `label: tr.pickupOverKmKm(km)`. AcceptRide caches the terms in `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms` (accept_ride.dart:989) and the static `WaitingTerms.active` (accept_ride.dart:612). waiting_time_sheet.dart:173 shows `tr.ruleForThisPickupRule(terms.rule)`, so after a switch the sheet prints a new-language prefix with an old-language rule.
failure_scenario: The driver accepts a far pickup (> 5 km) in Swedish, switches to French mid-trip and opens the waiting sheet at pickup. It shows 'Règle pour cette prise en charge : Upphämtning över 5 km'.
evidence:
waiting_rules.dart:230  `terms = terms._with(farPickup, label: tr.pickupOverKmKm(km));`
waiting_rules.dart:91-93  `rule: [ if (this.rule.isNotEmpty) this.rule, if ((label ?? rule.label).isNotEmpty) _shown(label ?? rule.label), ].join(' · '),`
accept_ride.dart:989  `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(`
waiting_time_sheet.dart:173  `tr.ruleForThisPickupRule(terms.rule),`
suggested_fix: Keep the rule ids (and the km value) in WaitingTerms and translate them in the sheet.

title: An Exclusive next-trip offer opens and runs out behind Chat, Support or Notifications, and counts as a miss that can send the driver offline
description: D-05 (comment at line 122) says no next-trip offer comes or runs out while the driver cannot see the trip. The only guard is _liveUpdatesPaused, and only didChangeAppLifecycleState sets it. AcceptRide is not route-aware. Several screens are pushed as opaque routes over the live trip: Chat (accept_ride_panel.dart:861, BottomToTopTransition opaque=true), the trip drawer's Support, Notifications and Scheduled rides, and the destination picker. While one of them is open, GPS fixes keep calling _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer (line 685). After 2.2 s, _presentOnTripOffer shows the offer on the hidden trip screen and _armOnTripOfferExpiry starts the full accept time (15 s by default). When that runs out, _denyNextTripRadar sets _onTripRadarDeclined = true, so no further offers come on this trip, and it calls ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed().
failure_scenario: On a trip with Radar scanning, inside the next-trip radius, the driver taps the message icon to chat with the rider. 2.2 s later an Exclusive offer opens under the Chat route, and 15 s later it expires unseen. The driver comes back to no offer and Radar declined for the rest of the trip. One more miss is counted, and at admin's autoOfflineAfter count the driver goes offline after this trip with the 'offline after N missed' message.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:122 '// D-05: no next-trip offer comes or runs out while the driver cannot see the trip'; :1123-1124 '// D-05: never while the trip is hidden; the resume looks again. if (_liveUpdatesPaused) { return; }'; :1168-1172 '_nextTripOfferExpiry = Timer(time, () { ... _denyNextTripRadar(); });'; :1219 '_onTripRadarDeclined = true;'; :1226 'if (ExclusiveAnswers.instance.missed()) { widget.sessionController?.setOnline(false); ...'; accept_ride.dart:715-727 (the only place that pauses live updates is the app lifecycle).
suggested_fix: Make AcceptRide a RouteAware subscriber of driverRouteObserver, as Home is. In didPushNext, hold the offer (pause its deadline, as _pauseLiveUpdates does) and do not present new ones; in didPopNext, resume with the time left.

title: Home island takes and plays posted messages while it is covered by the trip, Scheduled rides or another route, so they are never seen
description: IslandMessages is documented as 'Messages waiting for the Home island. Any screen can post one'. Home's listener _onIslandMessagesChanged calls _showNextIslandMessage, which checks only mounted and whether a message is already showing, never whether Home is visible (_liveVisible / _routeVisible). didPushNext pauses GPS and offers but not the island queue. So a message posted while another route covers Home is taken from the queue, shown on the hidden island for 2 to 4.5 s, and dropped. Real posters during the journey: AcceptRide's offlineAfterMissed (accept_ride_trip.dart:1228, posted while the trip screen covers Home), demo arrival and document popups through _showNoticePopups (home_account.dart:237), and Scheduled rides' reservationAcceptedAt and reservationCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:235, 678). The trip island (AdaptiveTripIsland) never reads IslandMessages.
failure_scenario: During a trip the driver misses the Nth Exclusive offer. AcceptRide calls setOnline(false) and posts 'offline after N missed' (high priority). Home, under the trip route, consumes it at once and its 4.5 s timer ends it. After the trip the driver lands on Home, offline, with no explanation. In the same way, the 20 s 'High demand' and 50 s event popups and a 'Reservation accepted' confirmation play unseen under the trip or the Scheduled rides screen.
evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:1257-1268 'void _showNextIslandMessage() { if (!mounted || _islandMessage != null) { return; } final next = IslandMessages.take(); ... _islandMessageTimer = Timer(next.priority.duration, _endIslandMessage);'; home.dart:174 'void didPushNext() { _routeVisible = false; _pauseHomeUpdates(); }' (_pauseHomeUpdates does not touch the island queue); island_messages.dart:57 '/// Messages waiting for the Home island. Any screen can post one'; accept_ride_trip.dart:1228 'IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.offlineAfterMissed(...))'.
suggested_fix: In _onIslandMessagesChanged and _showNextIslandMessage, return early while !_liveVisible, and call _showNextIslandMessage from _resumeHomeUpdates, so queued messages wait until Home is on screen.

title: With a secured next trip, the hand-off pushReplacement replaces the Chat/Support route on top, not the trip, so the ended trip screen stays mounted under the new one
description: This is a separate call from the known Navigator.pop() finding at line 452, with a different consequence. When a rider cancels (line 472), or an authoritative terminal outcome arrives (line 382), and a next trip is secured, the code awaits the outcome sheet and then calls Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement(AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next)). pushReplacement replaces the navigator's top route. If the driver has Chat (pushSingle on the same navigator, accept_ride_panel.dart:861) or Support or Notifications from the trip drawer (rootNavigator) open, the route replaced is that screen, not the ended AcceptRide. The ended AcceptRide stays in the stack with its realtime subscription and its WidgetsBindingObserver. On app resume, its _resumeLiveUpdates has no terminal guard and restarts GPS, routing and resync for the dead trip. When the new trip later completes, it pushReplaces itself with DriverRideCompleted, and leaving that screen reveals the old cancelled trip screen, whose PopScope(canPop: false) blocks Back.
failure_scenario: On trip with a secured next trip, the driver opens Chat with the rider. The rider cancels, and 'Rider cancelled' appears over Chat; the driver taps OK. Chat is replaced by the next trip's AcceptRide. The cancelled trip's AcceptRide is still underneath and resumes GPS on every app resume. After the next trip finishes, the driver is returned to the stale cancelled trip screen and cannot leave it with Back.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:470-476 'if(next!=null) { _waybills.promoteNextToCurrent(); Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement(BottomToTopTransition(AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next, ...))); return; }'; accept_ride_trip.dart:380-386 same for authoritative outcomes; accept_ride_trip.dart:137-139 '_resumeLiveUpdates() { if (!_liveUpdatesPaused) { return; } _liveUpdatesPaused = false; ...' (no terminal check); accept_ride.dart:1107-1108 'PopScope( canPop: false,'.
suggested_fix: Replace the trip's own route: capture ModalRoute.of(context) and use navigator.replace(oldRoute: thisRoute, newRoute: ...), or first popUntil the trip route is current.

title: Support inbox card keeps the old preview after a reply is saved in the conversation
description: _Conversation.saveMessage changes widget.ticket.preview and saves it through onChanged (_saveTickets), but only the conversation calls setState. The inbox opens the conversation with pushSingle(...) and neither awaits it nor rebuilds when it returns. It is not RouteAware, and the inbox build does not depend on any InheritedWidget that changes on pop. Flutter caches the page under a ModalRoute, so _TicketCard keeps the preview String it was built with until something else rebuilds the inbox, for example tapping another ticket.
failure_scenario: In Support, the driver opens the ticket 'Fare wrong' (preview 'Rider paid cash'), saves the reply 'Here is the receipt', and taps Back. The card still shows 'Rider paid cash' although storage now holds the reply as the preview. Closing and reopening Support shows the correct text.
evidence: support_inbox.dart:427-437 'void _open(_Ticket ticket) { ... setState(() => ticket.unread = false); pushSingle(context, MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => _Conversation(ticket: ticket, onChanged: _saveTickets),),); }'; :675-678 'setState(() { widget.ticket.messages.add(message); widget.ticket.preview = text; });' (the conversation's setState, not the inbox's); :604-605 'Text( ticket.preview,'.
suggested_fix: await pushSingle(...) and then call setState(() {}) when mounted, or make the tickets a ValueNotifier that the list listens to.

title: Rider-contact message is hard-coded English in the chat app bar tooltip and SnackBar and on the trip's call button
description: RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage is a const English string. The chat app bar uses it as the call button's tooltip and SnackBar text, and the trip's Call rider button uses it for its SnackBar. Every other chat string around it is localized (tr.chatLocalDemo, tr.chatSaveLocally, tr.chatLocalNotSent, tr.callRider), and the sv/fr ARB files have no key for it.
failure_scenario: With the app in Swedish, the driver taps the phone icon in Chat or on the trip sheet and sees 'Rider phone contact is not connected in this demo.' in English. Screen readers announce the same English tooltip.
evidence: rider_contact.dart:9-10 'static const String unavailableMessage = 'Rider phone contact is not connected in this demo.';'; appbar.dart:57-59 'tooltip: RiderContactPolicy.available ? tr.callRider : RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage,'; appbar.dart:69 'content: Text(RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage),'; accept_ride_panel.dart:851 'content: const Text(RiderContactPolicy.unavailableMessage),'.
suggested_fix: Add a riderContactUnavailable ARB key and use tr.riderContactUnavailable at these three call sites; keep the const only for tests or remove it.

title: Logout does not reset the in-memory notification feed: the next driver sees the previous driver's notifications and read state
description: DriverNotificationFeed.instance is a process-wide singleton with a reset() method ('Back to the demo list'), but _logout never calls it. It does reset waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and the session. Notices added during the session stay in the feed after logout: documentExpiring for that driver's documents, newScheduledRide, scheduledReminder, scheduledPaused, documentApproved and exclusiveOffer. The read set stays too. arrivals was already emptied by takeArrivals, so the next session gets no demo arrivals.
failure_scenario: Driver A gets 'Driving licence expires in 3 days' and 'New scheduled ride · Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr', then logs out. Driver B signs in on the same phone without restarting the app, opens Notifications, and sees A's document and reservation notices, with A's read and unread state.
evidence: main.dart:179-195 '_logout() async { ... await clearLocalUserData(); MapTrafficSetting.reset(); DriverLanguage.reset(); ... _waybills.reset(); ... _safetyAlerts.reset(); _session.reset(); }'; driver_notifications.dart:169-176 'void reset() { _items = null; _read.clear(); _popups.clear(); arrivals = DriverNotices.demoArrivals; _changes.value++; }' (no caller in lib/).
suggested_fix: Call DriverNotificationFeed.instance.reset() in _logout (and in the profile fallback path that calls clearLocalUserData directly).

title: Notification time label says 'Yesterday' for anything 24 to 47 h old, even when it was two calendar days ago
description: noticeTimeLabel uses elapsed duration buckets: below 24 h it shows 'N h ago', and ago.inDays == 1 shows 'Yesterday'. 'Yesterday' is a calendar-day claim, but the code applies it to any 24 to 47 h elapsed span without comparing calendar dates. The seeded demo payout notice sits exactly 26 h back.
failure_scenario: At 01:00 on Oct 21 the payout notice is from 23:00 on Oct 19 (now minus 26 h). The Notifications screen labels it 'Yesterday' although it was the day before yesterday. The label also never refreshes while the screen stays open.
evidence: driver_notifications_screen.dart:175-181 'final ago = now.difference(at); ... if (ago.inHours < 24) { return tr.hoursAgo(ago.inHours); } if (ago.inDays == 1) { return tr.yesterday; } return tr.daysAgo(ago.inDays);'; driver_notifications.dart:350 'at: now.subtract(const Duration(days: 1, hours: 2)),'.
suggested_fix: Choose between 'Yesterday' and 'N days ago' by comparing local calendar dates (DateUtils.dateOnly) instead of elapsed hours.

title: The category the driver picks for a support ticket is thrown away when the ticket is saved
description: The draft form has a required-looking Category dropdown, and the choice is kept in the draft. When the driver saves, the ticket is built as _Ticket(subject, message, 'LOCAL DRAFT', false). _Ticket has no category field and toJson does not write one, and the draft is then reset to 'Trip & rider'. The chosen category exists nowhere once the ticket is saved, and the inbox and conversation never show it.
failure_scenario: The driver chooses 'Wallet & payments', enters a subject and message, and saves. The ticket is stored without the category and the draft category goes back to 'Trip & rider', so the input is lost and could never reach a support service.
evidence: support_inbox.dart:335-340 'final ticket = _Ticket( subject.text.trim(), message.text.trim(), 'LOCAL DRAFT', false, );'; :826-834 toJson writes subject, preview, status, unread and messages only; :394-398 the draft is reset to 'category': 'Trip & rider'.
suggested_fix: Add a category field to _Ticket and to its JSON (the validator already allows unknown keys), and show it on the card.

title: Chat's 'Save message locally' messages are only in widget memory and disappear when Chat is closed
description: The send button is labelled tr.chatSaveLocally ('Save message locally'), and each bubble says 'Local preview · not sent'. The messages live only in _ChatState._messages, a field of the route's State. Closing Chat with Back disposes it, and reopening Chat from the same trip shows an empty conversation. Nothing is saved locally, so the action label does not match what happens.
failure_scenario: During a trip the driver writes 'I'm at the north entrance' and taps 'Save message locally', then goes back to the map. Reopening Chat for the same rider shows no messages.
evidence: chat.dart:24 'final List<String> _messages = [];'; :55 '_messages.add(_messageController.text.trim());'; :149 'label: tr.chatSaveLocally,'; app_en.arb:2843 '"chatSaveLocally": "Save message locally"'.
suggested_fix: Keep the per-trip local messages in a store keyed by tripId (pass tripId to Chat), or relabel the action as preview-only.

title: Reservation day words ('Today'/'Tomorrow') are fixed when the reservation is built but read against the current date, so every reservation moves one day ahead at midnight
description: _DemoReservationSet._at (line 495) stamps each demo reservation with a relative day word ('Today'/'Tomorrow') worked out from the anchor date at the clock's first reading. The set is cached in the static DemoReservations._set, and ScheduledRideStore._requests/_accepted keep the same objects for the whole process. ReservationRequestPreview.pickupAt (lines 237-246) then reads that word against the date of whatever `now` it is given: DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset). Once the app stays open past midnight, 'Tomorrow 00:10' resolves to the day after the real pickup, and 'Today 17:00' (already passed) resolves to 17:00 on the new day. Admin-sent previews use the same relative words and break the same way. Every consumer reads this value: untilPickup / _exclusiveStepReached (home_scheduled.dart:94), _untilExclusiveStep, _planScheduled (reminders, 'be online', 'Leave now', backup handover), SmartGap clash/leaveAt, ScheduledRideStore.freeCancelUntil/isLateCancel, ScheduledRideStore.upcoming and ReservationWhen.ofRequest.
evidence:
driver_home_admin_content.dart:495 `return build(clockLabel(at), days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow');`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:239-245 `final day = pickupDay.trim().toLowerCase(); final offset = day == 'today' ? 0 : day == 'tomorrow' ? 1 : null; ... return DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset).add(Duration(minutes: minute));`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:343-344 `static _DemoReservationSet get _rides => _set ??= _DemoReservationSet(_anchor(), plan);`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. A driver on a night shift opens the app at 22:10. The anchor is 22:10, so main is 00:10 'Tomorrow', airport is 03:10 'Tomorrow' and assigned is 06:40 'Tomorrow'. The driver accepts the 03:10 airport ride. At 00:01 _planScheduled runs again, and pickupAt returns 03:10 on the day after the real pickup (27 h away). No reminder or 'Leave now' fires at the real 03:10, the free-cancel window is a day too late, and the ride stays in Accepted with a wrong countdown. The opposite also happens: a 'Today 17:00' request whose pickup has passed comes back as a future 17:00 pickup after midnight.
suggested_fix: Keep an absolute pickup DateTime (or an ISO date) on ReservationRequestPreview and make pickupDay a display label only. Failing that, store the reference date the day word is relative to, and resolve the offset from that date instead of from `now`.

title: pickupAt/untilPickup understand only 'Today'/'Tomorrow', but the reservation sheet parses dates, so a dated admin reservation is shown with a countdown yet has no reminders, Leave now, late-cancel rule, clash check or Exclusive step
description: ReservationWhen.pickupOf (reservation_when.dart:103-140) supports pickupDay values such as 'Mon 20 Oct', '20 Oct', '2026-10-20' or a weekday. The reservation sheet and island use it, so the driver sees 'In 45 min' or 'Saturday 14:33'. The model's own ReservationRequestPreview.pickupAt, which all the scheduling logic uses, returns null for anything other than 'today'/'tomorrow'. For such a reservation: ScheduledRideStore.upcoming drops it (it requires pickupAt != null), so _planScheduled never plans reminders, 'be online', 'Leave now' or the backup handover. freeCancelUntil returns null, so isLateCancel is always false and the late-cancel pause can be bypassed. SmartGap.clash treats it as not clashing. _exclusiveStepReached returns false forever, so the request never becomes the Exclusive offer.
evidence:
driver_home_admin_content.dart:239-243 `final offset = day == 'today' ? 0 : day == 'tomorrow' ? 1 : null; if (minute == null || offset == null) { return null; }`
reservation_when.dart:104-111 `final known = request.pickupAt(now); if (known != null) return known; ... final iso = RegExp(r'^(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})$')...`
scheduled_rides.dart:630 `if (ride.route case final route? when route.pickupAt(now) != null)`
scheduled_rides.dart:516-518 `freeCancelUntil(...) => ride?.pickupAt(_now)?.subtract(...)`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Admin sends a reservation two days ahead with pickupDay 'Fri 23 Oct', pickupTime '07:40'. The driver accepts it. On Friday at 07:00 the sheet says 'In 40 min', but no reminder or 'Leave now' arrives and the ride is never handed to a backup. A cancel at 07:30 is not counted as late.
suggested_fix: Have pickupAt delegate to the same parser as ReservationWhen.pickupOf (or move that parser into the model), so display and scheduling read one pickup instant.

title: Destination mode's per-day limit is read from 'destinationsPerDay' but the contract field is 'perDay', so the admin's limit from a contract document is ignored
description: The contract's DriverAppConfig schema (contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:380 and openapi.yaml) defines destinationMode as {perDay: integer >= 0}, and the contract fixture contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json sends `"destinationMode": {"perDay": 2}`. DestinationModeRules.fromJson reads only json['destinationsPerDay'] and falls back to 2. A contract document with perDay 4 (or 1) is therefore silently treated as 2. DestinationModeSession.refusal then blocks or allows destinations on the wrong count. A perDay of 0, which the contract allows, can never be expressed because _positive rejects 0. The admin export fixtures happen to carry both keys, and the contract-fixture test never asserts destinationsPerDay, so no test can catch this.
evidence:
trip_rules_admin_config.dart:94-95 `destinationsPerDay: _positive(json['destinationsPerDay'], 2).round(),`
contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json:155-157 `"destinationMode": { "perDay": 2 }`
contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:380 `("destinationMode", {"type": "object", "properties": {"perDay": i(minimum=0)}}),`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. A backend that follows openapi.yaml publishes destinationMode {perDay: 1}. DriverHomeAdminContentService(appConfig: DriverAppConfig.fromJson(doc)).load() returns destinationsPerDay 2, and Home sets DestinationModeRules.current to it. The driver can set a second destination that the zone does not allow.
suggested_fix: Read `perDay` (falling back to `destinationsPerDay` for older exports), accept 0, and add a contract-fixture assertion that uses a value other than the default.

title: The contract's nextTrips.on switch is ignored: admin cannot turn next-trip offers off
description: The contract defines nextTrips as {on: boolean} (gen_openapi.py:381), and both the contract fixture and the admin export send `"on": true`. NextTripRules has no on/off field, and fromJson never reads json['on']. A document with `nextTrips: {on: false}` gives the defaults (offerTypes exclusive + exclusiveReservation, 5 km / 10 min), so NextTripGate.allows still lets next-trip offers through during a trip in a production build (demo: !driverProductionRequested).
evidence:
trip_rules_admin_config.dart:137-158 `factory NextTripRules.fromJson(Object? json) { ... return NextTripRules(offerTypes: types is List ? [...] : base.offerTypes, withinKmOfDropoffOn: ..., ...` (no 'on')
contracts/tools/gen_openapi.py:381 `("nextTrips", {"type": "object", "properties": {"on": b()}}),`
next_trip_gate.dart:28-30 `final r = rules ?? NextTripRules.current; if (r.offerTypes.isEmpty) { return false; } if (r.wholeLastLeg) { return true; }`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Admin switches next trips off for the zone, so the document says nextTrips {on: false}. The driver app loads it through DriverHomeAdminContentService, and Home sets NextTripRules.current to the defaults. Near the drop-off the driver is still offered a next Exclusive trip.
suggested_fix: Parse `on` (default true). When it is false, return rules with an empty offerTypes list (which NextTripGate already treats as off), or add an explicit enabled flag.

title: A waiting.byCategory block that omits a category drops the seed per-category rules, so XL loses its contract default of 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show
description: When `waiting.byCategory` is present, _waiting builds the category map only from the entries the document lists. The seed rules (xl: 3 free minutes and 3 min no-show; premium per-minute) are kept only when byCategory is missing altogether. contract.json#configDefaults says the apps fall back to the defaults (freeWaitMin default 5, xl 3) 'when a document lacks a field or has a bad value', and the contract's own sample document lists byCategory for economy and comfort only. With that document, termsFor(category: 'Movera XL') gives 5 free minutes and a 5 min no-show instead of 3/3. An XL driver waits 2 extra unpaid minutes before the waiting fee starts and before the no-show button appears. A broken xl entry ('xl': 'three') also falls to 5, and a test asserts that.
evidence:
driver_app_config.dart:257-263 `final byCategory = _map(json['byCategory']); final categories = <String, WaitingRule>{}; if (byCategory == null) { for (final entry in seed.categories.entries) {...} } else { for (final entry in byCategory.entries) {`
contract.json configDefaults: `"freeWaitMin": {"default": 5, "xl": 3}`
contracts/fixtures/config/driver_app_config.json byCategory: only "economy" and "comfort"
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Applying the contract sample config (DriverAppConfig.fromJson(contract fixture).apply()) and starting an XL pickup: WaitingRules.current.termsFor(category: 'Movera XL').freeMinutes is 5, not 3. The waiting clock bills from minute 5 and the no-show button appears at 5 min.
suggested_fix: Start from the seed category rules (rebased to the document currency) and override them with the entries the document provides, instead of replacing the whole map whenever byCategory exists.

title: Pickup pay is always computed in SEK and added only to SEK labels: on a EUR/TND offer it is silently left out of the total, and the pickup line shows 'kr'
description: PickupPayCalculator.pay returns Money.ore(...) from kr-per-km rates, which is always SEK whatever the offer's currency. PickupPayQuote.totalOf parses the fare with Money.parseSekLabel, which returns null for '24,50 €' or '12,500 DT', so the total is returned unchanged and the pay the card claims is included disappears. PickupPayQuote.line formats `pay.formatted` as kr. RideOffer.fare comes from the wire with its own currency (api_dispatch_repository), and fareLabel formats it in that currency, so any non-SEK offer reaches this code. hasPay is true, so with the breakdown display the card says 'incl. 2,50 kr pickup' while the total excludes it.
evidence:
pickup_pay.dart:42-43 `final base = Money.parseSekLabel(fare); return base == null ? fare : (base + pay).formatted;`
pickup_pay.dart:81-82 `final ore = (kronor * 100 + 1e-6).round(); return Money.ore(math.max(0, ore));`
pickup_pay.dart:48-49 `'incl. ${pay.formatted} pickup · ${leg.label}'`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. A FR-PC (EUR) Radar offer with fare 18,00 € and a 6 km / 10 min Movera pickup: pay = (6-1)*2.5 + (10-2)*0.8 = 18.90, stored as SEK 18,90 kr. totalOf('18,00 €') returns '18,00 €' because parseSekLabel fails, so the pickup pay is dropped. With fareWithPickupLine the card reads 'incl. 18,90 kr pickup'.
suggested_fix: Take the offer's Money (or currency) into the calculator, produce pay in that currency, and add it with Money.parseLabel(label, currency: …) or, better, on the Money value itself.

title: With admin's 'net fare' offer-card setting on, the driver's share is always shown in 'kr' with two decimals, whatever the offer currency
description: OfferCardDetails.fare (offer_rules.dart:153-163) shows the driver's share when admin sets offers.offerCard.netFare. It goes through WaybillPayment.fromFare/earnings. fromFare takes the first number with at most 2 decimals, and _format always appends ' kr'. An EUR fare '24,50 €' is shown as '18,38 kr'. A TND fare '12,500 DT' is matched as '12,50' and shown as '9,38 kr', which is the wrong currency and a tenth of the value per millime digit. The radar card, the Exclusive sheet and the reservation sheet all call _show.fare(...). This is separate from the known thousands-grouping defect at waybill.dart:296.
evidence:
waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);`
waybill.dart:331-333 `String _format(int ore) { final text = '${ore ~/ 100}.${...}'; return '${_comma ? text.replaceAll('.', ',') : text} kr';`
offer_rules.dart:157-162 `final payment = WaybillPayment.fromFare(full, ...); return payment?.earnings ?? full;`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. In a FR-PC zone with offerCard.netFare = true, a 24,50 € offer appears on the Radar card as '18,38 kr' (24.50 × 0.75). In TN-TC, '12,500 DT' appears as '9,38 kr'.
suggested_fix: Compute the net share on the offer's Money (minor units with the currency's exponent) and format it with Money.formatted. Do not reparse display labels.

title: RideOffer.reservation throws ArgumentError for any admin reservation whose fare, boost or cash label is not in SEK
description: Reservation previews come from admin content (ScheduledRidesAdminConfig.homeRequests, dispatch reservations). RideOffer.reservation converts their fare, fareBoost and cashToCollect labels with Money.parseSekLabel and throws when parsing fails. home_scheduled.dart:82 (_soonReservationOffer, the Exclusive step), :233 (Leave now) and :368 (the assigned-ride Exclusive card), plus demo_dispatch_repository.dart:198/549, call it with no try/catch. A EUR or TND reservation ('24,50 €', '12,500 DT'), or a SEK label written as '126,75 SEK kr', raises an uncaught ArgumentError inside a Home timer or build path. The code notes 'Reservation previews still carry SEK labels', but nothing stops a non-SEK zone from sending one, and Money.parseLabel already handles every contract currency.
evidence:
dispatch_repository.dart:88-92 `static Money? _amount(String? label, String field) { if (label == null) return null; return Money.parseSekLabel(label) ?? (throw ArgumentError.value(label, field, 'Not a SEK amount')); }`
home_scheduled.dart:80-83 `return _HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(RideOffer.reservation(request), reason: ExclusiveReasons.pickupSoon);`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. In a FR-PC zone, admin sends a reservation preview with fare '32,00 €'. When it reaches its Exclusive step, _soonReservationOffer calls RideOffer.reservation, which throws 'Not a SEK amount'. The Exclusive offer never shows and the error goes to the global error hook. Accepting an assigned EUR ride throws in the same way.
suggested_fix: Parse with Money.parseLabel (which reads €, DT and kr), and skip or log a preview it cannot read instead of throwing in UI paths.

title: Analytics crashes with StateError when admin's Stockholm work stats have no inner areas
description: _demand takes the strongest area with stats.innerAreas.reduce(...). Iterable.reduce throws StateError('No element') on an empty list. StockholmWorkStatsConfig.innerAreas is admin content (DriverHomeAdminContentService is documented as the only thing that changes when the admin backend is connected). An admin who clears the inner-city list, or a zone that has none, makes the Analytics screen throw in build and show the red error box. IslandWaitingSignals handles an empty list correctly, so only Analytics breaks.
evidence:
