analytics.dart:186-189 `final strongest = stats.innerAreas.reduce((current, next) => next.demandPercent > current.demandPercent ? next : current,);`
analytics.dart:139 `_demand(const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load().stockholmWork),`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. When the admin content sends stockholmWork.innerAreas = [], opening Side menu > Analytics throws 'Bad state: No element' during build.
suggested_fix: Skip the 'strongest area' card when innerAreas is empty (or use a fold with a nullable result).

title: Admin demand labels and the 'Around Stockholm' title are shown untranslated in the Swedish/French Analytics screen, and the chip colour only works for the English words
description: The admin seed content holds English labels ('Busy', 'Steady', 'Quiet', 'Around Stockholm'). Analytics renders area.demandLabel and stats.surroundingTitle as-is, next to localized headings (tr.anaSampleStrongestArea etc.), so a Swedish driver (the zone default) sees 'Busy'/'Steady' chips. _chip colours an area by comparing demandLabel.toLowerCase() with 'busy'/'quiet', so a label admin writes in the zone language ('Hög', 'Lugnt') always gets the 'steady' colour. IslandWaitingSignals.fromHome (island_waiting_signals.dart:101) uses the same English comparison for its 'Demand rising' tip. This is not among the known Analytics literals ('DEMO DATA', 'Central Station → Södermalm', 'Comfort · 21:42').
evidence:
analytics.dart:353 `area.demandLabel,`
analytics.dart:292 `stats.surroundingTitle,`
analytics.dart:386-388 `final status = area.demandLabel.toLowerCase(); final isBusy = status == 'busy'; final isQuiet = status == 'quiet';`
driver_home_admin_content.dart:716 `demandLabel: 'Busy',`, :734 `surroundingTitle: 'Around Stockholm',`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. With the app in Swedish (the zone default), Analytics lists 'Södermalm  Busy  86%' and an 'Around Stockholm' card. If admin localizes the labels, every chip turns the neutral colour and the island's 'Demand rising' tip never appears.
suggested_fix: Send a demand level enum and localize it in the app (tr.demandBusy, …), or treat the label as display-only and drive colour and tips from demandPercent.

title: Eight admin-editable Driver app texts are never read by any screen, so admin's edits to them have no effect
description: DriverTexts.all is 'Every key admin can change' (Content › Driver app texts, Q30). offerFare, offerHide, offerReservationRequest, offerYourNextRide, offerViewRoute, offerNewReservation, offerViewDetails and tripCompleteRide are listed and mapped in driver_text_l10n.dart, but nothing in lib calls driverText() with them, and the matching tr getters (tr.offerHide, tr.offerViewRoute, …) are not used either. An admin who edits these texts sees no change in the driver app.
evidence: driver_app_texts.dart:208-209 `static const offerFare = DriverTextKey('offer.fare', 'Fare', ...)`; :228-239 offerHide, offerReservationRequest, offerYourNextRide, offerViewRoute, offerNewReservation, offerViewDetails; :258-259 tripCompleteRide. A grep for `DriverTexts.<name>` outside driver_app_texts.dart returns 0 hits for each of these eight.
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Admin sets offer.viewRoute (sv) to 'Visa rutt nu' and trip.completeRide to 'Avsluta'. No driver screen changes, because no widget reads these keys.
suggested_fix: Either wire these keys into the widgets that show the matching text, or remove them from DriverTexts.all so admin is not offered dead keys.

title: Any category not in the hard-coded list (e.g. an admin-added 'child_seat') passes the vehicle check, and the driver cannot switch it off
description: The contract says category ids come from the admin Pricing catalog and admins can add more (the admin export already has 'child_seat'). For a wire categoryId such as 'child_seat', ApiDispatchRepository sets category to CategoryCatalog.labelOf(...), which gives 'child_seat'. DriverCategoryAccess.allows returns true for every name not in DriverCategoryAccess.all, whatever the car's `allowed` list says. So every vehicle 'drives' every new category, and Preferences (which lists only the 8 built-in names) gives no way to turn it off. DriverCategoryChoice.takes therefore lets these offers onto Home, Radar and the reservation popup for cars admin never approved.
evidence:
ride_categories.dart:45-48 `bool allows(String category) { final name = nameOf(category); return !all.contains(name) || allowed.contains(name); }`
api_dispatch_repository.dart:63 `category: CategoryCatalog.labelOf(text('categoryId')),`
category_catalog.dart:52-55 `labelOf` returns the raw id for a non-seed category
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. Admin adds 'child_seat' and allows it only on cars that have a child seat. A driver whose car (allowed list without it) is online gets 'child_seat' Radar offers and Exclusive offers, and Ride preferences has no tile to turn them off.
suggested_fix: Treat an unknown category as not allowed unless the vehicle's allowed list names it (by id), and build the Preferences tiles from the zone catalog.

title: Outside the demo, the island promises 'Expect a trip in 2–5 min' and 'Demand rising' from static admin area labels, not from the driver's area or any trend
description: IslandWaitingSignals.fromHome is the non-demo path; its comment says a message only exists when its fact does, so the island never makes something up. Yet expectTripSoon is true when any of the 12 Greater Stockholm areas (Arlanda included) is at 80% or more, wherever the driver is. demandRising is true whenever any area's static label equals 'busy', which is a level, not a rise. A driver waiting in Täby (46%, 'Quiet') is told to expect a trip within 2–5 minutes and that demand is rising.
evidence:
island_waiting_signals.dart:86-104 `for (final area in areas) { if (area.demandPercent > top) { top = area.demandPercent; } } ... demandRising: areas.any((a) => a.demandLabel.toLowerCase() == 'busy'), expectTripSoon: top >= expectPercent,`
home_map_sheet.dart:1206 `: IslandWaitingSignals.fromHome(_adminHomeConfig, now: ScheduledClock.instance.now());`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. With a real (non-demo) dispatch repository, the driver waits in Täby. The admin seed has Södermalm at 86% and Arlanda at 82%, so the island rotates 'Expect a trip in 2–5 min' and 'Demand rising' with nothing behind either claim.
suggested_fix: Show these tips only when the driver's own area (by position) meets the threshold, and drop 'Demand rising' unless a trend value is sent.

title: Side menu and Analytics read DriverPerformanceConfig.sample and a fresh content service instead of Home's injected admin config, so they can show different numbers from Home
description: Home reads performance and work stats from widget.homeConfigRepository (DriverHomeConfigRepository, 'Local seed today, remote later'). The side menu reads DriverPerformanceConfig.sample directly. Analytics uses the static _sample and builds its own `const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load()`, and AcceptanceRate/CancelationRate default to sample. The UI-10 comment says these screens show the same value. Once a repository returns admin numbers, or hides a metric with showRating/showAcceptanceRate = false, Home shows the admin value or hides the row, while the side menu and Analytics keep the sample and ignore the show flags.
evidence:
side_menu.dart:289,301 `DriverPerformanceConfig.sample.ratingLabel`
analytics.dart:20 `static const DriverPerformanceConfig _sample = DriverPerformanceConfig.sample;`
analytics.dart:139 `_demand(const DriverHomeAdminContentService().load().stockholmWork),`
home.dart:463-465 `_adminHomeConfig = (widget.homeConfigRepository ?? const LocalDriverHomeConfigRepository()).load();`
failure_scenario: Worked by hand, not run. With a homeConfigRepository whose performance rating is 4.61 and showCancellationRate false, the Home performance sheet shows 4.61 with no cancellation row. The side menu shows 4.88, and Analytics shows 4.88 / 94% / 2.4%.
suggested_fix: Pass the loaded DriverHomeAdminConfig (or the repository) to the side menu and Analytics, and respect the show* flags there.

title: Strip leg identity ignores the stop index: every stop-to-stop leg carries the previous leg's best ETA and shows a false 'Traffic ahead · +N min'
description: AdaptiveTripIsland maps pointKind to TripLeg (adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-267). On a trip with 2 or more stops, the leg from stop k to stop k+1 has the same TripLeg.stop. TripStripController.update decides whether a new leg has started only from `last.leg != next.leg`, so `_bestEta` and `_arrivingSaid` are not reset when the stop changes. At the end of the stop-1 leg, `_routeEtaText` (accept_ride.dart:927-929) has fallen to its floor of `max(1, ...)` = 1 min, so `_bestEta` = 1. It stays 1 during the paid stop wait, because the island keeps feeding the stale route's ETA. When the driver slides 'Go to second stop', `_stopCursor` becomes 1 and the stop-2 route arrives with an ETA such as 9 min. The check `eta - best >= 2` fires and `_say(tr.trafficAheadValueMin(8))` is queued. The '<stop> next' message for stop 2 is also skipped, because it is guarded by newLeg.
evidence:
trip_island_controller.dart:302 `final newLeg = last == null || last.leg != next.leg;`
:321 `if (newLeg && next.leg == TripLeg.stop && next.stopLabel != null) {`
:326-329 `if (best != null && eta - best >= 2) { _say(tr.trafficAheadValueMin(eta - best)); ...`
adaptive_trip_island.dart:262-271 `final leg = switch (widget.pointKind) { ArrivalPointKind.stop => TripLeg.stop, ...}; ... stopLabel: leg == TripLeg.stop ? widget.pointLabel : null, etaMinutes: int.tryParse(RegExp(r'^(\d+)\s*min').firstMatch(widget.eta)?.group(1) ?? '')`
accept_ride.dart:800-801 `if (_stopCursor < widget.stopAddresses.length) { return ArrivalPointKind.stop; }`
failure_scenario: A trip with stops A and B. The driver reaches A (ETA shown as 1 min), waits, then slides 'Go to second stop'. The route to B is 9 min. The island strip shows 'Traffic ahead · +8 min' (in fr 'Trafic devant · +8 min') with no traffic involved, and never shows 'Stop 2 next'. This repeats at every intermediate stop.
suggested_fix: Include the stop label/index in the leg identity, for example `newLeg = last == null || last.leg != next.leg || last.stopLabel != next.stopLabel`, so a new stop resets `_bestEta`/`_arrivingSaid` and plays its own announcement.

title: Island invents 'Traffic ahead · +N min' from any ETA rise, which docs/driver-island-state-map.md says must stay inactive
description: docs/driver-island-state-map.md lists concept 73 'Traffic ahead' and 74 'Delay · 2 min' as 'Inactive until a truthful data/acknowledgment source exists' and says 'Do not invent those confirmations'. The strip controller nevertheless emits tr.trafficAheadValueMin whenever the island's ETA minutes rise by 2 or more over the best seen on the leg. The ETA comes from AcceptRide._routeEtaText = route duration × (1 − routeFraction) (accept_ride.dart:923-929). It uses no traffic data and only rises when a new or longer route replaces the old one, for example after the driver misses a turn and reroutes, or on the stop leg handover described in the other finding.
failure_scenario: Heading to the drop-off with 5 min left, the driver misses a turn and the reroute is 8 min. The island strip says 'Traffic ahead · +3 min', although no traffic source exists and the delay was caused by the detour.
suggested_fix: Remove the traffic message until a real traffic/delay signal exists, or word it as a route change ('Route updated · +3 min') and drive it from the reroute counter instead of ETA deltas.

title: English 'left'/'right' is inserted into the localized 'Pickup on the {side} side' strip message
description: _stripInput passes the raw English words 'left'/'right' as pickupSide. TripStripController then calls tr.pickupOnPickupSideSide(next.pickupSide!), which puts them into the French and Swedish templates unchanged.
evidence:
adaptive_trip_island.dart:277-281
```
pickupSide: b?.symbol == NavigationBannerSymbol.arriveLeft
    ? 'left'
    : b?.symbol == NavigationBannerSymbol.arriveRight
    ? 'right'
    : null,
```
trip_island_controller.dart:351 `_say(tr.pickupOnPickupSideSide(next.pickupSide!));`
app_fr.arb:526 `"pickupOnPickupSideSide": "Prise en charge côté {pickupSide}"`
app_sv.arb:526 `"pickupOnPickupSideSide": "Upphämtning på {pickupSide} sida"`
failure_scenario: With the app in French, the route's arrival step reports the pickup on the right. The island strip reads 'Prise en charge côté right'. In Swedish it reads 'Upphämtning på right sida'.
suggested_fix: Pass a side enum and pick localized strings (for example tr.sideLeft/tr.sideRight, or separate pickupOnLeftSide/pickupOnRightSide messages).

title: On-trip next-trip offer card floats over the web map without PointerInterceptor or the map-gesture block that every other overlay uses
description: When `_incomingOfferOpen` is true, the sliding panel collapses to 0 height (minHeight 0 / maxHeight 1), so the full-screen map (an HtmlElementView on web) lies under the card. Every other overlay on this screen goes through `_mapOverlay` (PointerInterceptor plus `_setMapGesturesBlocked`): the sheet, the island, the map controls and the Ride check layer. Home's equivalent offer sheet is also wrapped in PointerInterceptor, with the comment 'Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them'. The incoming ride card is added bare, so on web the map's DOM element receives pointer events in the card's area, and `_blockMapGestures` is never set while the driver touches it.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:1347-1354
```
if (offerOpen)
  Positioned(
    key: const ValueKey<String>('on-trip-radar-layer'),
    ...
    child: _AcceptRidePanel(this)._buildIncomingRideCard(),
  ),
```
versus accept_ride.dart:1177/1279/1342/1359 `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(...)`; accept_ride_panel.dart:13-22 `_mapOverlay` = `PointerInterceptor(child: Listener(onPointerDown: (_) => _setMapGesturesBlocked(true) ...))`; home_offer_sheet.dart:291-292 `// Opaque to touches: nothing under the sheet (dock, map) gets them. final sheet = PointerInterceptor(`
failure_scenario: In the Safari/PWA build, during a trip an Exclusive next-trip offer appears in the bottom card. When the driver taps Accept or Decline, the touch reaches the Google map, which pans or ignores it, instead of the card button. The offer can run out unanswered.
suggested_fix: Wrap the card in `_AcceptRidePanel(this)._mapOverlay(child: ...)`, as the other overlays are.

title: AppLifecycleState.inactive (app still visible) stops GPS, freezes the car and suspends the camera and offer timers
description: didChangeAppLifecycleState treats `inactive` the same as `paused`/`hidden` and calls _pauseLiveUpdates. That cancels the position subscription, sets `_hasLiveLocation = false`, suspends the camera, stops the wait ticker and pauses the next-trip offer expiry and demo timers. `inactive` is reported while the app is still on screen: on Android when the activity loses window focus (split-screen or multi-window with the other app focused, notification shade pulled down), and on iOS for Control Center or Notification Center. DECISIONS.md records 'Lifecycle pause persists the snapshot and stops GPS', which is a pause, not focus loss.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:720-725
```
case AppLifecycleState.inactive:
case AppLifecycleState.hidden:
case AppLifecycleState.paused:
case AppLifecycleState.detached:
  _rideLifecycle.persistNow();
  _AcceptRideTrip(this)._pauseLiveUpdates();
```
accept_ride_trip.dart:126-129 `_locationEpoch++; _hasLiveLocation = false; _positionSubscription?.cancel(); _positionSubscription = null;`
failure_scenario: An Android driver runs Movera in split-screen next to a music app and touches the music app. Movera becomes inactive: the car marker stops moving while the driver keeps driving, and the camera stops following. On returning focus, 'I've arrived' answers 'Location unavailable' until a new fix comes in, because _startLiveLocation first awaits getCurrentPosition.
suggested_fix: Pause live updates only on hidden/paused/detached. On inactive at most persist the snapshot, as Home should also do.

title: When the first GPS fix fails, the trip routes from the hard-coded Stockholm fallback point and shows a pickup ETA and car marker for a position the app does not know
description: `_driverPosition` starts at `_fallbackDriverPosition` (accept_ride.dart:423, 543), and the LiveVehicleAnimator starts there too (accept_ride.dart:649-651). When `getCurrentPosition` throws (for example location permission denied), the catch in _startLiveLocation sets the 'Location updating…' status and then calls `_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)`. That requests a road route with `origin: GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition)`, the fallback point. NavigationController.ensureRoute has no guard against an origin that is not a live fix. The resulting `_routeDurationSeconds` feeds `_etaLabel`, and the trip card shows 'Pickup · N min' with a route line from the fallback point. The car marker also sits at that fixed point.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:423 `static const LatLng _fallbackDriverPosition = LatLng(59.3262, 18.0595);`
accept_ride.dart:543 `LatLng _driverPosition = _fallbackDriverPosition;`
accept_ride_trip.dart:621-628 `} catch (_) { ... _locationStatus = tr.locationUpdatingEllipsis; }); unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute(force: true));`
accept_ride_trip.dart:704-705 `await _navigation.ensureRoute(origin: GeoPointMaps.fromLatLng(_driverPosition), ...`
accept_ride_sheet.dart:60 `String? get _etaLabel => _routeDurationSeconds == null ? null : _routeEtaText;` and :73 `ActiveRideStage.headingToPickup => _withEta(tr.pickup, eta)`
failure_scenario: A native driver with location permission denied accepts a trip in Enhörna. The trip card reads 'Pickup · 40 min', the map draws a black route from Stockholm central to Enhörna, and the car is shown at 59.3262, 18.0595, although the app has no idea where the driver is.
suggested_fix: Do not request a route (and hide the car marker and ETA) until a real usable fix exists. Show the location fault instead.

title: During a persistent GPS/route fault the island never reveals its default face, so the in-trip side menu is unreachable
description: The side menu on the trip screen opens only from the default (Home-like) island face: `drawerEnableOpenDragGesture: false` and `onMenu` is passed only to TripIsland. TripIslandController.release() refuses to show the default face while `_fault` is set, and `defaultFace` also returns false with a fault. A fault such as 'Location updating…' stays on screen for as long as GPS is unavailable (accept_ride_trip.dart:621-627 keeps `_locationStatus` set until a usable fix arrives). For that whole time, tapping the island does nothing and the driver cannot open the menu (support, history and the rest) for the rest of the trip.
evidence:
trip_island_controller.dart:53 `bool get defaultFace => _defaultFace && !(_fault?.isNotEmpty ?? false);`
:123 `if (_fault?.isNotEmpty ?? false) return;`
accept_ride.dart:1120 `drawerEnableOpenDragGesture: false,`
accept_ride.dart:1305 `onMenu: () => _rideScaffoldKey.currentState?.openDrawer(),` (only via AdaptiveTripIsland -> TripIsland)
failure_scenario: GPS is denied or lost for a whole trip. The island permanently shows 'Location updating…'. Tapping it never reveals menu or search, and there is no other way to open the drawer on the trip screen.
suggested_fix: Allow the default face on touch even with a fault (and return to the fault face afterwards), or put the menu in the long-press tools sheet.

title: Message/waiting island width is clamped only to the screen, not to the documented maximum of 224.48
description: docs/driver-island-state-map.md says the renderer uses 'default width195.2 and maximum224.48 (+15%)', and TripIslandGeometry.maximumWidth exists for this. The status/waiting branch clamps the measured width to `available`, the full screen width minus 24, and maximumWidth is never used outside a test. A longer status grows the island far beyond the documented cap.
failure_scenario: French UI with no GPS: the status face 'Mise à jour de la position…' (about 175 px at 12.5 pt) plus 84 px of slots is about 259 px wide, beyond the 224.48 maximum. On a 390 px phone the island spreads to about 259 px instead of capping and ellipsizing.
suggested_fix: Clamp to `math.min(available, TripIslandGeometry.maximumWidth)`; the title Text already ellipsizes.

title: Maneuver cue semantics label reads the Dart enum name ('slightLeft', 'roundaboutClockwise') to screen readers in every language
description: The cue's Semantics label is `symbol?.name`, the identifier of NavigationBannerSymbol, which is camelCase English. It is also passed into the localized tr.navExitSemantics, so TalkBack/VoiceOver reads 'roundaboutClockwise, sortie 2' in French.
evidence:
adaptive_trip_island.dart:986-990
```
return Semantics(
  label:
      exit == null
          ? symbol?.name ?? tr.navToDestination
          : tr.navExitSemantics(symbol?.name ?? tr.navToDestination, exit),
```
failure_scenario: A blind or low-vision driver using VoiceOver in Swedish focuses the island's turn cue and hears 'sharpRight' or 'roundaboutClockwise, avfart 2'.
suggested_fix: Map each symbol to a localized cue label (RouteCue labels already exist) instead of `symbol.name`.

title: Island big distance rounds 999.5–999.9 m to '1000 m' and 9.95–9.99 km to '10,0 km'
description: _bannerDistance is the island's own formatter, separate from RouteInstructionCopy.formatDistance. It checks `meters < 1000` before rounding, so 999.6 m renders as '1000 m'. It checks `km < 10` before toStringAsFixed(1), so 9.96 km renders as '10,0 km' instead of '10 km'.
failure_scenario: The banner reports 999.7 m to the next turn. The island's large number shows '1000 m'. At 9 960 m it shows '10,0 km'.
suggested_fix: Round first, then choose the unit and precision based on the rounded value.

title: Destination mode set from the island search during a trip is not persisted, so a crash or reload soon after loses it
description: The island's search callback (accept_ride.dart:1306 `onSearch: _openDestinationPicker`) sets `_destinationActive`, `_destinationAddress` and `_destinationPosition` through `_rebuild` (setState only) and records the daily use with `OnTripDestination.started()`. It never calls `_rideLifecycle.persistNow()`. `_buildSnapshot` does write destinationModeActive/destinationAddress/destinationPoint, but the next save only happens on a stage change, a lifecycle pause, or a GPS fix more than 2 minutes after the last snapshot (accept_ride_trip.dart:672-677). DECISIONS.md documents restoring from the snapshot after Safari kills the tab mid-trip.
failure_scenario: During a trip the driver sets a destination from the island (one of the day's limited uses is consumed). The Safari tab crashes 60 s later. The trip is restored from a snapshot without destination mode, so next-trip offers no longer follow the destination, and the daily use is still counted.
suggested_fix: Call `_rideLifecycle.persistNow()` after setting the destination.

title: Crash/reload restore drops the rider's bag count, so the island's bag notice is lost
description: AcceptRide.bags drives the island strip's 'Rider has N bags' notice on the pickup leg (accept_ride.dart:1314 → adaptive_trip_island.dart:275 → trip_island_controller.dart:318-320). Neither _buildSnapshot nor AcceptRide.fromPersisted carries bags, so a restored trip always has bags = 0.
evidence: accept_ride.dart:253-291 `return AcceptRide(... restoredSnapshot: snapshot, destinationModeActive: ..., )` with no `bags:`; accept_ride_trip.dart:13-61 PersistedActiveRide built without bags; trip_island_controller.dart:318 `if (newLeg && next.leg == TripLeg.pickup && next.bags > 0) { _say(tr.riderBags(next.bags)); }`
failure_scenario: A rider booked with 2 bags. The PWA reloads while the driver is heading to the pickup. After the restore the island never says 'Rider has 2 bags'.
suggested_fix: Persist bags in PersistedActiveRide and pass it through fromPersisted.

title: Island spring is under-damped although docs/driver-trip-island.md specifies a critically damped spring
description: The doc states 'IslandMorph owns one critically damped spring controller for width, height and corner geometry'. The spring uses mass 1, stiffness 210, damping 25. Critical damping is 2·sqrt(210) ≈ 28.98, so the damping ratio is about 0.86 (under-damped) and the motion overshoots past 1. The value is then clamped by `_phase`, so the geometry sits pinned at the target while the spring is still overshooting, and the settle takes longer than the visible motion.
evidence:
island_morph.dart:146 `const SpringDescription(mass: 1, stiffness: 210, damping: 25),`
island_morph.dart:64 `double get _phase => _motion.value.clamp(0.0, 1.0);`
failure_scenario: A resize with incoming velocity (up to 3.0 carried in) overshoots past 1. The clamp holds the island at the target size until the spring comes back, and the outgoing layers only clear when the spring settles. This differs from the documented critically damped motion.
suggested_fix: Use damping = 2*sqrt(stiffness*mass) (≈ 29), or update the doc.

title: Radar offer sound keeps looping after the app goes to the background: _pauseHomeUpdates never silences it
description: The radar sound is a loop (AudioRadarSound.startLoop uses ReleaseMode.loop). It only stops through _offerSound.tap(), a Match tap, or _syncOfferSound. _syncOfferSound runs only from build() and does its check in a post-frame callback (home_offer_sound.dart:7-18). When the app is backgrounded, didChangeAppLifecycleState calls _pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:188-203). That method cancels the offer timers, GPS and animation controllers, but it does not call _offerSound.silence() and does not call setState. Once the lifecycle is paused or hidden, Flutter turns frames off, so no build and no post-frame callback runs. The silence check (`!_liveVisible -> _offerSound.silence()`) therefore never executes. Because the offer timers are cancelled too, nothing else changes state that could stop the loop.
evidence:
home.dart:188-191 `void didChangeAppLifecycleState(AppLifecycleState state) { _foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed; if (_liveVisible) { _resumeHomeUpdates(); } else { _pauseHomeUpdates(); } }`
home.dart:192-203 `_pauseHomeUpdates()` cancels the camera, GPS, radar subscription, offer timers and controllers, with no _offerSound call and no setState.
home_offer_sound.dart:10-17 `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) { ... if (!_liveVisible || ...) { _offerSound.silence(); return; }`
radar_offer_sound.dart:150 `await audio.setReleaseMode(ReleaseMode.loop);`
failure_scenario: The driver is online and a Radar card arrives, so the radar sound starts looping. Without touching the screen, the driver presses Home or switches to another app (Android or a mobile browser tab). The radar sound keeps looping in the background until the driver comes back to the app, although the offers were paused and their pick windows run out meanwhile.
suggested_fix: Call _offerSound.silence() in _pauseHomeUpdates. _syncOfferSound already restarts the sound on resume when offers are still available.

title: System Back on the 'Unresolved trip' dialog closes the saved trip and marks it terminal
description: For a stale snapshot (older than 6 h) or one without verified endpoints, Home shows an AlertDialog with 'Close trip' and 'Resume trip'. barrierDismissible: false only blocks taps outside the dialog. The Android or browser Back button still pops the DialogRoute with a null result, because there is no PopScope in the builder. The code treats any result other than true as 'Close trip' (`if (resume != true)`). It then writes a terminal marker (driver cancel, or released to dispatch) and clears the saved ride. So Back, which the driver expects to dismiss the dialog, silently cancels a trip that could have been resumed.
failure_scenario: The driver's phone restarts during a long trip, and the saved ride is more than 6 h old or the app is reopened late. Home shows 'Unresolved trip' with Resume enabled. The driver presses Android Back (or browser Back on the PWA) to get rid of the dialog. The trip is marked cancelled by the driver or released to dispatch, and its recovery record is deleted, with no confirmation.
suggested_fix: Wrap the AlertDialog in PopScope(canPop: false), or treat a null result as 'ask again' rather than 'close'.

title: A trip matched from the full Radar list leaves Home's Radar deck in place, so after the trip Home shows the pre-trip cards (the trip just driven as 'Taken')
description: When the driver matches from the Home deck, _openOfferTrip clears all Home offer state in a post-frame callback (_outsideRadarOffer, _radarHomeOffers, _pendingRadarHomeOffers, _hasRideOffers = false). When the driver matches from the embedded RideRequests list (shown when showRideRequests is true), Home only receives onCloseRides and the session callbacks, and nothing clears Home's deck. The sequence is as follows. (1) RideRequests claims the offer. The demo dispatch _removeOffer emits the new offer list to Home's still-live _watchDispatchRadar listener, which calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, unavailable) on Home's copy of the same trip and marks it claimedElsewhere. (2) Within 500 ms AcceptRide is pushed, and didPushNext -> _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) cancels the 2.8 s cleanup but keeps every list and deadline. (3) After the trip, endTrip sets resumeHomeAfterTrip, and _onDriverSessionChanged only sets showRideRequests = false. didPopNext -> _resumeOfferTimers shows the driven trip as a 'Taken' card for 1.2 s. Other cards have old deadlines and come back already expired (Match faded), and _hasRideOffers stays true.
evidence:
home.dart:746-766 `RideRequests(... onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; _hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty; }); }, )`. No match callback exists.
home.dart:664-668 `if (_driverSession.consumeResumeHomeAfterTrip()) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; }); return; }`
Compare home_offer_radar.dart:983-990 (Home-deck accept): `_rebuild(() { _outsideRadarOffer = null; _radarHomeOffers.clear(); _pendingRadarHomeOffers.clear(); _hasRideOffers = false; ...`
home_offer_radar.dart:604-610 `if (!ids.contains(offer.id) && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == available) { _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, _RadarOfferGone.unavailable); }`
failure_scenario: The driver is online with three Radar cards on Home, taps the orb to open the full Radar list, and taps Match on the first trip. They drive it and complete it 20 minutes later. Back on Home, the deck still holds the pre-trip cards: the trip just completed is shown as 'Taken', and the rest have Match faded. If that card was the expanded front card, the island also posted 'Trip unavailable' at the moment of the match.
suggested_fix: Give RideRequests an onMatched callback, or clear Home's deck in _onDriverSessionChanged when a trip begins, in the same way as the Home-deck accept path.

title: _hasRideOffers set from the Radar list on close is never cleared when those offers leave dispatch: the orb says 'Trip found', 'Finding trips' never shows and Exclusive offers are held back
description: Closing the full Radar list sets `_hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty`, where hasOffers comes from the list's own dispatch offers. _hasRideOffers is reset only by _dismissRadarHomeOffer, _refreshRadarHomeOffers (which needs pending Home offers), _openOfferTrip, go online and go offline. The dispatch watcher (_watchDispatchRadar) updates _latestDispatchOffers but never recomputes _hasRideOffers. Suppose the Home deck was emptied while the list was open, for example when a card was withdrawn or taken and removed after 2.8 s, and the list still had other trips. The flag then stays true after those trips expire. While it is true: _buildTripRadarButton shows 'Trip found / NEW / Tap for all' with zero trips (totalTrips = max(0, 0)); _waitingForTrips is false, so the island never says 'Finding trips'; and _showOutsideRadarOffer returns early for every non-reservation Exclusive offer (`!offer.reservation && (_pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _hasRideOffers)`).
evidence:
home.dart:759-764 `onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; _hasRideOffers = hasOffers || _radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty; }); }`
home.dart:1055-1056 `final hasRadarOffer = _hasRideOffers || homeTrips > 0; final totalTrips = hasRadarOffer ? math.max(radarTrips, homeTrips) : 0;`
home_offer_radar.dart:238-239 `(!offer.reservation && (_pendingRadarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty || _hasRideOffers)) ||` -> return
home_map_sheet.dart:1197 `!_hasRideOffers && _radarHomeOffers.isEmpty &&` (gates 'Finding trips')
failure_scenario: The driver opens the Radar list. Meanwhile the only Home card is taken by another driver and removed, and the list still shows two other trips. The driver closes the list, and those two trips then expire in dispatch. Home keeps showing 'Trip found · NEW · Tap for all' with nothing to take, never shows 'Finding trips', and no Exclusive offer can rise until the driver taps the orb again.
suggested_fix: Recompute _hasRideOffers from live state (Home deck, pending, or _radarTripsOpen > 0) in the dispatch listener, or derive it instead of storing it.

title: After crash recovery, the trip's waybill and completion record carry the last snapshot save time and 'Demo driver — identity unavailable'
description: _waybillFromSnapshot builds the current waybill with issuedAt = snapshot.savedAt, which is the time of the last persist (a stage change or background pause), not when the trip was accepted, although the snapshot has acceptedAt. It also sets driverName to tr.demoDriverIdentityUnavailable, whereas a trip that was not restored uses tr.moveraDriver (accept_ride_trip.dart:181,187). AcceptRide keeps Home's record because the tripId matches (accept_ride.dart:621). _loadVehicleIdentity patches only the vehicle and plate. _paidWaybill copies _waybills.current, so the completed waybill and the journal record keep the wrong time and driver.
evidence:
home.dart:627 `issuedAt: snapshot.savedAt ?? DateTime.now(),`
home.dart:635 `driverName: tr.demoDriverIdentityUnavailable,`
accept_ride.dart:621 `if(_waybills.current?.tripId != widget.tripId) { _waybills.beginCurrent(...); }`
accept_ride_trip.dart:77 `return (_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill()).copyWith(`
active_ride_repository.dart:143 `final DateTime? acceptedAt;`
failure_scenario: A trip is accepted at 14:02. The app is backgrounded at 14:20 (snapshot saved) and killed. On reopen the trip is restored. The waybill sheet now shows Time 14:20 and Driver 'Demo driver — identity unavailable', and the completed record keeps those values. The same trip without a crash would show 14:02 and 'Movera Driver'.
suggested_fix: Use snapshot.acceptedAt ?? snapshot.savedAt for issuedAt and tr.moveraDriver for driverName, as the live path does.

title: Radar sweep wedge never fades: SweepGradient with a negative startAngle clamps the whole arc to the end colour
description: RadarWedgePainter draws the arc from -tail to 0 rad with SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0). Both Skia and Impeller compute a pixel's sweep parameter from its angle in [0, 2π), then remap it with (t - start) / (end - start). Pixels in the drawn arc (-60°..0°) have t in [5/6, 1), which remaps to [6, 7) and is clamped by the default TileMode.clamp to stop 1.0 (white at 0.6 alpha). The documented 'light wedge that fades behind its leading edge' therefore renders as a solid 60° white fan with a hard trailing edge. Worked by hand: a pixel at -30° has t_raw = 11/12, so (11/12 + 1/6) * 6 = 6.5, which clamps to 1.
evidence: movera_radar_orb.dart:487-499 `canvas.translate(center.dx, center.dy); canvas.rotate(lead); ... ..shader = SweepGradient(startAngle: -tail, endAngle: 0, colors: [Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0), Colors.white.withValues(alpha: 0.6)]).createShader(rect); canvas.drawArc(rect, -tail, tail, true, paint);`
failure_scenario: The driver goes online. Home's radar orb shows a uniform bright 60° slice rotating around the ring instead of a soft sweep that fades out behind its leading edge.
suggested_fix: Use startAngle: 2*math.pi - tail and endAngle: 2*math.pi (the same position as -tail..0 in the gradient's [0, 2π) domain), or draw from 0 to tail and rotate by lead - tail.

title: Radar orb always announces itself as a button, even when it has no action (scanning, starting)
description: MoveraRadarOrb wraps its content in Semantics(button: true, ...) whatever the value of onTap. Home passes onTap: null while scanning with no offers (_buildTripRadarButton: `onTap: hasRadarOffer ? _openRideOffers : null`) and while going online (_buildGoingOnlineButton has no onTap). A screen reader then reads 'Radar, LIVE. Scanning, button', and a double-tap does nothing.
evidence:
movera_radar_orb.dart:151-157 `return Semantics(button: true, label: "$title, $status. $subtitle", child: GestureDetector(key: touchKey, behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque, onTap: onTap,`
home.dart:1078 `onTap: hasRadarOffer ? _openRideOffers : null,`
failure_scenario: A TalkBack or VoiceOver user is online with no trips found. Focus on the orb announces a button. Activating it does nothing, and nothing says the control is disabled.
suggested_fix: Use `button: onTap != null`, or add `enabled: onTap != null`.

title: Pickup-pay line on Radar offer cards is hard-coded English ('incl. … pickup') in fr/sv
description: RadarOfferCard renders PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay) under the fare (radar_offer_card.dart:386). When admin chooses PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine, the line text comes from PickupPayQuote.line, which concatenates the English words 'incl.' and 'pickup' around the localized amount and leg label.
evidence:
pickup_pay.dart:48-49 `String? get line => hasPay && display == PickupPayDisplay.fareWithPickupLine ? 'incl. ${pay.formatted} pickup · ${leg.label}' : null;`
radar_offer_card.dart:386 `PickupPayLine(quote: offer.pickupPay),`
failure_scenario: Admin sets pickup pay to 'fare with pickup line'. A French or Swedish driver sees Radar cards reading 'incl. 21,60 kr pickup · 4.2 km · 9 min'.
suggested_fix: Move the template to the ARB files (e.g. tr.pickupPayIncluded(amount, leg)).

title: Go online / Locate / resume mute Home's running GPS stream until a fresh one-shot fix returns
description: _startDriverLocation bumps _locationEpoch before it awaits getCurrentPosition(). The existing _driverLocationSubscription stays subscribed, but its listener drops every update because `epoch != _locationEpoch`. It is replaced only after the one-shot fix returns or throws. _goOnline (home.dart:924) and the locate button call this while a working stream is already running, so the car marker and camera freeze for the whole one-shot wait: up to the 8 s time limit natively, and without a limit on web (the time limit is not enforced there).
evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart:35-38 `final epoch = ++_locationEpoch; if (!_liveVisible) { return; } try { final position = await _driverLocationService.getCurrentPosition();`
home_map_sheet.dart:65 `if (!mounted || !_liveVisible || epoch != _locationEpoch) { return; }`
home.dart:924 `unawaited(_HomeMapSheet(this)._startDriverLocation(moveCamera: true));`
failure_scenario: The driver is moving with live GPS on Home and taps the radar to go online while the GPS signal is weak. The car marker stops updating until getCurrentPosition returns or times out (several seconds, longer on web), although the stream was already delivering fixes.
suggested_fix: Keep the old stream active until the new subscription is in place: bump the epoch only when replacing the subscription, or skip the one-shot when a subscription is already live.

title: An Exclusive offer hidden behind the open side menu keeps counting down and is counted as missed (toward auto-offline)
description: The drawer is not a route, so opening it does not trigger didPushNext or pause. The Exclusive sheet sits under the drawer's 90%-wide panel and its scrim, where the driver cannot see it or tap Accept, and its _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer keeps running. When it fires, the offer is dismissed with missed: true, which feeds ExclusiveAnswers (Q16), and enough misses in a row take the driver offline. The same offer hidden by a pushed route is paused and, per R13-3, 'ran out while the driver could not see it: not a miss'.
evidence:
home.dart:712-716 `drawer: DriverSideMenu(isOnline: _isOnline, ...)` (no drawer-open handling)
home_offer_radar.dart:275-281 `_outsideOfferTimeoutTimer = Timer(lifetime, () { ... // Ran out without Accept: it counts as missed (Q16). _dismissOutsideRadarOffer(missed: true); });`
home_exclusive.dart:110-112 `// It ran out while the driver could not see it: not a miss.`
failure_scenario: An Exclusive offer rises and the driver opens the side menu from the island to check Notifications, reading the menu for 15 s. The offer runs out under the drawer and counts as a missed Exclusive. At the admin's limit, the driver is taken offline.
suggested_fix: Pause the Exclusive timeout while the drawer is open (Scaffold.onDrawerChanged), or do not count a timeout as a miss while the drawer covers the offer.
